title: The Crows That Never Forgot
paragraphs: If a crow sees you do something it does not like, it may remember your face for years. That is what [[researchers|L4-0838]] at a university in the United States found when they studied the [[behavior|L4-0091]] of wild crows on their campus. Crows [[occupy|L4-0686]] parks and streets in many cities, so the team had plenty of birds to watch.

In the [[research|L4-0837]], a few team members wore the same frightening mask whenever they caught crows. They were careful not to [[injure|L4-0532]] the birds; they only put a small band on each one's leg and let it go. Before long, the crows began to [[associate|L4-0066]] the mask with danger. Whenever someone wore it near the [[site|L4-0894]] where the birds had been caught, crows would gather around and make loud, angry calls at that person.

The most surprising [[evidence|L4-0366]] [[emerged|L4-0342]] years later. [[Despite|L4-0274]] the fact that the team had stopped catching birds, the number of crows that reacted to the mask kept growing. [[Moreover|L4-0652]], many of them were young birds that had never been caught. It seems that the crows had learned from one another which face to watch out for.

This study has had a big [[impact|L4-0517]] on how people see these birds. Crows are not just noisy neighbors; they are clever animals with long memories. So the next time a crow looks at you, be kind. It may be remembering your face.
zh: 如果烏鴉看見你做了牠不喜歡的事，牠可能會把你的臉記上好幾年。這是美國一所大學的研究人員研究校園裡野生烏鴉的行為時所發現的。烏鴉占據了許多城市的公園和街道，所以研究團隊有很多鳥可以觀察。
在這項研究中，幾位團隊成員每次捕捉烏鴉時，都戴著同一個嚇人的面具。他們很小心，不讓鳥受傷，只在每隻烏鴉的腳上套一個小腳環，然後就放牠走。沒過多久，烏鴉就開始把那個面具和危險聯想在一起。只要有人戴著面具出現在當初捉鳥的地點附近，烏鴉就會聚集過來，對那個人發出又大又憤怒的叫聲。
最令人驚訝的證據在幾年後才出現。儘管團隊早已不再捉鳥，對面具有反應的烏鴉數量卻持續增加。此外，其中有許多是從來沒被捉過的年輕烏鴉。看來烏鴉會互相學習，知道該提防哪一張臉。
這項研究大大影響了人們對這種鳥的看法。烏鴉不只是吵鬧的鄰居，牠們是記性很好的聰明動物。所以下次有烏鴉看著你的時候，對牠友善一點吧。牠可能正在記住你的臉。

questions.stem: What did the team members do when they caught the crows?
options: They taught the birds to fly along a new path.
They wore a mask and put a band on each bird's leg.
They kept the birds in a cage for several years.
They gave the birds food so the birds would like them.
questions.explain: 第二段說團隊成員捉烏鴉時都戴著同一個嚇人的面具，並在每隻鳥腳上套一個小腳環後放走，故選 (B)。(C) 文中說他們只套上腳環就放鳥走（let it go），並沒有把鳥關起來。
questions.evidence: they only put a small band on each one's leg and let it go

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, which of the following is true?
options: Only the crows that had been caught reacted to the mask.
The crows forgot the mask after a few months.
Some young crows that had never been caught also reacted to the mask.
The team caught more crows every year.
questions.explain: 第三段說對面具有反應的烏鴉越來越多，而且其中許多是從沒被捉過的年輕烏鴉，故選 (C)。(A) 與文意相反；(D) 文中說團隊早已停止捉鳥。
questions.evidence: many of them were young birds that had never been caught

questions.stem: The word "associate" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 烏鴉開始把面具和「危險」連在一起，所以只要看到戴面具的人就會大叫，associate A with B 是「把 A 和 B 聯想在一起」，故選 (A)。(C) make friends with 與烏鴉生氣大叫的反應正好相反。
questions.evidence: the crows began to associate the mask with danger

questions.stem: What can we infer from the passage?
options: Crows only remember people who feed them.
Crows are afraid of all people who wear masks.
Crows can share information about danger with other crows.
Crows become less clever as they get older.
questions.explain: 沒被捉過的年輕烏鴉也會對面具大叫，作者推測烏鴉會互相學習該提防哪張臉，可見烏鴉能把危險的訊息傳給同伴，故選 (C)。(B) 烏鴉針對的是「那一個」面具，文中沒說牠們怕所有戴面具的人。
questions.evidence: It seems that the crows had learned from one another which face to watch out for.

vocab.stem: The ______ of the light bulb changed the way people lived at night.
vocab.explain: 電燈泡的「發明」改變了人們夜晚的生活方式，故選 invention。behavior（行為）、competition（競爭；比賽）、evidence（證據）放進句中都說不通。

vocab.stem: The bus took a different ______ today because the main road was closed.
vocab.explain: 主要道路封閉，所以公車今天走了不同的「路線」，故選 route。site（地點）不能和 take a different 搭配表示改道；percent（百分比）、device（裝置）也不合語意。

title: Three Small Wins a Day
paragraphs: When Yu-ting [[transferred|L4-0959]] to a new senior high school in the middle of her first year, she thought the hardest part would be making friends. She was wrong. Her new school was much more [[demanding|L4-0264]], and she soon had trouble [[coping|L4-0220]] with all the extra work.

Every night she studied until after midnight. Her stress became so [[severe|L4-0881]] that it began to cause [[physical|L4-0735]] problems, [[including|L4-0522]] headaches and trouble sleeping. Even small sounds would [[disturb|L4-0308]] her when she tried to rest.

Finally, she went to see the school counselor, a [[professional|L4-0772]] who had helped many students with the same [[issue|L4-0568]]. The counselor explained that Yu-ting's stress came [[largely|L4-0579]] from trying to do everything perfectly. She suggested that Yu-ting [[adopt|L4-0025]] a simple habit: at the end of each day, write down three small [[accomplishments|L4-0011]], such as finishing a page of math problems or asking a question in class.

[[Despite|L4-0274]] her doubts, Yu-ting tried it. Slowly, she [[acquired|L4-0017]] a new way of looking at her day. She also noticed that daily [[interactions|L4-0553]] with classmates, like chatting at lunch, made her feel calmer. Now she is [[content|L4-0201]] with doing her best instead of being perfect, and her story has [[inspired|L4-0538]] a few friends to start their own lists of small wins.
zh: 鈺婷在高一讀到一半時轉學到一所新的高中時，以為最困難的會是交朋友。她錯了。新學校的要求高出許多，她很快就應付不了那些額外的課業。
她每天晚上都讀書讀到半夜以後。她的壓力大到開始引起身體上的問題，包括頭痛和睡不好。就連一點小聲音，都會在她想休息時打擾到她。
最後，她去找學校的輔導老師。這位專業人員曾幫助過許多有同樣問題的學生。輔導老師解釋說，鈺婷的壓力主要來自想把每件事都做到完美。她建議鈺婷養成一個簡單的習慣：每天結束時，寫下三件小小的成就，例如寫完一頁數學題，或是在課堂上提出一個問題。
儘管半信半疑，鈺婷還是試了。慢慢地，她學會了用新的角度看待自己的一天。她也注意到，每天和同學的互動，像是午餐時聊聊天，讓她心情比較平靜。現在她滿足於盡力而為，而不是追求完美；她的故事也啟發了幾個朋友，開始寫下自己的「小勝利」清單。

questions.stem: Why did Yu-ting have trouble at her new school?
options: She could not find the way to her classroom.
The work at school was much harder than she expected.
Her classmates did not want to talk to her.
She had to take a long bus ride every day.
questions.explain: 第一段說新學校的要求高出許多（much more demanding），她很快就應付不了額外的課業，故選 (B)。(C) 她原本以為交朋友最難，但文中說「她錯了」，同學並沒有不理她。
questions.evidence: Her new school was much more demanding, and she soon had trouble coping with all the extra work.

questions.stem: According to the counselor, where did Yu-ting's stress mainly come from?
options: Spending too much time with friends
questions.explain: 第三段輔導老師說鈺婷的壓力主要來自想把每件事都做到完美，故選 (D)。(B) 正好相反，她是讀書讀到半夜、睡不好。
questions.evidence: The counselor explained that Yu-ting's stress came largely from trying to do everything perfectly.

questions.stem: The word "content" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 她現在對「盡力就好、不求完美」感到滿意，be content with 是「對……感到滿足」，故選 (C) satisfied。(A) worried 與全文她心情變平靜的發展相反。
questions.evidence: Now she is content with doing her best instead of being perfect

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A small daily habit helped a student deal with stress.
Students should study until midnight to get good grades.
Counselors should give students more homework.
Transferring to a new school is always a bad idea.
questions.explain: 全文描述鈺婷轉學後壓力過大，在輔導老師建議下每天寫三件小成就，逐漸找回平靜，主旨是一個小習慣幫助她面對壓力，故選 (A)。(B) 熬夜讀書正是造成她身體不適的原因，不是文章的建議。
questions.evidence: write down three small accomplishments

vocab.stem: Lisa likes to ______ small animals out of wood in her free time.
vocab.explain: 用木頭「雕刻」出小動物，carve A out of B 是常見用法，故選 carve。install（安裝）、disturb（打擾）、transfer（轉移）都不能和 out of wood 搭配。

vocab.stem: Plastic in the ocean can ______ sea turtles, which often mistake it for food.
vocab.explain: 海龜常把塑膠誤當成食物，所以海洋中的塑膠會「危及」海龜，故選 endanger。preserve（保護）、inspire（激勵）意思正面，與上下文矛盾；acquire（獲得）也不合語意。

title: Lantern Night at River Park
paragraphs: Join us for the third [[annual|L4-0043]] River Park [[Community|L4-0163]] Lantern Night on February 21! Since it began, this [[celebration|L4-0129]] has [[expanded|L4-0372]] from one small street to the whole park, and this year we hope to welcome even more families. There will be food, music, and fun for people of all ages.

Schedule: 3:00-5:00 p.m., lantern-making class. Choose from three [[options|L4-0692]]: a rabbit, a fish, or a flower. Paper, glue, and all other [[equipment|L4-0357]] will be provided. 5:30 p.m., lantern show. [[Numerous|L4-0674]] [[creations|L4-0233]] by local artists will be on display, [[including|L4-0522]] an [[enormous|L4-0352]] dragon [[constructed|L4-0193]] from more than 500 used plastic bottles. 7:00 p.m., lantern walk along the river.

How to join: Sign up at the front [[counter|L4-0227]] of the community center by February 14. The class is free, but space is limited. [[Furthermore|L4-0433]], children under ten must come with an adult. Please [[attach|L4-0074]] a card with your name to your lantern so that it can be returned to you after the walk.

Safety notes: Please stay [[alert|L4-0031]] near the water, especially after dark, and keep young children close to you. If it rains, the lantern walk will be moved indoors to our sports [[facility|L4-0383]] next to the community center. If you have any questions, please call the community center. We look forward to seeing you there!
zh: 歡迎參加2月21日舉辦的第三屆河濱公園社區燈籠夜！這個慶祝活動自開辦以來，已經從一條小街擴大到整座公園，今年我們希望迎接更多家庭。現場將有美食、音樂，以及適合各年齡層的歡樂活動。
活動時間表：下午3:00至5:00，燈籠製作課。有三種選擇：兔子、魚或花。紙、膠水和所有其他用具都由我們提供。下午5:30，燈籠展。眾多在地藝術家的作品將公開展示，其中包括一條用超過500個回收塑膠瓶建造而成的巨大龍燈。晚上7:00，沿河提燈遊行。
參加方式：請在2月14日前到社區中心前方櫃檯報名。課程免費，但名額有限。此外，十歲以下兒童必須由一位成人陪同。請在你的燈籠上附一張寫有姓名的卡片，以便遊行結束後歸還給你。
安全須知：在水邊請保持警覺，天黑後尤其要注意，並讓年幼的孩子待在身邊。如果下雨，提燈遊行將移到社區中心旁的運動設施室內舉行。如果有任何問題，請致電社區中心。期待在那裡見到你！

questions.stem: What will people see at the 5:30 p.m. show?
options: A boat race on the river
A dance by children from the community
A large dragon made from used bottles
Fish swimming in a big tank
questions.explain: 活動表中下午5:30的燈籠展，會展出一條用超過500個回收塑膠瓶做成的巨大龍燈，故選 (C)。(D) fish 只是燈籠製作課的造型選項之一，不是展覽內容。
questions.evidence: including an enormous dragon constructed from more than 500 used plastic bottles

questions.stem: What must a family with a seven-year-old child do?
options: Make sure an adult comes with the child
Bring their own paper and glue
questions.explain: 第三段說十歲以下兒童必須由成人陪同，七歲的孩子符合這條規定，故選 (A)。(B) 課程是免費的；(D) 紙和膠水都由主辦單位提供。
questions.evidence: children under ten must come with an adult

questions.stem: The word "facility" in paragraph 4 refers to ______.
options: a bus that takes people home
a small street near the park
questions.explain: 第四段說下雨時遊行會移到室內的 sports facility，指的是供運動使用的場館建築，故選 (D)。(C) 一條小街是第一段提到活動最初的規模，與 facility 無關。
questions.evidence: the lantern walk will be moved indoors to our sports facility next to the community center

questions.stem: What can we infer about Lantern Night?
options: It is held for the first time this year.
It has become more popular since it began.
Only artists are allowed to make lanterns.
It only takes place when the weather is good.
questions.explain: 第一段說活動自開辦以來從一條小街擴大到整座公園，今年還希望迎接更多家庭，可推知它越來越受歡迎，故選 (B)。(A) 錯，今年已是第三屆；(D) 錯，下雨時改在室內舉行，並不會取消。
questions.evidence: this celebration has expanded from one small street to the whole park

vocab.stem: Weather experts ______ that a strong typhoon will reach Taiwan this weekend.
vocab.explain: 氣象專家「預測」強颱本週末會到台灣，predict that... 表示預測某事會發生，故選 predict。abandon（拋棄）、construct（建造）、disguise（偽裝）後面都不能接 that 子句表達這個意思。

vocab.stem: There is a small ______ in my phone screen because I dropped it last week.
vocab.explain: 上週把手機摔到地上，所以螢幕上有一道小「裂痕」，故選 crack。concept（概念）、blessing（祝福）、breed（品種）都不會出現在螢幕上。

title: Notes from a Friend
paragraphs: The first note appeared in Pei-chen's desk two weeks before her final exams, a [[critical|L4-0237]] time for any student. "Breathe. You have more [[potential|L4-0753]] than you think," it said. It was signed "A friend." Pei-chen had been fighting [[anxiety|L4-0044]] for months, and the short message [[relieved|L4-0827]] some of her worry.

After that, a new note arrived every Monday. Each one made [[reference|L4-0812]] to things that only a close friend could know, such as the name of her cat and her fear of speaking in front of the class. Pei-chen wanted to [[identify|L4-0502]] the writer, so she looked for [[evidence|L4-0366]]. She compared the notes with her classmates' homework, but none of the writing [[resembled|L4-0839]] them. This [[annoyed|L4-0042]] her more than she expected.

[[Nevertheless|L4-0668]], the notes kept her going, and she did well on her exams. On the last day of the semester, she [[encountered|L4-0346]] her class teacher, Ms. Wang, at the classroom door. Ms. Wang was holding one more note. "I think it's time you knew," she said with a smile. "I've been [[involved|L4-0565]] from the start."

A year earlier, she explained, everyone in the class had written ten short notes to their future selves. Ms. Wang had [[retained|L4-0850]] them all, and when she noticed Pei-chen's stress, she began to deliver Pei-chen's notes one by one. Pei-chen could not [[recall|L4-0803]] writing a single word of them. She had compared the writing with everyone's except her own.
zh: 第一張紙條出現在佩甄的抽屜裡時，離期末考只剩兩週，這對任何學生來說都是關鍵時刻。紙條上寫著：「深呼吸。你的潛力比你以為的還要大。」署名是「一位朋友」。佩甄好幾個月來一直在和焦慮對抗，這則短短的訊息減輕了她一些煩惱。
從那之後，每個星期一都會出現一張新紙條。每一張都提到只有好朋友才會知道的事，例如她家貓咪的名字，還有她害怕在全班面前說話。佩甄想認出寫紙條的人，於是開始找證據。她把紙條拿來和同學的作業比對，但沒有一個人的字跡和紙條相像。這比她預料的還讓她惱火。
然而，這些紙條支撐著她，她的期末考也考得很好。學期最後一天，她在教室門口遇到了導師王老師。王老師手上拿著另一張紙條，笑著說：「我想是時候讓你知道了。我從一開始就參與其中。」
王老師解釋說，一年前全班每個人都寫了十張短短的紙條給未來的自己。王老師把紙條全都保留了下來，當她注意到佩甄壓力很大時，就開始把佩甄的紙條一張一張放進她的抽屜。佩甄完全想不起來自己寫過其中任何一個字。她拿每個人的字跡去比對，偏偏漏掉了自己的。

questions.stem: What did Pei-chen do to find out who wrote the notes?
options: She asked Ms. Wang to read them to the class.
She hid near her desk every Monday.
She compared the notes with her classmates' homework.
She asked her cat to find the writer.
questions.explain: 第二段說佩甄想找出寫紙條的人，於是把紙條拿來和同學的作業比對，故選 (C)。(A) 文中沒有提到她請老師在班上念紙條。
questions.evidence: She compared the notes with her classmates' homework

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, why did the notes seem to come from a close friend?
options: They were written on expensive paper.
They mentioned things that only a close friend could know.
They were signed with a classmate's name.
They arrived on the same day as her exams.
questions.explain: 第二段說每張紙條都提到只有好朋友才知道的事，例如貓的名字和她害怕上台說話，故選 (B)。(C) 錯，紙條署名是「一位朋友」，沒有寫出任何人的名字。
questions.evidence: Each one made reference to things that only a close friend could know

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, what does the word "This" in "This annoyed her" refer to?
options: Being afraid of speaking in front of the class
Getting a new note every Monday
Not being able to find a match for the writing
Having to take her final exams
questions.explain: This 指前一句的內容：她比對了所有同學的字跡，卻找不到和紙條相像的，所以覺得惱火，故選 (C)。(B) 收到紙條其實讓她安心，並不是讓她惱火的原因。
questions.evidence: none of the writing resembled them

questions.stem: Who most likely wrote the notes?
options: A classmate who sat next to her
questions.explain: 最後一段說全班一年前寫了紙條給未來的自己，由王老師保留並一張張轉交，而佩甄比對字跡時唯獨漏掉自己的，可見紙條是她自己寫的，故選 (B)。(A) 王老師只是保管並轉交紙條的人，不是作者。
questions.evidence: She had compared the writing with everyone's except her own.

vocab.stem: The cat ______ from the room as soon as it heard the thunder.
vocab.explain: 貓一聽到雷聲就「逃離」房間，故選 fled（flee 的過去式）。retained（保留）、resembled（像）、relieved（減輕）都是及物動詞，不能接 from the room，語意也不通。

vocab.stem: Before sailing out to sea, the men loaded their nets onto the ______.
vocab.explain: 出海前把漁網搬到「船」上，故選 vessel。landscape（風景）、rhythm（節奏）、virus（病毒）都不能裝載漁網。

title: Three Generations of One Recipe
paragraphs: For many people in Taiwan, a night market is more than a place to eat. It is a [[landmark|L4-0577]] of local life, where families, students, and tourists walk side by side under bright lights. The [[diversity|L4-0310]] of food is amazing: within a few steps, you can find stinky tofu, sweet potato balls, and bubble tea.

At one small shop in a night market in Tainan, the same [[recipe|L4-0805]] for pork rice has been passed down for three [[generations|L4-0439]]. The owner, Mr. Huang, learned it from his grandfather in an [[era|L4-0358]] when the market was only a few tables on a dirt road. "The [[essential|L4-0359]] thing is the sauce," he says. "We cook it slowly every afternoon, just like Grandpa did."

Times have changed, though. Today's [[consumers|L4-0199]] care more about the environment, so Mr. Huang's son has [[adapted|L4-0018]] the business. Customers who bring their own [[durable|L4-0321]] [[containers|L4-0200]] get a small discount, and the shop no longer hands out plastic bags unless people ask for them.

Night markets also play an important [[economic|L4-0328]] role. They give [[numerous|L4-0674]] small businesses a chance to grow, and they help [[preserve|L4-0761]] traditional flavors. Based on years of [[observation|L4-0681]], Mr. Huang believes people come back for more than just the food. "When people who ate here as children bring their own kids," he says, "I know the market is still alive."
zh: 對許多台灣人來說，夜市不只是吃東西的地方。它是在地生活的地標，家庭、學生和觀光客在明亮的燈光下並肩而行。食物的多樣性令人驚奇：走沒幾步，就能找到臭豆腐、地瓜球和珍珠奶茶。
台南某個夜市裡有一家小店，同一份滷肉飯的食譜已經傳了三代。老闆黃先生是從祖父那裡學來的，那個年代的夜市只是泥土路上的幾張桌子。他說：「最重要的是滷汁。我們每天下午都用小火慢慢煮，就像阿公以前那樣。」
不過，時代已經改變了。現今的消費者更在意環境，所以黃先生的兒子調整了經營方式。自備耐用容器的客人可以享有小小的折扣，除非客人要求，店裡也不再主動提供塑膠袋。
夜市在經濟上也扮演重要的角色。夜市讓眾多小商家有成長的機會，也有助於保存傳統風味。根據多年來的觀察，黃先生相信人們回來不只是為了食物。他說：「當小時候在這裡吃過飯的人，帶著自己的孩子回來時，我就知道夜市還活著。」

questions.stem: According to Mr. Huang, what is the most important part of his pork rice?
options: The kind of rice he buys
The low price of each meal
The sauce that is cooked slowly
questions.explain: 第二段黃先生說最重要的是滷汁，每天下午用小火慢慢煮，故選 (D)。(B) 價格文中完全沒有提到。

questions.stem: How has Mr. Huang's son changed the business?
options: He moved the shop to a bigger market.
He created a new recipe for the sauce.

He stopped selling food to tourists.
questions.explain: 第三段說自備耐用容器的客人可享折扣，店家也不再主動給塑膠袋，故選 (C)。(B) 錯，食譜是三代傳承下來的，並沒有改變。

questions.stem: The word "era" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: era 指「時代、年代」，文中說黃先生從祖父那裡學會食譜，那個年代夜市只是泥土路上的幾張桌子，故選 (A)。(C) a famous place 比較接近第一段的 landmark，不是 era 的意思。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to cook pork rice at home
How a night market shop keeps old traditions while changing with the times
How plastic bags are made in Taiwan
Why tourists should not visit night markets
questions.explain: 文章以夜市為背景，介紹黃家三代傳承的食譜，以及兒子為了環保做出的調整，並說明夜市保存傳統風味的意義，主旨是傳承與改變，故選 (B)。(A) 文中沒有教讀者在家做滷肉飯。
questions.evidence: the same recipe for pork rice has been passed down for three generations

vocab.stem: I have a dentist ______ at three o'clock, so I need to leave school early.
vocab.explain: 三點有牙醫「預約」，所以要提早離開學校，dentist appointment 是固定搭配，故選 appointment。explosion（爆炸）、diversity（多樣性）、observation（觀察）都不能這樣用。

vocab.stem: Please enter the four-digit ______ to open the door.
vocab.explain: 輸入四位數的「密碼」才能開門，故選 code。theme（主題）、era（時代）、council（議會）都不是可以「輸入」的東西。

title: The Scientist Who Changed the Rules
paragraphs: Today, many young women dream of becoming scientists. A little more than a hundred years ago, however, this dream was hard to [[fulfill|L4-0427]]. In many places, women could not study at universities, and few people believed that they could do serious [[research|L4-0837]]. One woman who helped change this was Marie Curie.

Marie was born in Poland in 1867. Because women there were not allowed to attend university, she worked as a private teacher for several years and saved money. In 1891, she moved to Paris to study science and math. She was often hungry and cold. [[Nevertheless|L4-0668]], she finished among the best students in her classes.

In Paris, she began working with the scientist Pierre Curie, who later became her husband. Together they studied a strange [[phenomenon|L4-0730]]: certain materials gave off a kind of energy that no one could see. Through careful [[observation|L4-0681]] and years of hard work, they [[identified|L4-0502]] two new elements. One of them was radium. Their discovery had a huge [[impact|L4-0517]] on science, and it later [[inspired|L4-0538]] new ways to treat cancer.

Marie's [[accomplishments|L4-0011]] were amazing. In 1903, she became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. In 1911, she won a second one in a different science. She is still the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences. She also helped [[establish|L4-0360]] a research center in Paris, where many young scientists were trained.

However, no one in her [[era|L4-0358]] understood how dangerous this energy was. Marie often worked with radium without any protection, and long [[exposure|L4-0379]] to it caused [[severe|L4-0881]] damage to her health. She died in 1934. Even today, her notebooks are kept in special boxes, and visitors must wear protective clothing to read them. Her story has encouraged [[generations|L4-0439]] of young people, of every [[gender|L4-0437]], to follow their dreams.
zh: 今天，許多年輕女性夢想成為科學家。然而在一百多年前，這個夢想很難實現。在許多地方，女性不能上大學，也很少人相信她們能做嚴謹的研究。居禮夫人就是幫助改變這一切的女性之一。
瑪麗在1867年出生於波蘭。由於當地不允許女性上大學，她當了好幾年的家庭教師，把錢存了下來。1891年，她搬到巴黎攻讀科學和數學。她常常又餓又冷。然而，她仍然以班上名列前茅的成績完成學業。
在巴黎，她開始和科學家皮耶・居禮一起工作，皮耶後來成為她的丈夫。他們一起研究一種奇怪的現象：某些物質會放出一種沒人看得見的能量。透過仔細的觀察和多年的努力，他們辨認出兩種新元素，其中之一就是鐳。他們的發現對科學產生巨大的影響，後來也啟發了治療癌症的新方法。
瑪麗的成就非凡。1903年，她成為第一位獲得諾貝爾獎的女性。1911年，她又在另一個科學領域拿下第二座諾貝爾獎。至今她仍是唯一在兩個不同科學領域都獲得諾貝爾獎的人。她也協助在巴黎建立了一個研究中心，培養出許多年輕科學家。
然而，在她那個時代，沒有人了解這種能量有多危險。瑪麗經常在毫無防護的情況下處理鐳，長期暴露在其中嚴重損害了她的健康。她在1934年過世。即使到了今天，她的筆記本仍被保存在特殊的箱子裡，訪客必須穿上防護衣才能閱讀。她的故事鼓舞了一代又一代、不分性別的年輕人追逐自己的夢想。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How radium is used to treat cancer today
Why women could not study at universities in Poland
The life and work of a great woman scientist
How to keep old notebooks safe
questions.explain: 文章依序介紹居禮夫人的求學、與皮耶共同的發現、兩座諾貝爾獎，以及長期暴露於鐳對健康的傷害，主旨是這位女科學家的一生與成就，故選 (C)。(B) 只是第二段的背景細節，不是全文主旨。
questions.evidence: One woman who helped change this was Marie Curie.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Marie Curie?
options: She won two Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
She discovered radium by herself in Poland.
She studied in Paris because it was free.
She knew from the start that radium was dangerous.
questions.explain: 第四段說她1903年和1911年分別在不同科學領域獲獎，是唯一在兩個不同科學領域得過諾貝爾獎的人，故選 (A)。(B) 錯，她是和皮耶在巴黎一起發現的；(D) 錯，第五段說當時沒有人了解這種能量的危險。
questions.evidence: She is still the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

questions.stem: Why must visitors wear protective clothing to read Marie's notebooks?
options: The notebooks are very old and easy to break.
The notebooks still carry some of the dangerous energy.
Visitors might write in the notebooks by mistake.
The notebooks are kept in a very cold room.
questions.explain: 第五段先說長期暴露在鐳的能量下嚴重傷害了她的健康，接著說至今她的筆記本仍放在特殊箱子裡，看的人要穿防護衣，可推知筆記本上仍帶有危險的能量，故選 (B)。(A) 若只是年代久遠、容易損壞，並不需要穿防護衣。
questions.evidence: her notebooks are kept in special boxes, and visitors must wear protective clothing to read them

questions.stem: The word "phenomenon" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: something that happens and can be studied
a place where people do experiments
questions.explain: phenomenon 指「現象」，冒號後面說明這個現象是某些物質會放出看不見的能量，是可以被觀察研究的事情，故選 (C)。(D) 做實驗的地方是 laboratory，不是 phenomenon。
questions.evidence: Together they studied a strange phenomenon: certain materials gave off a kind of energy that no one could see.

vocab.stem: If your stress lasts for a long time, talking to a ______ may help you understand your feelings.
vocab.explain: 壓力持續很久時，和「心理學家」談談可能有助於了解自己的感受，故選 psychologist。landmark（地標）、container（容器）、generation（世代）都不是可以談話的對象。

vocab.stem: Cooking dinner together every Sunday helps build a strong ______ between the children and their parents.
vocab.explain: 每週日一起煮晚餐，有助於在孩子和父母之間建立緊密的「聯繫」，a strong bond between A and B 是常見搭配，故選 bond。recipe（食譜）雖和做菜有關，但不能說「建立在親子之間的食譜」。

title: Homework Helper or Shortcut?
paragraphs: [[Artificial|L4-0057]] intelligence, or AI, is no longer something from the movies. Today, anyone with a phone or another [[device|L4-0278]] can [[access|L4-0008]] AI tools that answer questions, write poems, or plan trips. For high school students, one use is especially attractive: homework.

Imagine you have a writing [[assignment|L4-0064]] due tomorrow. You could ask an AI to write the whole thing, and in a few seconds, you would have [[adequate|L4-0020]] work to hand in. However, teachers warn that this shortcut has a cost. If a machine does the thinking for you, your own writing skills will not improve.

On the [[contrary|L4-0207]], AI can be a great help when it is used wisely. Some students [[consult|L4-0196]] it the way they would ask a tutor. They write the essay by themselves first and then ask the AI for [[comments|L4-0159]]. It may point out a [[clumsy|L4-0151]] sentence or suggest a better word, but the student decides what to [[adjust|L4-0021]].

Another [[issue|L4-0568]] is that AI sometimes gives wrong answers in a very confident way, so checking facts is still an [[essential|L4-0359]] skill. Teachers also point out that good writing has a personal [[aspect|L4-0060]] that no machine can copy. The best essays [[blend|L4-0096]] facts with the writer's own experiences and feelings. AI has great [[potential|L4-0753]] as a learning tool, but in most [[circumstances|L4-0142]], it works best as a helper, not as a replacement for your own mind.
zh: 人工智慧（AI）已經不再是電影裡才有的東西。如今，任何人只要有手機或其他裝置，就能使用回答問題、寫詩或規劃旅行的AI工具。對高中生來說，其中一種用途特別誘人：寫作業。
想像一下，你明天要交一份寫作作業。你可以叫AI把整篇寫完，幾秒鐘後，你就有一份夠格交出去的作品。然而，老師們提醒，這條捷徑是有代價的。如果由機器替你思考，你自己的寫作能力就不會進步。
相反地，如果用得聰明，AI可以幫上大忙。有些學生向AI請教的方式，就像請教家教一樣。他們先自己把文章寫完，再請AI給意見。AI可能會指出一個寫得笨拙的句子，或建議更好的用字，但要修改什麼，由學生自己決定。
另一個問題是，AI有時會用非常肯定的語氣給出錯誤的答案，所以查證事實仍是必備的能力。老師們也指出，好的文章有一個機器無法複製的個人面向。最好的文章會把事實和作者自身的經驗與感受融合在一起。AI作為學習工具有很大的潛力，但在大多數情況下，它最適合當作幫手，而不是取代你自己的思考。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, what is the problem with letting AI write a whole assignment?
options: The work will be too long to hand in.
Your own writing skills will not get better.
The AI will take several hours to finish.
Teachers will not accept any work about AI.
questions.explain: 第二段說如果由機器替你思考，你自己的寫作能力不會進步，這就是捷徑的代價，故選 (B)。(C) 錯，文中說AI只要幾秒鐘就能寫完。
questions.evidence: If a machine does the thinking for you, your own writing skills will not improve.

questions.stem: How do some students use AI wisely?
options: They let AI choose the topic and write every sentence.
They ask AI to check facts for them instead of doing it themselves.
They use AI only to plan trips and write poems.
They write the essay on their own first and ask AI for comments.
questions.explain: 第三段說有些學生先自己把文章寫完，再請AI給意見，最後由自己決定要改什麼，故選 (D)。(B) 錯，第四段反而提醒AI會給錯誤答案，查證事實仍要自己來。
questions.evidence: They write the essay by themselves first and then ask the AI for comments.

questions.stem: The phrase "On the contrary" at the beginning of paragraph 3 shows that the writer is ______.
options: giving another example of the same idea
questions.explain: 第二段講直接讓AI代寫的壞處，第三段以 On the contrary 開頭，轉而說明AI用得聰明可以幫大忙，表示提出相反的觀點，故選 (A)。(B) 前後兩段的看法方向相反，不是同一觀點的另一個例子。
questions.evidence: On the contrary, AI can be a great help when it is used wisely.

questions.stem: Which statement would the writer most likely agree with?
options: Students should never use AI for homework.
AI will soon replace teachers in most schools.
AI should support students' thinking, not replace it.
questions.explain: 作者一方面提醒讓AI代寫會阻礙進步，另一方面肯定AI當作幫手的價值，最後說它最適合當幫手而非取代你的思考，故選 (C)。(A) 太絕對，作者並沒有反對使用AI。
questions.evidence: it works best as a helper, not as a replacement for your own mind

vocab.stem: These flowers only ______ in spring, so the park is full of color in April.
vocab.explain: 這些花只在春天「開花」，所以四月的公園一片繽紛，故選 bloom。retreat（撤退）、consult（請教）、circulate（循環；流傳）都不能用來描述花。

vocab.stem: Life in ______ areas is often quieter than in big cities, with more farms and fewer cars.
vocab.explain: 有較多農田、較少車輛、比大城市安靜的是「鄉村」地區，故選 rural。clumsy（笨拙的）、aggressive（有攻擊性的）、circular（圓形的）都不能用來形容這樣的地區。

title: Read the Back First
paragraphs: Taiwan's [[convenience|L4-0211]] stores are [[fantastic|L4-0386]] for busy students. A rice ball for breakfast, a sandwich for lunch, a sweet drink after class: everything is ready in seconds. But how healthy are these [[options|L4-0692]]? Health experts say that much of the answer is printed on the back of the package.

Instead of [[dismissing|L4-0299]] food labels as boring numbers, try to [[evaluate|L4-0363]] them. Start with sugar and salt. A large cup of sweet milk tea, for example, can contain more sugar than health experts suggest for a whole day. Seeing the number in black and white often makes people think twice.

Experts also put special [[emphasis|L4-0343]] on balance. A meal of white bread or rice alone gives you energy quickly, but you may feel hungry again soon after. Adding an egg, a glass of milk, or some fruit can help [[ensure|L4-0353]] that your body gets [[adequate|L4-0020]] protein and vitamins.

Of course, eating well takes some [[discipline|L4-0295]]. However, you do not have to give up every snack or [[devote|L4-0280]] hours to cooking. Compared with [[conventional|L4-0213]] advice like "Never eat junk food," small changes are easier to follow. The [[explanation|L4-0375]] is simple: people keep habits that feel possible. That is why some schools now [[distribute|L4-0305]] short guides that help students choose better meals, [[including|L4-0522]] ones from the store around the corner.
zh: 台灣的便利商店對忙碌的學生來說非常棒。早餐一個飯糰、午餐一份三明治、下課後一杯甜飲料：每樣東西幾秒內就準備好。但這些選擇到底有多健康呢？健康專家說，答案有很大一部分就印在包裝背面。
別把食品標示當成無聊的數字而不理會，試著評估一下吧。先從糖和鹽看起。例如，一大杯全糖奶茶所含的糖，可能比健康專家建議的一整天攝取量還多。親眼看到白紙黑字的數字，往往會讓人三思。
專家也特別強調均衡。一餐只吃白麵包或白飯，能很快給你能量，但你可能很快又會餓。加一顆蛋、一杯牛奶或一些水果，有助於確保身體獲得足夠的蛋白質和維生素。
當然，好好吃飯需要一點自律。不過，你不必戒掉所有零食，也不必花好幾個小時下廚。和「絕對不要吃垃圾食物」這種傳統的建議相比，小小的改變更容易做到。原因很簡單：人們會維持那些感覺做得到的習慣。這就是為什麼現在有些學校會發放簡短的指南，幫助學生選擇更好的餐點，包括轉角那家商店裡的食物。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, what can a large cup of sweet milk tea contain?
options: Enough protein for a whole day
Less sugar than a glass of milk
More sugar than experts suggest for a whole day
questions.explain: 第二段說一大杯全糖奶茶的含糖量，可能超過健康專家建議的一整天攝取量，故選 (D)。(B) 文中說蛋白質要靠加蛋、牛奶等來補充，與奶茶無關。
questions.evidence: A large cup of sweet milk tea, for example, can contain more sugar than health experts suggest for a whole day.

questions.stem: What does the writer suggest adding to a meal of white bread or rice?
options: An egg, a glass of milk, or some fruit
questions.explain: 第三段建議在只有白麵包或白飯的一餐中加一顆蛋、一杯牛奶或一些水果，以獲得足夠的蛋白質和維生素，故選 (B)。(A)、(C) 都會增加作者提醒要注意的糖和鹽。
questions.evidence: Adding an egg, a glass of milk, or some fruit can help ensure that your body gets adequate protein and vitamins.

questions.stem: The word "dismissing" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 前文說「與其把食品標示當成無聊的數字而 dismissing，不如試著評估它們」，可知 dismissing 是「不予理會」的意思，故選 (A)。(C) reading carefully 正好是作者希望讀者做的事，和 dismissing 相反。
questions.evidence: Instead of dismissing food labels as boring numbers, try to evaluate them.

questions.stem: Why does the writer think small changes work better than "Never eat junk food"?
options: Small changes are more fun to talk about.
People are more likely to keep habits that feel possible.
Schools do not allow students to eat snacks.
questions.explain: 第四段說小改變比「絕對不要吃垃圾食物」更容易做到，因為人們會維持那些感覺做得到的習慣，故選 (C)。(A) 作者並沒有說垃圾食物是健康的。
questions.evidence: The explanation is simple: people keep habits that feel possible.

vocab.stem: Hang your ______ towel outside so that it can dry in the sun.
vocab.explain: 把「濕的」毛巾掛到外面讓太陽曬乾，故選 damp。elegant（優雅的）、fatal（致命的）、digital（數位的）都和「需要曬乾」無關。

vocab.stem: The train to Kaohsiung will ______ at 8:15, so please don't be late.
vocab.explain: 往高雄的火車8:15「出發」，請不要遲到，故選 depart。defend（防衛）、enclose（圍住）、dye（染色）都是及物動詞，而且都不能描述火車開車。

title: When Coral Turns White
paragraphs: Coral reefs are some of the most [[incredible|L4-0523]] places on Earth. Although they cover only a tiny part of the ocean floor, they are home to an [[enormous|L4-0352]] number of sea animals. A reef may look like colorful rock, but it is actually built by tiny living animals called coral.

Coral lives in close [[harmony|L4-0477]] with algae, tiny living things that stay inside its body. The algae use the light of the sun to make food and share it with the coral. In return, the coral gives them a safe home. The algae also give coral its bright colors. This relationship, however, is [[fragile|L4-0419]]. When the water stays too warm for too long, the coral is put under [[intense|L4-0548]] stress and pushes the algae out. Without them, the coral turns white. If the water does not cool down, the coral may slowly die.

Scientific [[investigations|L4-0564]] show that warmer oceans are caused [[largely|L4-0579]] by the burning of [[fossil|L4-0416]] fuels. The situation is [[grave|L4-0462]]: in recent years, large areas of some of the world's biggest reefs have turned white.

There is still hope. In [[laboratories|L4-0575]], [[researchers|L4-0838]] are raising young coral that can better survive [[harsh|L4-0478]] conditions, and they plant it in the sea to help [[restore|L4-0848]] damaged reefs. These efforts [[illustrate|L4-0508]] that people can make a difference, but they also have [[limitations|L4-0593]]. No laboratory can replace a healthy ocean. This [[implies|L4-0518]] that the future of coral depends on cutting the pollution that heats our planet.
zh: 珊瑚礁是地球上最令人驚嘆的地方之一。雖然珊瑚礁只占海底的一小部分，卻是數量龐大的海洋動物的家。珊瑚礁看起來也許像彩色的岩石，但其實是由名叫珊瑚的微小動物建造而成的。
珊瑚和藻類和諧地共同生活，這些微小的生物就住在珊瑚的身體裡。藻類利用陽光製造養分，並分給珊瑚；作為回報，珊瑚提供藻類一個安全的家。藻類也賦予珊瑚鮮豔的顏色。然而，這種關係十分脆弱。當海水長時間過熱，珊瑚會承受強烈的壓力，把藻類排出體外。少了藻類，珊瑚就會變白。如果海水一直沒有降溫，珊瑚可能會慢慢死去。
科學調查顯示，海洋變暖主要是燃燒化石燃料造成的。情況很嚴重：近年來，世界上幾個最大的珊瑚礁都有大片區域變白。
不過，希望仍在。研究人員在實驗室裡培育能在惡劣環境中存活得更好的小珊瑚，再把它們種回海裡，幫助修復受損的珊瑚礁。這些努力說明了人類能帶來改變，但也有其限制。沒有任何實驗室能取代健康的海洋。這意味著珊瑚的未來，取決於減少讓地球變熱的污染。

title: The Cloth Seller Who Found a Hidden World
paragraphs: [[Nowadays|L4-0672]], almost every high school has a [[microscope|L4-0633]] for students to look at plant cells. About 350 years ago, however, such a [[device|L4-0278]] was rare. One of its most [[prominent|L4-0774]] early users was not even a trained scientist. He was a cloth seller in Holland named Leeuwenhoek.

Leeuwenhoek did not [[possess|L4-0750]] a university degree, but he was curious and extremely patient. He taught himself to make tiny glass lenses, and his simple microscopes could make objects look more than 200 times larger. He [[obtained|L4-0683]] water from ponds and rain and studied it for hours. What he saw was [[incredible|L4-0523]]: the water was full of tiny living things swimming around. He called them "little animals."

Starting in 1673, he described these creatures in [[multiple|L4-0658]] letters to the Royal Society, a famous group of scientists in London. At first, many members found his reports hard to believe, and some felt his [[remarks|L4-0829]] could not be [[realistic|L4-0801]]. However, his letters were careful and detailed, and in the end they proved [[persuasive|L4-0727]]. In 1677, scientists in London built their own microscopes and saw the same tiny creatures.

Because Leeuwenhoek had no science training, experts could easily have [[overlooked|L4-0703]] his work. Instead, his [[observations|L4-0681]] made him well known across Europe, and he kept writing letters [[regarding|L4-0819]] his discoveries for about fifty years. Today, he is remembered as one of the first people to see bacteria. His story shows that a [[promising|L4-0775]] discovery can come from anyone with a curious mind and great patience.
zh: 現在幾乎每所高中都有顯微鏡，讓學生觀察植物細胞。然而大約 350 年前，這種裝置非常少見。早期最有名的顯微鏡使用者之一，甚至不是受過訓練的科學家，而是一位住在荷蘭、名叫雷文霍克的布商。
雷文霍克沒有大學學歷，但他充滿好奇心，而且極有耐心。他自學磨製小小的玻璃透鏡，他做的簡易顯微鏡能把物體放大兩百倍以上。他從池塘和雨水中取得水樣，一看就是好幾個小時。他看到的景象令人難以置信：水裡滿是游來游去的微小生物。他把牠們稱為「小動物」。
從 1673 年起，他在多封信中向倫敦一個著名的科學家團體「皇家學會」描述這些生物。起初，許多會員覺得他的報告難以置信，有些人認為他說的話不可能是真的。然而，他的信寫得仔細又詳盡，最後終於說服了大家。1677 年，倫敦的科學家自己做了顯微鏡，也看到了同樣的微小生物。
由於雷文霍克沒有受過科學訓練，專家們很可能忽視他的研究。但事實正好相反，他的觀察讓他聞名全歐洲，此後大約五十年間，他一直寫信報告自己的發現。今天，人們記得他是最早看見細菌的人之一。他的故事告訴我們：只要有好奇心和極大的耐心，任何人都可能做出大有可為的發現。

title: Build It, Test It, Fix It: Join the Maker Club!
paragraphs: Do you love taking things apart to see how they work? If so, the Maker Club wants you! Every Wednesday after school, our members meet in Room 204 to design, build, and test their own projects. It is a place where [[creativity|L4-0234]] matters more than grades.

Last year, our members [[transformed|L4-0960]] old desk lamps into small robot arms. They also built a camera for a bird feeder to record which [[species|L4-0906]] visit our school. You don't need any [[professional|L4-0772]] skills to join. We will teach you how to [[fasten|L4-0389]] parts together, use a [[knob|L4-0573]] to control the speed of a motor, and [[secure|L4-0878]] wires so that nothing comes loose. All the [[equipment|L4-0357]] is provided.

In the first week of each term, there is an [[orientation|L4-0695]] meeting, where older members show their best work and explain how the club runs. After that, you will work in a team of three to draw a plan, test it, and [[revise|L4-0855]] it until it works. Patience is [[essential|L4-0359]], and mistakes are welcome here! At the end of the term, every team shows its project at the school science fair. Projects with strong [[visual|L4-0985]] design are always a big [[attraction|L4-0075]] for visitors.

Want to join? Fill out the form on the club [[website|L4-0991]] by March 10. There are only 24 places, and last year they were all gone in three days. If you want to join, it is [[urgent|L4-0974]] that you sign up soon! Questions? Ask Ms. Huang in the science office.
zh: 你喜歡把東西拆開，看看它們是怎麼運作的嗎？如果是，創客社正需要你！每週三放學後，社員們會在 204 教室設計、製作並測試自己的作品。在這裡，創造力比成績更重要。
去年，社員們把舊檯燈改造成小型機器手臂，還替鳥類餵食器裝了攝影機，記錄有哪些鳥類來學校造訪。你不需要任何專業技能就能加入。我們會教你如何把零件固定在一起、用旋鈕控制馬達的速度，以及把電線固定好，讓它們不會鬆脫。所有器材都由社團提供。
每學期第一週會有新生說明會，學長姐會展示他們最好的作品，並說明社團怎麼運作。之後，你會和另外兩人組成三人小組，一起畫設計圖、動手測試，並不斷修改直到成功為止。耐心是必備的，在這裡犯錯是受歡迎的！學期末，每一組都會在校內科展展出作品，而視覺設計出色的作品總是最吸引參觀者的焦點。
想加入嗎？請在 3 月 10 日前到社團網站填寫表單。名額只有 24 個，去年三天內就全部額滿。如果你想加入，務必儘快報名！有問題嗎？請到自然科辦公室找黃老師。

title: How the Ocean Shapes Our Climate
paragraphs: Look at a picture of the Earth taken from space, and you will see that it is mostly blue. Oceans cover more than two-thirds of our planet's surface. It is easy to [[overlook|L4-0703]] how much the sea does for us. In fact, the ocean plays a key role in shaping the world's climate.

First, the ocean works like a giant store of heat. Water can hold far more heat than air. As a result, much of the extra heat that gases from burning [[fossil|L4-0416]] fuels trap in the [[atmosphere|L4-0071]] ends up in the sea. Without the ocean, temperatures on land would have risen much faster. Ocean currents also [[circulate|L4-0140]] this heat around the world, carrying warm water toward the poles and cold water back again.

However, this service comes at a cost. Water takes up more space as it warms. This [[expansion|L4-0373]], together with melting ice on land, is slowly raising sea levels. Warmer water also harms [[fragile|L4-0419]] coral reefs. When the sea stays too hot, corals lose the tiny living partners that give them food and color, and they turn white. If such [[harsh|L4-0478]] [[circumstances|L4-0142]] last too long, the corals may die, and the many [[species|L4-0906]] that depend on them can lose their homes.

To understand these changes, scientists have [[devoted|L4-0280]] years to studying the sea. Ships go on long [[voyages|L4-0989]] to measure the temperature of deep water, and thousands of floating machines send back reports from [[multiple|L4-0658]] depths. With these [[technological|L4-0937]] tools, scientists can [[obtain|L4-0683]] information that could not be collected a few decades ago. Their [[investigations|L4-0564]] help experts [[evaluate|L4-0363]] how quickly the ocean is changing.

The message from this work is [[urgent|L4-0974]]. For many years, the ocean has protected us from the worst effects of a warming world, but its ability to do so has limits. If we want the ocean to keep taking care of us, we will have to take better care of it.
zh: 看看從太空拍下的地球照片，你會發現它大部分是藍色的。海洋覆蓋了地球表面三分之二以上。我們很容易忽略大海為我們做了多少事。事實上，海洋在塑造全球氣候上扮演著關鍵角色。
首先，海洋就像一座巨大的儲熱庫。水能容納的熱比空氣多得多，因此，燃燒化石燃料產生的氣體困在大氣中的額外熱量，有很大一部分最後都進了海裡。如果沒有海洋，陸地上的氣溫會上升得更快。洋流也讓這些熱在全球循環流動，把溫暖的海水帶往兩極，再把冰冷的海水帶回來。
然而，這項服務是有代價的。水變暖時體積會變大。這種膨脹，加上陸地上的冰融化，正讓海平面緩緩上升。較溫暖的海水也會傷害脆弱的珊瑚礁。當海水一直太熱，珊瑚會失去提供牠們養分與顏色的微小共生夥伴，因而變白。如果這種嚴酷的環境持續太久，珊瑚可能會死亡，許多依賴珊瑚生存的物種也會失去家園。
為了了解這些變化，科學家們投入多年時間研究海洋。船隻進行長途航行，測量深海的水溫；數以千計的漂浮儀器則從不同深度傳回報告。有了這些科技工具，科學家能取得幾十年前無法蒐集到的資訊。他們的調查幫助專家評估海洋變化的速度有多快。
這些研究傳達的訊息十分緊迫。多年來，海洋一直保護我們免受全球暖化最嚴重的影響，但它的能力是有極限的。如果我們希望海洋繼續照顧我們，就必須更好地照顧它。

options: Air can hold more heat than water.

Burning fossil fuels has no effect on the sea.
Without the ocean, land on Earth would be hotter today.
questions.explain: 第二段說如果沒有海洋，陸地氣溫會上升得更快，可推知海洋吸收了熱，否則陸地現在會更熱，故選 (D)。(A) 與文中「水能容納的熱比空氣多得多」相反。
questions.evidence: Without the ocean, temperatures on land would have risen much faster.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does the word "them" in "the many species that depend on them" refer to?
questions.explain: 這句前半說「珊瑚可能會死亡」，後半接著說許多「依賴它們」的物種會失去家園，them 指的是珊瑚，故選 (B)。珊瑚礁是許多海洋生物的家，所以珊瑚死了牠們才會無家可歸。
questions.evidence: the corals may die, and the many species that depend on them can lose their homes

vocab.stem: Doing these exercises every day will ______ the muscles in your legs.
vocab.explain: 每天做這些運動會「強化」腿部肌肉，故選 strengthen。revise（修訂）、summarize（摘要）、compose（組成；作曲）都不能拿來形容運動對肌肉的效果。

vocab.stem: Long ago, ______ traveled from town to town to sell tea and other goods.
vocab.explain: 很久以前，「商人」們從一個城鎮到另一個城鎮販賣茶葉等貨物，故選 merchants。只有人才會四處旅行做生意，species（物種）、websites（網站）、knobs（旋鈕）都不合理。

title: The Poster That Kept Disappearing
paragraphs: For a week, something strange happened at Mei's school. Every afternoon, the drama club hung its new poster, a colorful [[illustration|L4-0509]] in a wooden [[frame|L4-0420]], in the hallway. But every morning, the poster was gone. Later, someone would always find it in the art room.

To Mei, a drama club member, it felt like the [[plot|L4-0742]] of a mystery novel. To [[complicate|L4-0168]] things, the art room was locked at night with a [[combination|L4-0156]] lock, and few people knew the numbers. A student had seen one of the Wang twins there late one evening. However, the twins were [[identical|L4-0500]], so the [[witness|L4-0997]] could not [[identify|L4-0502]] which girl it was, and both said they had gone straight home.

Mei [[recalled|L4-0803]] a [[fundamental|L4-0429]] rule of mystery stories: notice small details. The girl on the poster had an interesting [[facial|L4-0382]] expression, half happy and half sad. Then, in the art room, Mei found the [[evidence|L4-0366]] she needed: a drawing book full of faces with that same expression.

The book belonged to Hannah, a first-year student. This [[prompted|L4-0777]] Mei to talk with her, and Hannah quickly made an [[admission|L4-0024]]. The art teacher had told her the lock numbers for after-school practice. Each evening, she took the poster to the art room to copy the girl's face. She always planned to return it early the next morning, but never arrived in time. "I didn't think about the [[consequences|L4-0186]]," she said. Instead of getting angry, the drama club asked Hannah to draw next year's poster.
zh: 有一個星期，梅的學校發生了一件怪事。每天下午，戲劇社都會把新海報──一張裝在木頭相框裡、色彩繽紛的插畫──掛在走廊上。可是每天早上，海報都不見了。後來，總會有人在美術教室找到它。
對戲劇社社員梅來說，這感覺就像推理小說的情節。讓事情更複雜的是，美術教室晚上會用密碼鎖鎖上，而且很少人知道密碼。有個學生某天傍晚很晚的時候，在那裡看到王家雙胞胎的其中一個。然而，這對雙胞胎長得一模一樣，所以這位目擊者無法認出是哪一個，而兩人都說她們當天直接回家了。
梅想起推理故事的一條基本原則：注意小細節。海報上女孩的臉部表情非常耐人尋味，一半開心、一半悲傷。接著，她在美術教室找到了她需要的證據：一本畫滿了相同表情臉孔的畫冊。
畫冊的主人是一年級的漢娜。這促使梅去找她談談，而漢娜很快就承認了。原來美術老師告訴她密碼，讓她放學後練習用。每天傍晚，她都把海報拿到美術教室，臨摹畫中女孩的臉。她總打算隔天一早就把海報放回去，卻從來沒有及時趕到。「我沒有想過後果。」她說。戲劇社並沒有生氣，反而請漢娜畫明年的海報。

questions.stem: Where was the poster found each day?
questions.explain: 第一段說海報每天早上不見後，當天稍晚總會有人在美術教室找到它，故選 (B)。(A) 走廊是海報原本掛的地方，不是失蹤後被找到的地方。

questions.stem: Why could the witness not tell which twin she had seen?
options: It was too dark to see anything.
The twins were not at school that day.
She did not know the Wang family.
The two sisters looked exactly alike.
questions.explain: 第二段說這對雙胞胎長得一模一樣（identical），所以目擊者認不出是哪一個，故選 (D)。文中沒有提到天色太暗，(A) 是無中生有。

questions.stem: The word "admission" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: a ticket to enter a place
a statement that she had done something
questions.explain: 接下來漢娜說明了自己每天傍晚把海報拿走的經過，可知 made an admission 是「承認自己做了某事」，故選 (C)。admission 也有「入場許可」的意思，但 (A) 放在這裡不合文意。
questions.evidence: Hannah quickly made an admission.

questions.stem: What can we infer about the drama club's reaction?
options: They reported Hannah to the art teacher.
They decided to stop making posters.
They still believed one of the twins took the poster.
questions.explain: 最後一句說戲劇社沒有生氣，反而請漢娜畫明年的海報，可推知他們欣賞她的畫畫能力，故選 (A)。(D) 錯，真相大白後已知是漢娜拿走的，與雙胞胎無關。
questions.evidence: Instead of getting angry, the drama club asked Hannah to draw next year's poster.

vocab.stem: Wash your hands before you eat, because they may carry ______ that can make you sick.
vocab.explain: 吃東西前要洗手，因為手上可能帶有會讓人生病的「細菌」，故選 germs。frames（框架）、mills（磨坊）、plots（情節）都不會讓人生病。

vocab.stem: With no wind to push it, the small boat ______ slowly out to sea.
vocab.explain: 沒有風推動，小船慢慢「漂流」到海上，故選 drifted。complicated（使複雜）、entertained（娛樂）、prompted（促使）都是及物動詞，後面需要受詞，也不能描述船的移動。

title: The Message That Said Too Little
paragraphs: Last spring, Joy was [[absorbed|L4-0003]] in planning a small party for the third [[anniversary|L4-0041]] of her friendship with Emma. She made a [[reservation|L4-0840]] at their favorite dessert shop and sent Emma a long, excited message about the plan. A few minutes later, Emma replied with a single word: "Fine." Was Emma upset? That night, Joy almost [[accused|L4-0014]] her friend of being cold, but she decided to wait.

The next day, Emma explained that she had been busy preparing for an [[academic|L4-0005]] contest and had typed the reply while running to class. "I was really happy about the plan!" she said. She made a quick [[apology|L4-0045]] for sounding so short, and they both laughed.

In face-to-face [[communication|L4-0162]], we hear a friend's tone of voice and see her expression, so it is easy to tell a joke from a complaint. In a text message, those signals disappear, and we must guess. Our guesses often lack [[accuracy|L4-0013]]. A short reply might simply mean the writer is busy, but a worried reader may [[interpret|L4-0556]] it as anger, and a [[comment|L4-0159]] meant as a joke can sound rude.

So what is the [[alternative|L4-0033]] to guessing? First, if a message hurts your feelings, don't reply right away; ask a friendly question instead. Second, when something important needs to be said, it is [[vital|L4-0986]] to call or talk in person. Now Emma [[urges|L4-0973]] her friends to follow one simple rule: "Read it twice before you get upset."
zh: 去年春天，喬伊全心投入籌劃一個小派對，慶祝她和艾瑪成為朋友三週年。她在兩人最愛的甜點店訂了位，並傳給艾瑪一則興奮的長訊息說明計畫。幾分鐘後，艾瑪只回了一個字：「好。」艾瑪不高興嗎？那天晚上，喬伊差點指責朋友態度冷淡，但她決定先等等。
隔天，艾瑪解釋說，她那時忙著準備一場學科競賽，是在趕去上課的路上打字回覆的。「我其實很喜歡這個計畫！」她說。她很快為回覆太簡短道了歉，兩人都笑了出來。
面對面溝通時，我們聽得到朋友的語氣、看得到她的表情，所以很容易分辨她是在開玩笑還是在抱怨。但在文字訊息裡，這些訊號消失了，我們只能用猜的，而我們的猜測常常不夠準確。簡短的回覆可能只代表對方很忙，但心裡不安的讀者卻可能把它解讀成生氣；一句本來是開玩笑的評論，也可能聽起來很沒禮貌。
那麼，除了猜測還有什麼辦法呢？第一，如果一則訊息讓你難過，先不要馬上回覆，改用友善的方式問問看。第二，有重要的事要說時，打電話或當面談是非常重要的。現在艾瑪總是勸朋友們遵守一條簡單的規則：「先讀兩遍，再決定要不要生氣。」

questions.stem: Why did Emma reply with only one word?
options: She was angry about the party.
She did not like the dessert shop.
She was busy and typed it while running to class.
Her phone was not working well.
questions.explain: 第二段艾瑪解釋，她當時忙著準備學科競賽，是在趕去上課途中打字回覆的，故選 (C)。(A) 是喬伊一開始的誤會，艾瑪其實說她很喜歡這個計畫。
questions.evidence: had typed the reply while running to class

questions.stem: What did Joy do after she got Emma's reply?
options: She almost accused Emma of being cold but waited.
She asked other friends what to do.
questions.explain: 第一段說那天晚上喬伊差點指責艾瑪態度冷淡，但決定先等等，故選 (B)。文中沒有說她取消訂位或打電話，(A)、(C) 都是無中生有。
questions.evidence: That night, Joy almost accused her friend of being cold, but she decided to wait.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, what does "those signals" refer to?
options: A friend's tone of voice and expression
questions.explain: 前一句說面對面時我們聽得到語氣、看得到表情；接著說在文字訊息裡「這些訊號」消失了，指的就是語氣和表情，故選 (D)。(A) 是我們要靠這些訊號去分辨的內容，不是訊號本身。
questions.evidence: we hear a friend's tone of voice and see her expression

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Text messages can easily be read the wrong way, so we should not react too quickly.
Friends should stop sending text messages.
Planning a party takes a lot of time.
A short reply always shows that a person is angry.
questions.explain: 文章以喬伊誤會艾瑪的故事開頭，說明文字訊息缺少語氣和表情、容易被誤解，最後建議先別急著回覆、重要的事當面談，故選 (A)。(D) 與文意相反，文中說簡短回覆可能只是對方很忙。
questions.evidence: In a text message, those signals disappear, and we must guess.

vocab.stem: Many ______ do not eat meat, fish, or eggs.
vocab.explain: 許多「素食者」不吃肉、魚或蛋，故選 vegetarians。settlers（移居者）、amateurs（業餘者）、applicants（申請人）都和飲食習慣無關。

vocab.stem: During the storm, the visitors found ______ in a small cave.
vocab.explain: 暴風雨中，遊客們在小山洞裡找到「遮蔽處」，find shelter 是常見搭配，故選 shelter。reward（獎賞）、accent（口音）、spear（矛）都不合文意。

title: From Tree Bark to Medicine Cabinet
paragraphs: For thousands of years, people in many [[civilizations|L4-0144]] have used plants to treat pain. In ancient Egypt and Greece, people used willow bark to ease pain and fever. Some simply [[chewed|L4-0136]] on the bark. They did not know why it worked, only that it often did.

In the 1800s, scientists studied the [[association|L4-0067]] between willow bark and lower fevers. They found a natural chemical in the bark that fights pain and fever. Medicines made from this chemical worked, but they often upset the stomach. In 1897, a scientist at a German company made a gentler form of it, which was soon sold as [[aspirin|L4-0061]]. Today, aspirin is still found in many medicine [[cabinets|L4-0112]]. Few medicines can [[boast|L4-0101]] such a long history.

For decades, however, no one knew how aspirin worked. The answer came only in 1971, when a British scientist and his [[colleagues|L4-0155]] showed that it stops the body from making certain chemicals that cause pain. [[Researchers|L4-0838]] have not [[ceased|L4-0128]] studying it and still find new uses for it.

Aspirin's story shows both the value and the limits of traditional [[remedies|L4-0831]]. Old treatments can point scientists in the right direction. However, not every traditional remedy works, and some can even be harmful. That is why health [[authorities|L4-0078]] ask for careful tests and clear [[evidence|L4-0366]] before a new medicine is sold. In other words, science does not throw tradition away; it tests it. A plant remedy that passes such tests can move from the [[category|L4-0127]] of "old belief" to "modern medicine."
zh: 數千年來，許多文明的人們都用植物來治療疼痛。在古埃及和古希臘，人們用柳樹的樹皮來減輕疼痛、退燒，有些人乾脆直接嚼樹皮。他們不知道為什麼有效，只知道它常常管用。
到了 1800 年代，科學家研究了柳樹皮和退燒之間的關聯。他們發現樹皮中含有一種能對抗疼痛和發燒的天然化學物質。用這種物質做成的藥雖然有效，卻常常讓人胃不舒服。1897 年，一家德國公司的科學家做出了比較溫和的形式，不久便以「阿斯匹靈」的名稱販售。今天，許多藥櫃裡仍然有阿斯匹靈。很少有藥能誇耀如此悠久的歷史。
然而，有幾十年的時間，沒有人知道阿斯匹靈的作用原理。答案直到 1971 年才揭曉：一位英國科學家和他的同事證明，它能阻止身體製造某些引起疼痛的化學物質。研究人員至今仍未停止研究它，也仍不斷為它找到新用途。
阿斯匹靈的故事同時顯示了傳統療法的價值與侷限。古老的療法可以為科學家指引正確的方向；然而，並非每一種傳統療法都有效，有些甚至可能有害。這就是為什麼衛生主管機關在新藥上市前，要求進行仔細的試驗並提出明確的證據。換句話說，科學並不是丟棄傳統，而是檢驗傳統。通過這類檢驗的植物療法，就能從「古老信仰」的類別移到「現代醫學」。

questions.stem: How did some people in ancient times use willow bark?
options: They burned it to keep warm.
They chewed on it to ease pain.
They used it to build boats.
questions.explain: 第一段說古埃及和古希臘人用柳樹皮止痛退燒，有些人乾脆直接嚼樹皮，故選 (B)。其他選項文中都沒有提到。

questions.stem: What happened in 1897?
options: Willow trees were first planted in Europe.
A British scientist won a prize.
A scientist made a gentler medicine that became aspirin.
questions.explain: 第二段說 1897 年一家德國公司的科學家做出較溫和的形式，後來以阿斯匹靈販售，故選 (D)。(B) 是 1971 年才發生的事。
questions.evidence: In 1897, a scientist at a German company made a gentler form of it, which was soon sold as aspirin.

questions.stem: The word "ceased" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 句子後半說研究人員「仍然」不斷找到新用途，可知 have not ceased studying 是「仍未停止研究」，ceased 意思是 stopped，故選 (A)。(B) started 會與「持續研究」的意思矛盾。
questions.evidence: Researchers have not ceased studying it

questions.stem: What is the writer's view of traditional remedies?
options: They are always better than modern medicine.
They should all be thrown away.
They can be useful, but they need to be tested.
They are only used in ancient countries.
questions.explain: 最後一段說傳統療法能為科學指引方向，但不是每一種都有效，所以科學「不是丟棄傳統，而是檢驗傳統」，故選 (C)。(A)、(B) 都太極端，與作者平衡的看法不符。
questions.evidence: science does not throw tradition away; it tests it.

vocab.stem: After the party, Dad used a ______ to sweep the floor.
vocab.explain: 派對結束後，爸爸用「掃帚」掃地，故選 broom。blade（刀刃）、bin（箱子；垃圾桶）、canoe（獨木舟）都不是用來掃地的工具。

vocab.stem: The ball hit the wall and ______ back to me.
vocab.explain: 球打到牆壁後「彈」回我這裡，故選 bounced。chewed（咀嚼）、boasted（自誇）、choked（噎住）都不能描述球的動作。

title: The Secret of the Spinning Ball
paragraphs: In a [[competitive|L4-0166]] table tennis match, a ball that suddenly dips or [[curves|L4-0249]] can win a point. To the player on the other side, it may look like magic. Scientists, however, can [[demonstrate|L4-0265]] that it follows simple scientific rules.

When a ball spins as it flies, it drags a thin layer of air around with it. As a result, the air passing the ball is pushed off to one side, and the ball is pushed the opposite way. This [[phenomenon|L4-0730]] is called the Magnus effect, after a German scientist who studied it in the 1850s. It explains why a spinning ball does not travel in a straight line.

When the top of the ball spins forward, the ball dives quickly onto the table. This lets players hit hard without sending the ball off the end of the table. A [[defensive|L4-0259]] player, in [[contrast|L4-0208]], often makes the ball spin backward, which keeps it low and makes it harder to attack. Top players also watch for small [[cues|L4-0244]], such as the angle of the other player's bat, to guess what kind of spin is coming.

Of course, knowing the science alone will not make anyone a champion. It takes years of [[intense|L4-0548]] practice and deep [[concentration|L4-0173]]. Players must [[commit|L4-0161]] themselves to daily training and build [[physical|L4-0735]] strength. Still, many coaches are [[convinced|L4-0216]] that understanding spin can [[contribute|L4-0209]] to faster progress. After all, when a player wins a point with a perfect curving shot, she [[deserves|L4-0272]] to know why it worked.
zh: 在一場競爭激烈的桌球比賽中，一顆突然下墜或轉彎的球，就能拿下一分。對另一邊的選手來說，這看起來可能像魔術。然而，科學家可以證明它遵循的是簡單的科學原理。
球一邊飛一邊旋轉時，會帶動周圍一層薄薄的空氣跟著轉。結果，流過球的空氣被推向一側，球則被推往相反方向。這種現象叫做「馬格努斯效應」，名稱來自 1850 年代研究它的一位德國科學家。它說明了為什麼旋轉的球不會走直線。
當桌球的上方向前旋轉，球會迅速往下衝到桌面上，讓選手可以用力擊球而不會讓球飛出球桌。相對地，防守型的選手常常讓球向後旋轉，使球保持低平、更難進攻。頂尖選手也會留意一些小線索，例如對手球拍的角度，來猜測接下來會是哪一種旋轉。
當然，光懂科學並不能讓人成為冠軍。那需要多年的高強度練習和高度的專注力。選手必須全心投入每天的訓練，並鍛鍊體力。儘管如此，許多教練深信，了解旋轉的原理有助於進步得更快。畢竟，當一位選手用一記完美的弧線球拿下一分時，她也理應知道這球為什麼會成功。

questions.stem: What does the Magnus effect explain?
options: Why a spinning ball does not travel in a straight line
How to hold a table tennis bat
Why German players often win matches
Where the ball must land on the table
questions.explain: 第二段說馬格努斯效應說明了旋轉的球為什麼不會走直線，故選 (A)。(C) 文中只說這名稱來自一位德國科學家，和德國選手是否常贏球無關。
questions.evidence: It explains why a spinning ball does not travel in a straight line.

questions.stem: Why do players make the top of the ball spin forward?
options: To make the ball float slowly
To make the ball stop spinning
To hit hard and still keep the ball on the table
To make the ball fly off the end of the table
questions.explain: 第三段說球的上方向前旋轉時，球會往下衝向桌面，讓選手能用力擊球而不會讓球飛出球桌，故選 (C)。(D) 剛好相反。
questions.evidence: This lets players hit hard without sending the ball off the end of the table.

questions.stem: The word "cues" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.

title: Streets That Put People First
paragraphs: For most of the last hundred years, cars have been the [[dominant|L4-0314]] form of transport in many cities. Wide roads and huge parking lots took up much of the space, and [[exhaust|L4-0370]] from millions of engines filled the air. People who could not drive, such as young children and some people with a [[disability|L4-0291]], were often at a [[disadvantage|L4-0292]].

Now, many city designers are imagining a [[distinctly|L4-0302]] different future. In their [[drafts|L4-0316]] of future cities, streets are shared by buses, bicycles, and people on foot, and private cars are the [[exception|L4-0369]] rather than the rule. Some cities are testing buses that drive themselves, while others are building bike paths that connect [[diverse|L4-0309]] neighborhoods.

One famous example comes from Seoul, the [[capital|L4-0121]] of South Korea. In the early 2000s, the city decided to remove a busy highway that had been built over an old stream. Many drivers [[dreaded|L4-0317]] the change and expected terrible traffic. Instead, the stream was [[restored|L4-0848]], and a long public park opened along it in 2005. Today, it is a popular place for walking, and [[researchers|L4-0838]] have found that the area is cooler in summer than nearby busy roads.

Changes like these need careful [[engineering|L4-0350]] and honest [[evaluation|L4-0364]]. Not every plan works, and some cause problems at first. But the goal is [[evident|L4-0367]]: cities where everyone, not just drivers, can move around safely and breathe cleaner air. The [[eventual|L4-0365]] result may be streets that feel less like highways and more like [[dynamic|L4-0324]] public living rooms.
zh: 在過去一百年的大部分時間裡，汽車一直是許多城市最主要的交通方式。寬闊的道路和巨大的停車場佔去了大量空間，數以百萬計的引擎排出的廢氣充滿了空氣。不會開車的人，例如年幼的孩子和部分身心障礙者，常常處於不利的處境。
如今，許多城市設計者正在想像一個截然不同的未來。在他們的未來城市草圖裡，街道由公車、腳踏車和行人共享，私家車反而成了例外。有些城市正在測試自動駕駛公車，有些則在興建連接各種不同社區的自行車道。
一個著名的例子來自南韓首都首爾。2000 年代初期，首爾決定拆除一條蓋在一條老溪流上方、車流繁忙的高架道路。許多駕駛人非常擔心這項改變，以為交通會變得一團糟。結果，溪流恢復了原貌，沿岸一座長長的公園在 2005 年開放。如今那裡是熱門的散步地點，研究也發現，那一帶夏天比附近車多的道路還要涼爽。
這樣的改變需要細心的工程規劃和誠實的評估。不是每個計畫都會成功，有些一開始還會造成問題。但目標很明顯：打造一座不只駕駛人、而是每個人都能安全移動、呼吸更乾淨空氣的城市。最終，街道給人的感覺可能不再像公路，而更像充滿活力的公共客廳。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, who was often at a disadvantage in cities built for cars?
questions.explain: 第一段說不會開車的人，例如年幼的孩子和部分身心障礙者，常常處於不利的處境，故選 (B)。其他選項文中都沒有說他們處境不利。

questions.stem: The word "dreaded" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.

questions.explain: 文章先說汽車主導城市的問題，再介紹規劃者對未來街道的構想與首爾的例子，最後點出目標是讓每個人都能安全移動，故選 (C)。(A) 與文章立場相反。

vocab.stem: If you lose your passport while traveling abroad, you should go to your country's ______ for help.
vocab.explain: 在國外弄丟護照時，應該到本國的「大使館」求助，故選 embassy。dynasty（朝代）、drill（演習；鑽子）、draft（草稿）都不是可以求助的機構。

vocab.stem: Amy is a ______ student; she reviews her notes every night and never misses a class.
vocab.explain: 艾咪每晚複習筆記、從不缺課，是個「勤奮的」學生，故選 diligent。desperate（絕望的；拚命的）、elementary（基本的；初級的）、distinct（明顯的；不同的）都不能說明分號後面的認真表現。

title: The Painters Who Were Laughed At
paragraphs: Today, Impressionist paintings are among the most popular works in museums around the world. Their soft colors and bright light attract crowds wherever they are shown. Yet when these paintings first appeared in Paris about 150 years ago, many people thought they were not finished, and some even called them ugly.

In the 1800s, the art world in France followed strict [[academic|L4-0005]] rules. A huge yearly show in Paris decided which artists would succeed. Its judges preferred large paintings of history and [[legends|L4-0586]], painted with great [[accuracy|L4-0013]] and smooth surfaces. Pictures of daily life belonged to a lower [[category|L4-0127]] and received less respect.

A group of young painters, such as Claude Monet, wanted to break these rules. Instead of working indoors, they carried their paints outside to catch the changing light of a single moment. A [[fundamental|L4-0429]] new tool made this possible: paint sold in small metal tubes, which was invented in 1841 and was easy to carry. Their quick brush marks were clearly [[evident|L4-0367]], in sharp [[contrast|L4-0208]] to the smooth surfaces the judges loved. After the yearly show refused their work again and again, the group held its own show in 1874.

One of the paintings Monet showed there was a view of a harbor at sunrise called Impression, Sunrise. A [[critic|L4-0236]] used its title to make fun of the whole group, calling them "Impressionists." The name was meant to hurt, but the painters [[eventually|L4-0365]] [[adopted|L4-0025]] it themselves.

For years, few people bought their work, and several of the artists [[endured|L4-0348]] serious money problems. Still, their [[ambitious|L4-0036]] idea that a painting could [[convey|L4-0215]] the feeling of a passing moment slowly won many fans. Today, these artists are seen as [[pioneers|L4-0740]] of modern art. Their story [[demonstrates|L4-0265]] that an idea laughed at in one [[era|L4-0358]] may be admired in the next.
zh: 今天，印象派畫作是世界各地美術館裡最受歡迎的作品之一。它們柔和的色彩與明亮的光線，無論在哪裡展出都能吸引人潮。然而，大約 150 年前這些畫作剛在巴黎出現時，許多人覺得它們看起來像沒畫完，有些人甚至說它們很醜。
在 1800 年代，法國藝術界遵循嚴格的學院派規則。巴黎每年舉辦一場大型展覽（沙龍展），它決定了哪些藝術家能夠成功。沙龍的評審偏愛描繪歷史與傳說的大型畫作，要畫得極為精確、表面平滑。描繪日常生活的畫則被歸在較低的類別，也較不受重視。
一群年輕畫家，例如克勞德・莫內，想要打破這些規則。他們不在室內作畫，而是把顏料帶到戶外，捕捉某一瞬間變化的光線。一項根本性的新工具讓這件事成為可能：裝在小金屬管裡販售的顏料。這種顏料於 1841 年發明，攜帶十分方便。他們快速的筆觸清晰可見，與評審們喜愛的平滑表面形成強烈對比。在作品一再被這個年度大展拒絕之後，這群畫家於 1874 年自行舉辦了展覽。
莫內在那次展覽中展出的作品之一，是一幅描繪日出時港口景色的畫，名為《印象・日出》。一位評論家借用這個標題來嘲笑整群畫家，稱他們為「印象派」。這個名稱本來帶有惡意，但這些畫家最後卻自己採用了它。
多年來，很少人購買他們的作品，其中好幾位畫家還熬過了嚴重的經濟困境。儘管如此，他們那個充滿野心的想法──一幅畫可以傳達稍縱即逝的瞬間感受──慢慢贏得了許多喜愛者。如今，這些畫家被視為現代藝術的先驅。他們的故事證明了：在某個時代被嘲笑的想法，到了下一個時代可能會備受推崇。

options: How the yearly show chose its judges
How a group of painters who were once laughed at became important
Why paint in tubes was invented
How to paint a harbor at sunrise
questions.explain: 文章從印象派畫作當年被嘲笑寫起，說明他們如何對抗學院規則、名稱的由來，最後成為現代藝術的先驅，故選 (B)。(C) 顏料管只是第三段提到的一個細節。

options: It was cheaper than other paint.

questions.explain: 第三段說這群畫家把顏料帶到戶外作畫，而裝在金屬管裡、方便攜帶的顏料「讓這件事成為可能」，可推知管裝顏料讓他們能在戶外作畫，故選 (C)。文中沒有提到價格或顏色，(A)、(B) 無中生有。
questions.evidence: paint sold in small metal tubes, which was invented in 1841 and was easy to carry

questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does the word "it" in "the painters eventually adopted it themselves" refer to?
questions.explain: 前一句說評論家用「印象派」這個名稱嘲笑整群畫家，接著說這個名稱本來帶有惡意，但畫家們最後自己採用了 it，指的就是這個名稱，故選 (A)。這也是「印象派」一詞的由來。
questions.evidence: The name was meant to hurt, but the painters eventually adopted it themselves.

vocab.stem: Our school holds a fire ______ every term so that students know how to leave the building safely.
vocab.explain: 學校每學期都舉行消防「演習」，讓學生知道如何安全離開大樓，fire drill 是固定搭配，故選 drill。dynasty（朝代）、embassy（大使館）、exception（例外）都不能和 fire 搭配。

vocab.explain: 跑完十公里後，莉莉「筋疲力盡」，在沙發上睡著了，故選 exhausted。drilled（鑽孔；訓練）、endured（忍受）、drafted（起草）都不能放在 was completely 後面形容人的狀態。

title: Ten Pages a Day
paragraphs: Iris loved stories when she was little, but in high school she rarely finished a book. She was a [[habitual|L4-0472]] phone checker, and she found it hard to [[concentrate|L4-0172]] on anything for long. She felt a little [[guilty|L4-0470]] whenever she looked at the [[gigantic|L4-0445]] pile of books she had not read.

Everything changed when the library in her town started a program called "Ten Pages a Day." The [[founder|L4-0418]] of the program, a former teacher, believed that small goals are easier to keep than big ones. The rules were [[flexible|L4-0406]]: readers could choose any book and read at any time, as long as they read ten pages. Those who stayed [[faithful|L4-0384]] to the challenge for a month got a small [[reward|L4-0859]].

At first, Iris read only for the prize. But one evening, she caught a [[glimpse|L4-0448]] of the clock and realized she had been reading for two hours without touching her phone. Her [[genuine|L4-0442]] love of stories had come back. To some [[extent|L4-0381]], she says, the library staff helped too. Instead of telling her what she "should" read, they suggested books that matched her interests.

When the month ended, Iris's reading did not [[halt|L4-0473]]. She kept going and finished twelve books by the end of the year. [[Inspired|L4-0538]] by the program's success, the library has decided to [[extend|L4-0380]] it through the whole summer. "A reading habit is like a plant," the founder says. "Give it [[fertile|L4-0396]] soil and a little time, and it will grow on its own."
zh: 艾莉絲小時候很愛聽故事，但上了高中後卻很少讀完一本書。她習慣性地一直查看手機，做什麼事都很難專心太久。每次看著那一大疊沒讀過的書，她都會有點罪惡感。
直到她家鄉的圖書館推出一項名為「一天十頁」的活動，一切才有了改變。活動的發起人是一位以前當過老師的人，她相信小目標比大目標更容易堅持。規則很有彈性：讀者可以選任何書、在任何時間閱讀，只要讀滿十頁就好。一個月都忠實完成挑戰的人，可以得到一份小獎品。
一開始，艾莉絲只是為了獎品而讀。但某天晚上，她瞥了一眼時鐘，才發現自己已經連續讀了兩個小時，完全沒碰手機。她對故事真心的喜愛又回來了。她說，在某種程度上，圖書館的工作人員也有幫上忙。他們沒有告訴她「應該」讀什麼，而是推薦符合她興趣的書。
一個月結束後，艾莉絲並沒有停止閱讀。她持續讀下去，到年底一共讀完了十二本書。受到活動成功的鼓舞，圖書館決定把它延長到整個暑假。「閱讀習慣就像一株植物，」發起人說，「給它肥沃的土壤和一點時間，它自己就會長大。」

Write a report on each book

questions.explain: 第三段說她瞥見時鐘，才發現自己連續讀了兩小時都沒碰手機，接著說她對故事的喜愛回來了，故選 (A)。(D) 那疊書是第一段提到的、她原本沒讀的書，不是新買的。

questions.stem: The word "halt" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 後一句說她「持續讀下去」，到年底讀完十二本書，可知 did not halt 是「沒有停止」，halt 意思是 stop，故選 (D)。(A) grow 不能和後文「繼續讀下去」形成對照。

questions.stem: What does the founder mean by comparing a reading habit to a plant?
options: Reading books about plants is good for you.

questions.explain: 發起人說給植物肥沃的土壤和一點時間，它自己就會長大，用來比喻只要有適當的環境與時間，閱讀習慣就會自然養成，故選 (C)。(A)、(B) 只照字面理解「植物」，沒有看出這是比喻。
