vocab.stem: Mom was ______ when she found out that I had lied to her.
vocab.explain: 媽媽發現我對她說謊時「非常生氣」，故選 furious。fertile（肥沃的）、flexible（有彈性的）、functional（實用的）都不能形容人發現被騙時的情緒。

vocab.stem: This machine can ______ coffee beans into a fine powder.
vocab.explain: 這台機器可以把咖啡豆「磨」成細粉，grind A into B 是常見用法，故選 grind。flatter（奉承）、flush（沖洗；臉紅）、halt（停止）都不能把豆子變成粉。

title: A Summer Among the Machines
paragraphs: Yu-ting has always been [[keen|L4-0570]] on fixing things. Last summer, the 17-year-old got the chance to work as an intern at a small bicycle [[manufacturer|L4-0615]] near her home. Her [[initial|L4-0531]] feeling was fear. Rows of loud [[machinery|L4-0609]] filled the huge room, and every worker seemed to know exactly what to do.

Her [[instructor|L4-0542]], Mr. Ko, handed her a thick [[manual|L4-0613]] and told her to read it before touching any [[equipment|L4-0357]]. "Safety is [[essential|L4-0359]] here," he said. "Last year, a new worker caused a small [[incident|L4-0521]] when he skipped a step. A machine stopped, and the whole line had to wait for hours."

Over the next few weeks, Yu-ting learned how bicycles are [[manufactured|L4-0614]]. Machines cut and shape the metal, but much of the work is still careful [[labor|L4-0574]] by hand. Every part must fit perfectly, so there is little [[margin|L4-0617]] for error. Even the weather matters. When the [[humidity|L4-0496]] is high, the paint dries slowly, and workers have to [[adjust|L4-0021]] their plans.

Near the end of the summer, the company was getting ready to [[launch|L4-0580]] a new bike for students, and Mr. Ko asked for Yu-ting's [[input|L4-0534]]. She suggested a small basket that could fold flat when it was not in use. To her surprise, the designers liked the idea. "You don't have to be a [[professional|L4-0772]] to have a good idea," Mr. Ko told her. "You just have to pay attention." Yu-ting went home that day knowing what she wanted to study in college.
zh: 郁婷一向熱衷於修理東西。去年夏天，這位十七歲的女孩得到一個機會，到家附近一家小型自行車製造商當實習生。她一開始的感覺是害怕：一排排轟隆作響的機械設備擺滿了偌大的廠房，每位員工似乎都清楚知道自己該做什麼。
她的指導老師柯先生遞給她一本厚厚的操作手冊，要她在碰任何設備之前先讀完。他說：「安全在這裡是最基本的。去年有個新進員工跳過了一個步驟，結果引發了一起小事故：一台機器停擺，整條生產線等了好幾個小時。」
接下來幾個星期，郁婷學到了自行車是怎麼製造出來的。機器負責切割金屬、塑造外形，但很多工作仍然是細心的手工勞動。每個零件都必須完全吻合，所以幾乎沒有出錯的餘地。就連天氣都有影響：濕度高的時候，油漆乾得很慢，工人就得調整工作計畫。
暑假快結束時，公司正準備推出一款給學生騎的新車，柯先生問了郁婷的意見。她建議加一個不用時可以摺平的小籃子。讓她意外的是，設計師們很喜歡這個點子。柯先生對她說：「不必是專業人士也能有好點子，只要用心觀察就行了。」那天郁婷回家時，已經知道自己上大學想讀什麼了。

questions.stem: What did Mr. Ko ask Yu-ting to do before touching any equipment?
options: Watch a video about the factory
questions.explain: 第二段說柯先生遞給郁婷一本厚厚的操作手冊，要她在碰任何設備之前先讀完，故選 (B)。(C) 設計師是到第四段才出現，而且是在討論新車款時，並不是碰設備前要做的事。
questions.evidence: handed her a thick manual and told her to read it before touching any equipment

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, why do workers sometimes have to adjust their plans?
options: Some workers do not read the manual.
Paint dries slowly when the air is very wet.
The metal is too hard to cut by hand.
questions.explain: 第三段說濕度高時油漆乾得慢，工人就得調整計畫，故選 (C)。humidity 指空氣中的濕度，也就是 the air is very wet。(A) 機器停擺是第二段柯先生提到的去年事故，和調整計畫無關。
questions.evidence: When the humidity is high, the paint dries slowly, and workers have to adjust their plans.

questions.stem: The word "input" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 柯先生問了郁婷的 input，她接著就提出加裝可摺疊籃子的建議，可知 input 在此指「意見、想法」，故選 (A)。(B)、(C) 文中郁婷並沒有提供金錢或工具。
questions.evidence: Mr. Ko asked for Yu-ting's input

questions.stem: What can we infer about Yu-ting at the end of the passage?
options: She decided never to work in a factory again.
She was angry that no one used her idea.
She wanted to become Mr. Ko's instructor.
The internship helped her choose what to study.
questions.explain: 最後一句說郁婷回家時「已經知道上大學想讀什麼」，可推知這次實習幫助她確定了未來方向，故選 (D)。(B) 與文意相反，設計師們很喜歡她的點子。
questions.evidence: Yu-ting went home that day knowing what she wanted to study in college.

vocab.stem: From the top of the mountain, we had a ______ view of the whole city and the sea beyond it.
vocab.explain: 從山頂可以看到整座城市和遠方大海，是「壯麗的」景色，故選 magnificent。keen（熱衷的；敏銳的）、manual（手動的）、initial（最初的）都不能用來形容這樣的景色。

vocab.stem: You need a driver's ______ before you can drive a car on the road.
vocab.explain: 開車上路前需要駕駛「執照」，driver's license 是固定說法，故選 license。luxury（奢侈品）、humidity（濕度）、idiom（成語、慣用語）都和開車資格無關。

title: Stop Rereading, Start Testing
paragraphs: Many students [[memorize|L4-0626]] new words by reading them again and again. It feels like hard work, so it must be useful, right? Not always. Scientists who study the brain have found that [[merely|L4-0629]] reading something many times is not the best way to keep it in your head.

In the 1880s, a [[researcher|L4-0838]] named Hermann Ebbinghaus tested his own memory. He learned lists of made-up words and checked how many he could [[recall|L4-0803]] later. The [[outcome|L4-0698]] was surprising: he forgot much of what he had learned within a day. However, each time he reviewed a list, he forgot it more slowly.

Today, there is strong [[evidence|L4-0366]] for two simple tips. First, test yourself instead of just reading your notes. Cover the answers and try to remember them. Even when you fail, the effort helps your brain build stronger memories. Second, spread out your study time. Ten minutes a day for a week works better than one long night before a test. Your brain also keeps working [[overnight|L4-0704]], sorting and storing what you learned during the day.

Of course, there are [[obstacles|L4-0682]]. Getting answers wrong can make you feel [[miserable|L4-0643]], and many students give up. To [[overcome|L4-0702]] this, remember that a [[mild|L4-0634]] feeling of difficulty is a good sign: it means your brain is working hard. Set a [[modest|L4-0648]] [[objective|L4-0680]], such as ten new words a day, and [[monitor|L4-0650]] your progress. Watching yourself improve will [[motivate|L4-0653]] you to keep going.
zh: 許多學生背新單字的方法是一遍又一遍地讀。這感覺很費力，所以一定很有用，對吧？不一定。研究大腦的科學家發現，單純把東西讀很多遍，並不是把它記在腦中的最好方法。
1880 年代，一位名叫赫爾曼・艾賓豪斯的研究者拿自己的記憶做測試。他背下一串串自己編出來的字，再檢查之後能回想起多少。結果令人意外：他學過的東西有很大一部分在一天之內就忘了。不過，他每複習一次，遺忘的速度就變慢一些。
如今，有充分的證據支持兩個簡單的訣竅。第一，考自己，而不只是讀筆記。把答案遮起來，試著回想。就算想不起來，這份努力也能幫助大腦建立更牢固的記憶。第二，把讀書時間分散開來。一週內每天讀十分鐘，效果勝過考前熬一整晚。你的大腦在夜裡也會持續運作，整理並儲存你白天學到的東西。
當然，過程中會有障礙。答錯題目可能讓人覺得很挫折，許多學生因此放棄。要克服這一點，請記得：輕微的吃力感是個好跡象，代表你的大腦正在努力運作。設定一個不太大的目標，例如一天十個新單字，並追蹤自己的進度。看見自己進步，就會激勵你繼續努力下去。

glosses.zh: 赫爾曼・艾賓豪斯（德國心理學家）

questions.stem: What did Ebbinghaus find out from testing his own memory?
options: He could remember made-up words better than real ones.
He forgot much of what he learned within a day.
Reviewing the lists made him forget faster.
Sleep did not help him remember anything.
questions.explain: 第二段說實驗結果令人意外：他學過的東西很多在一天之內就忘了，故選 (B)。(C) 與文意相反，他每複習一次，遺忘的速度就變慢。
questions.evidence: he forgot much of what he had learned within a day

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, which study plan works better?
options: Studying ten minutes a day for a week
Studying all night before a test
Reading your notes many times in one day
Studying only when you feel motivated
questions.explain: 第三段說一週內每天讀十分鐘，效果勝過考前熬一整晚，故選 (A)。(C) 正是第一段說「不是最好方法」的反覆閱讀。
questions.evidence: Ten minutes a day for a week works better than one long night before a test.

questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does "it" in "it means your brain is working hard" refer to?
questions.explain: it 指的是同一句前面提到的 a mild feeling of difficulty（輕微的吃力感）；作者說這種感覺是好跡象，代表大腦正在努力，故選 (C)。(B) 設定目標是下一句才提到的建議。
questions.evidence: remember that a mild feeling of difficulty is a good sign: it means your brain is working hard

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why students feel miserable before tests
The life story of a famous researcher
How much sleep students need every night
Better ways to remember what you study
questions.explain: 全文先指出反覆閱讀不是最好的記憶方法，再用艾賓豪斯的實驗說明遺忘與複習，最後提出考自己、分散練習等建議，主旨是更有效的記憶方法，故選 (D)。(B) 艾賓豪斯只是第二段的例子，不是全文重點。
questions.evidence: merely reading something many times is not the best way to keep it in your head

vocab.stem: The weather in this town is ______ all year round; it is never too hot or too cold.
vocab.explain: 「從不太熱也不太冷」說明天氣是「溫和的」，故選 mild。mere（僅僅的）只能放在名詞前，mysterious（神祕的）、modest（謙虛的；不大的）都不用來形容氣候。

vocab.stem: The two companies ______ for hours before they finally agreed on a price.
vocab.explain: 兩家公司「協商」了好幾個小時才終於談定價格，故選 negotiated。memorize（背誦）、overthrow（推翻）、motivate（激勵）都需要受詞，放在這裡文意也不通。

title: Why Your Basket Is Always Full
paragraphs: Have you ever gone into a supermarket for one thing and come out with a bag full of snacks? You are not alone. Stores use [[psychology|L4-0787]] to get [[consumers|L4-0199]] to spend more, and the tricks start the moment you walk in.

Designing a store is a [[profession|L4-0771]] of its own, and every detail has a purpose. The [[prime|L4-0763]] spots are on shelves at eye level, so stores often put the products they most want to sell there. Cheaper choices are usually placed higher or lower. Basic [[goods|L4-0451]] like milk and eggs are often at the back of the store. To reach them, you have to walk past many other items, and some of them end up in your basket.

Next, listen. Many stores play slow music. Some [[published|L4-0790]] studies suggest that when music has a slow [[pace|L4-0707]], customers walk more slowly, and the longer they stay, the more they may buy. [[Promotions|L4-0776]] such as "Buy one, get one free" or "30 [[percent|L4-0721]] off" also work well. Even a small [[percentage|L4-0722]] off can make people feel they are getting a deal.

Advertising plays a part, too. Ads often [[portray|L4-0749]] products as the key to a happier life. Online stores go even further: they record everything you buy and use it to make [[predictions|L4-0756]] about what you will want next. This helps them sell more, but it also raises questions about [[privacy|L4-0766]]. So before you [[proceed|L4-0769]] to the [[counter|L4-0227]] to pay, stop and ask yourself: Did I really plan to buy this?
zh: 你是否曾經只是走進超市買一樣東西，出來時卻提著一整袋零食？你不是唯一這樣的人。商店會運用心理學讓消費者花更多錢，而這些手法從你踏進店門的那一刻就開始了。
設計賣場本身就是一門專業，每個細節都有用意。黃金位置是與視線同高的貨架，所以商店常把最想賣的商品擺在那裡；比較便宜的選擇通常放在較高或較低的地方。牛奶、雞蛋這類基本商品常放在賣場最裡面。為了拿到它們，你得走過許多其他商品，其中有些最後就進了你的購物籃。
接著，仔細聽。許多商店會播放慢節奏的音樂。一些已發表的研究指出，音樂節奏慢的時候，顧客走路也會變慢，而停留得越久，可能就買得越多。「買一送一」或「七折」這類促銷活動也很有效。即使只是打一點點折扣，也能讓人覺得自己撿到了便宜。
廣告也有它的作用。廣告常把商品描繪成通往更快樂生活的關鍵。網路商店更進一步：他們會記錄你買過的每樣東西，並用這些資料預測你接下來會想要什麼。這幫助他們賣出更多東西，卻也引發了隱私方面的疑慮。所以，在你走到櫃台結帳之前，先停下來問問自己：我真的有打算買這個嗎？

questions.stem: Where do stores often put the products they most want to sell?
options: Near the door of the store
At the back of the store
questions.explain: 第二段說黃金位置是與視線同高的貨架，商店常把最想賣的商品放在那裡，故選 (B)。(C) 賣場最裡面放的是牛奶、雞蛋等基本商品；(D) 較高或較低的位置放的是比較便宜的選擇。
questions.evidence: The prime spots are on shelves at eye level, so stores often put the products they most want to sell there.

questions.stem: Why are milk and eggs often placed at the back of the store?
options: They need to be kept in a cold place.
Shoppers have to walk past many other items to reach them.
They are cheaper than other products.
Stores do not want to sell them.
questions.explain: 第二段說為了拿到牛奶和雞蛋，顧客得走過許多其他商品，其中有些就被放進購物籃，故選 (B)。(A) 保冷的理由文中完全沒有提到，屬於無中生有。
questions.evidence: To reach them, you have to walk past many other items, and some of them end up in your basket.

questions.stem: The word "portray" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 廣告把商品 portray 成通往更快樂生活的關鍵，意思是把商品「描繪、呈現」成某種樣子，故選 (A)。(D) 隱藏、遮蓋與廣告想讓人看見商品的目的相反。
questions.evidence: Ads often portray products as the key to a happier life.

questions.stem: Which of the following would the writer most likely agree with?
options: Shoppers should only buy things on sale.
Online stores should not have member programs.
Shoppers should think carefully before they pay.
Slow music should not be played in stores.
questions.explain: 作者在文末建議結帳前先停下來問自己「我真的有打算買這個嗎」，可推知作者認為購物者付錢前應該想清楚，故選 (C)。(A) 作者反而提醒，打折促銷正是讓人多買的手法之一。
questions.evidence: stop and ask yourself: Did I really plan to buy this?

vocab.stem: The farmer used no chemicals to fight the ______ that were eating his vegetables.
vocab.explain: 會吃掉蔬菜、農夫要對付的是「害蟲」，故選 pests。panels（面板；小組）、penalties（處罰）、philosophies（哲學）都不會吃蔬菜。

vocab.stem: A large company plans to ______ her first novel next spring.
vocab.explain: 公司打算明年春天「出版」她的第一本小說，故選 publish。protest（抗議）、proceed（進行）、parachute（跳傘）放在這裡都不合文意，proceed 也不能直接接受詞。

title: The Coin in the Dumpling
paragraphs: Every Chinese New Year's Eve, three [[generations|L4-0439]] of the Huang family gather at Grandma's house for a [[reunion|L4-0853]] dinner. It is the biggest [[celebration|L4-0129]] of their year. This time, however, sixteen-year-old Jia-yi was [[reluctant|L4-0828]] to go. She had a big test after the holiday and did not want to [[spare|L4-0903]] a whole evening. "Just come," her mother said. "Grandma would be sad [[otherwise|L4-0697]]."

Grandma's [[signature|L4-0890]] dish was dumplings, and every year she hid one coin inside a single dumpling. Whoever found it would have good luck all year. Jia-yi's job was to [[scoop|L4-0875]] the meat onto each dumpling skin. When her little cousin dropped a dumpling on the floor, Jia-yi expected Grandma to [[scold|L4-0874]] him, but Grandma only laughed. "One dumpling won't [[ruin|L4-0866]] the New Year," she said.

During dinner, Jia-yi's uncle told the story behind the coin. Many years ago, the family [[endured|L4-0348]] hard times, and Grandma made great [[sacrifices|L4-0869]] so that her children could stay in school. The coin was her way of saying, "Better days will come." Jia-yi had never understood the [[significance|L4-0891]] of the tradition before. Something in her heart [[shifted|L4-0888]].

Then Jia-yi bit into a dumpling and felt something hard. It was the coin! Everyone cheered. Grandma looked at her with great [[sincerity|L4-0892]] and said, "Study hard, but don't forget your family." Jia-yi gave a [[slight|L4-0897]] smile and nodded. It had been a [[remarkable|L4-0830]] evening, and she was glad she had come.
zh: 每年除夕，黃家祖孫三代都會聚到奶奶家吃團圓飯，這是他們一年之中最盛大的慶祝活動。不過這一次，十六歲的佳儀並不太想去。年假過後她有一場大考，不想空出一整個晚上。媽媽說：「來就對了，不然奶奶會難過的。」
奶奶的招牌菜是水餃，每年她都會把一枚硬幣包進其中一顆水餃裡，誰吃到了，整年都會有好運。佳儀負責把肉餡舀到每一張水餃皮上。小表弟把一顆水餃掉到地上時，佳儀以為奶奶會罵他，沒想到奶奶只是笑著說：「一顆水餃不會毀了這個年的。」
吃飯時，佳儀的伯伯說起了這枚硬幣背後的故事。很多年前，家裡熬過了一段苦日子，奶奶做了很大的犧牲，讓孩子們能繼續上學。這枚硬幣是她在說：「好日子會來的。」佳儀以前從不明白這個傳統的意義，此刻，她心裡有些東西悄悄改變了。
接著，佳儀咬下一顆水餃，咬到了硬硬的東西──是那枚硬幣！大家都歡呼起來。奶奶誠懇地看著她說：「書要好好讀，但別忘了家人。」佳儀微微一笑，點了點頭。這是一個不平凡的夜晚，她很慶幸自己來了。

questions.stem: Why was Jia-yi reluctant to go to Grandma's house at first?
options: She did not like eating dumplings.
She had a big test after the holiday.
She had to work an evening shift.
She was angry with her little cousin.
questions.explain: 第一段說佳儀年假過後有一場大考，不想空出一整個晚上，所以不太想去，故選 (B)。(D) 表弟掉水餃是到了奶奶家之後才發生的事，而且文中沒說佳儀生他的氣。
questions.evidence: She had a big test after the holiday and did not want to spare a whole evening.

questions.stem: What did Grandma do when Jia-yi's cousin dropped a dumpling?
options: She scolded him in front of everyone.
She asked Jia-yi to make a new one.
She hid the coin in another dumpling.
questions.explain: 第二段說佳儀以為奶奶會罵表弟，但奶奶只是笑著說一顆水餃不會毀了這個年，故選 (C)。(A) 罵人只是佳儀原本的預期，並沒有真的發生。
questions.evidence: Jia-yi expected Grandma to scold him, but Grandma only laughed.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, the sentence "Something in her heart shifted" means that Jia-yi ______.
options: started to feel differently about the tradition
felt sick after eating too much
wanted to leave the dinner early
questions.explain: 前一句說佳儀以前從不明白這個傳統的意義，聽完硬幣的故事後「心裡有些東西改變了」，指她對傳統的看法和感受改變了，故選 (A)。(C) 與後文她很慶幸自己來了的心情相反。
questions.evidence: Jia-yi had never understood the significance of the tradition before.

questions.stem: What does the coin most likely mean to Grandma?
options: A way to make the children study harder
Hope that better days will come
A prize for the best cook in the family
Money she saved for the New Year
questions.explain: 第三段說奶奶在家裡辛苦的年代做了很多犧牲，而這枚硬幣是她在說「好日子會來的」，可推知硬幣代表對未來的希望，故選 (B)。(C) 硬幣是給吃到的人帶來好運，和廚藝無關。
questions.evidence: The coin was her way of saying, "Better days will come."

vocab.stem: When her school offered a chance to study in Japan for a year, Lily ______ it right away.
vocab.explain: 學校提供到日本留學一年的機會，莉莉馬上「把握、抓住」了它，seize a chance 是常見搭配，故選 seized。scold（責罵）、scoop（舀）、spark（引發）都不能搭配 chance 表示把握機會。

vocab.stem: Please put your ______ at the bottom of the form before you hand it in.
vocab.explain: 交表格之前要在最下方「簽名」，故選 signature。revenge（報復）、reunion（團聚）、resistance（抵抗）都不是會寫在表格上的東西。

title: Dancing Lights in the Polar Sky
paragraphs: Imagine standing in the snow on a dark winter night when the sky begins to glow. Waves of green light [[shift|L4-0888]] and dance above you, sometimes with touches of pink and purple. For thousands of years, people in the far north have looked up at this [[magnificent|L4-0611]] sight, known as the northern lights.

Long before science could explain them, the lights seemed [[mysterious|L4-0662]], and different cultures created their own [[legends|L4-0586]] about them. Some believed the lights were the spirits of their [[ancestors|L4-0040]]. Others saw them as a sign that trouble was coming.

Today we know the story begins on the sun. The sun is always sending out a stream of tiny pieces of matter that fly through space. Earth is protected by an invisible shield that pushes most of these pieces away, but it guides some of them toward the areas around the North and South Poles. There, they hit gases high in the air, making the gases give off light. [[Oxygen|L4-0706]] produces green and red light, while nitrogen adds blue and purple.

Seeing the lights takes planning and some luck. The best places are far north, such as Norway, Iceland, Canada, and Alaska, where winter nights are long and dark. Visitors often [[pursue|L4-0792]] clear skies, driving for hours to escape clouds, and they must be willing to [[sacrifice|L4-0869]] sleep, since the lights usually appear late at night. Scientists can make [[predictions|L4-0756]] a few days ahead by [[monitoring|L4-0650]] activity on the sun, but nothing is certain. Some travelers wait a week and catch only a [[glimpse|L4-0448]]; others see the whole sky light up on their first night.

The lights have also [[sparked|L4-0904]] a rise in travel, helping small towns in the far north become more [[prosperous|L4-0782]]. Yet for many visitors, the experience means more than a beautiful photo. Standing under the [[remarkable|L4-0830]] lights, they feel a [[genuine|L4-0442]] sense of wonder and are reminded how [[gigantic|L4-0445]] and powerful nature is.
zh: 想像一下，在一個漆黑的冬夜裡，你站在雪地上，天空忽然開始發光。一道道綠色的光波在你頭頂上變換、舞動，有時還帶著些許粉紅與紫色。數千年來，住在遙遠北方的人們一直仰望著這幅壯麗的景象，也就是所謂的北極光。
在科學能夠解釋之前，極光看起來十分神祕，不同的文化也各自創造了關於它的傳說。有些人相信極光是祖先的靈魂；也有人把它視為災禍即將來臨的徵兆。
如今我們知道，這個故事是從太陽開始的。太陽不斷向外送出一股由微小物質組成的粒子流，飛越太空。地球受到一道看不見的防護罩保護，大部分的粒子都被推開，但有一些會被導引到南北極周圍的地區。在那裡，它們撞上高空中的氣體，使氣體發出光芒。氧會發出綠光和紅光，氮則增添藍色與紫色。
想看到極光，需要事先規劃，也需要一點運氣。最好的地點在遙遠的北方，例如挪威、冰島、加拿大和阿拉斯加，那裡的冬夜漫長而黑暗。遊客常常得追逐晴朗的天空，開好幾個小時的車躲開雲層，而且必須願意犧牲睡眠，因為極光通常在深夜出現。科學家可以藉由監測太陽活動，提前幾天做出預測，但一切都沒有保證。有些旅客等了一個星期，只匆匆瞥見一眼；也有人第一晚就看見整片天空亮了起來。
北極光也帶動了旅遊人潮，幫助遙遠北方的小鎮變得更加繁榮。然而，對許多遊客來說，這段經歷的意義遠不只是一張美麗的照片。站在這片非凡的光芒之下，他們感受到發自內心的驚嘆，也再次體會到大自然是多麼巨大而強大。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why people in the north stopped believing old legends
How to take beautiful photos of the night sky
What the northern lights are, how they form, and how people experience them
Why traveling to the far north has become too expensive

vocab.explain: 因為「限水措施」，市民不能洗車也不能把泳池注滿水，water restrictions 指用水限制，故選 restrictions。quotations（引文；報價）、receptions（接待；歡迎會）、signatures（簽名）都無法說明為何不能用水。

title: Making Room for the Leopard Cat
paragraphs: In the hills of central Taiwan lives a wild cat about the size of a house cat. It has spots on its body and two white lines on its face. This is the leopard cat, the last wild cat [[species|L4-0906]] still living in Taiwan. Leopard cats are [[suspicious|L4-0930]] of humans and are rarely seen. Sadly, they are also [[endangered|L4-0347]].

One of the biggest dangers is roads. Leopard cats are most active at night, and they have a [[tendency|L4-0940]] to cross roads while looking for food. As [[transportation|L4-0964]] in [[rural|L4-0867]] areas has grown, more cars travel these roads, and many cats are killed in [[tragic|L4-0958]] accidents. Some cats also die after eating rats that farmers have poisoned. These deaths are [[accidental|L4-0009]], but they still hurt the cats' numbers.

Leopard cats sometimes eat farmers' chickens, so in the past, some farmers would not [[tolerate|L4-0953]] them. Today, government [[agencies|L4-0026]], [[volunteers|L4-0988]], and local [[communities|L4-0163]] [[strive|L4-0920]] to change this. They help farmers build stronger fences to keep their chickens safe, and they put up road signs that tell drivers to slow down. Some farmers have even stopped using poison and now grow rice in fields where leopard cats are welcome.

The work is not easy, and the leopard cat is not safe yet. But every farmer who becomes more [[tolerant|L4-0952]] and every driver who slows down is a small [[triumph|L4-0968]]. These efforts are [[admirable|L4-0022]], and they show that people and wild animals can share the land.
zh: 在台灣中部的山丘上，住著一種體型和家貓差不多的野生貓科動物。牠身上有斑點，臉上有兩條白線。這就是石虎，台灣僅存的野生貓科物種。石虎對人類充滿戒心，很少被人看見。可惜的是，牠們也瀕臨絕種。
最大的威脅之一是道路。石虎大多在夜間活動，牠們出外覓食時常會穿越馬路。隨著鄉村地區的交通越來越發達，行經這些道路的車輛變多，許多石虎在令人難過的車禍中喪命。也有些石虎吃了被農民下毒的老鼠而死亡。這些死亡雖然是意外，卻仍讓石虎的數量減少。
石虎有時會吃農民養的雞，所以過去有些農民無法容忍牠們。如今，政府機關、志工和地方社區都努力改變這種情況。他們幫農民蓋更堅固的圍籬來保護雞隻，也設立路標提醒駕駛人減速。有些農民甚至不再用毒，改在歡迎石虎出沒的田裡種稻。
這項工作並不容易，石虎也還沒有脫離險境。但每一位變得更包容的農民、每一位願意減速的駕駛人，都是一次小小的勝利。這些努力令人敬佩，也證明了人類和野生動物可以共享這片土地。

They are attracted by the lights of cars.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, what do people do to help leopard cats?

vocab.explain: 主角失去家人、觀眾哭成一片，表示這是「悲慘的」結局，故選 tragic。tolerable（可忍受的）、universal（普遍的）、suspicious（可疑的）都無法說明觀眾為何落淚。

title: Visitor Guide: Harbor Art Museum
paragraphs: Welcome to the Harbor Art Museum! Our museum is in an old train station, and you will enter through its famous stone [[arch|L4-0054]]. Inside, three floors of [[artistic|L4-0058]] treasures [[await|L4-0081]] you, from old pots to modern paintings. Every work on display is [[authentic|L4-0077]]; we do not show copies. [[Admission|L4-0024]] is free for students.

Before You Begin: Pick up a free [[audio|L4-0076]] guide at the front desk. It tells the story behind each work in Chinese, English, and Japanese. Elevators give easy [[access|L4-0008]] to every floor. If you need [[assistance|L4-0065]], look for staff members in green shirts. Please keep your voice at an [[appropriate|L4-0051]] level. Photos without flash are welcome in most rooms, but filming requires [[approval|L4-0052]] from the front desk.

Special Events This Month: Our new [[exhibit|L4-0371]], Faces of the Sea, opens on May 1. On Saturday, May 10, at 2 p.m., painter Lin Mei-hua will talk about her new [[autobiography|L4-0079]], My Life in Color. After the talk, she will sign [[autographs|L4-0080]] for visitors. Every Sunday morning, children aged 8 to 12 can join our Little Artists class, where they learn to [[analyze|L4-0039]] paintings by looking closely at color and shape. Families should [[assemble|L4-0062]] at the arch at 9:50 a.m.
We hope you enjoy your visit and leave with a deeper [[appreciation|L4-0050]] of art. The museum is open Tuesday to Sunday, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
zh: 歡迎來到海港美術館！本館位於一座老火車站內，您將從著名的石造拱門進入。館內三層樓的藝術珍品正等著您，從古老的陶罐到現代畫作應有盡有。所有展出的作品都是真跡，我們不展示複製品。學生免費入場。
參觀之前：請到服務台領取免費的語音導覽機，它會以中文、英文和日文介紹每件作品背後的故事。電梯可以方便地通往每一層樓。如需協助，請找穿綠色上衣的工作人員。請將說話音量保持在適當的程度。大部分展間歡迎拍照（請勿使用閃光燈），但錄影須先經服務台同意。
本月特別活動：新展覽「海洋的面孔」於 5 月 1 日開幕。5 月 10 日星期六下午 2 點，畫家林美華將暢談她的新自傳《我的彩色人生》，講座結束後將為觀眾簽名。每週日上午，8 到 12 歲的兒童可以參加「小小藝術家」課程，學習仔細觀察顏色與形狀來分析畫作。請家庭於上午 9:50 在拱門集合。
希望您參觀愉快，離開時對藝術有更深一層的欣賞。本館開放時間為星期二至星期日，上午 9 點到下午 5 點。

title: Tears in the Kitchen
paragraphs: From soups in France to noodles in China, onions are used in kitchens all over the world. They are a basic [[ingredient|L4-0530]] in many dishes, and cooks [[cherish|L4-0135]] them for the rich, sweet taste they add to almost any [[recipe|L4-0805]]. Yet anyone who has cut one knows the problem: soon, your eyes begin to hurt and tears run down your face.

The answer lies in [[chemistry|L4-0134]] and [[biology|L4-0094]]. An onion is made of many tiny cells. Inside each cell, certain chemicals are kept apart. When a knife cuts through the cells, these chemicals mix and form a gas. The air acts as a [[carrier|L4-0124]], bringing the gas up to your eyes. Your eyes have an amazing [[capacity|L4-0120]] to protect themselves. They [[identify|L4-0502]] the gas as a danger, so you [[blink|L4-0098]] quickly, and your body makes tears to wash the gas away. In this way, tears work as a natural [[barrier|L4-0087]].

Is there a [[remedy|L4-0831]]? Here are a few tips. First, put the onion in the fridge for half an hour, or leave it in a [[basin|L4-0088]] of cold water for a few minutes. Cold slows down the chemicals, so less gas is formed. Second, use a sharp knife, which breaks fewer cells than a dull one. Some people even wear special glasses sold in kitchen [[catalogues|L4-0126]].
Most importantly, be careful. It is hard to see clearly through tears, and one wrong move with the knife could mean you need a [[bandage|L4-0084]]. Take your time and enjoy cooking.
zh: 從法國的湯到中國的麵，世界各地的廚房都會用到洋蔥。它是無數料理中的基本食材，廚師們很珍惜它，因為它幾乎能為任何食譜增添濃郁香甜的滋味。然而，每個切過洋蔥的人都知道這個問題：沒多久，眼睛就開始刺痛，眼淚直流。
答案就藏在化學和生物學裡。洋蔥由許多微小的細胞組成，每個細胞裡都有某些化學物質被分隔開來。當刀子切開細胞時，這些物質混在一起，形成一種氣體。空氣就像運送者，把這種氣體帶到你的眼睛。你的眼睛有驚人的自我保護能力：它們把這種氣體辨識為危險，於是你會快速眨眼，身體也會分泌眼淚把氣體沖掉。如此一來，眼淚就成了一道天然的屏障。
有沒有解決的辦法呢？這裡有幾個訣竅。第一，把洋蔥放進冰箱半小時，或泡在一盆冷水裡幾分鐘。低溫會減緩化學物質的作用，產生的氣體就會變少。第二，用鋒利的刀子，因為它切破的細胞比鈍刀少。有些人甚至會戴上廚房用品型錄裡賣的特殊眼鏡。
最重要的是要小心。眼淚會讓人看不清楚，手中的刀子一個不小心，你可能就需要一片繃帶了。慢慢來，享受下廚的樂趣吧。

questions.stem: What happens when a knife cuts through the cells of an onion?
options: Chemicals inside the cells mix and form a gas.
The cells fill with cold water.
The onion loses all its taste.
questions.explain: 第二段說刀子切開細胞時，原本分開存放的化學物質混在一起，形成一種氣體，故選 (B)。(A) 洋蔥的甜味是第一段提到它為料理增添的味道，與切開細胞的變化無關。
questions.evidence: When a knife cuts through the cells, these chemicals mix and form a gas.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way to cry less?
options: Keeping the onion cold before cutting it
questions.explain: 第三段提到的方法有：先冰洋蔥或泡冷水、用鋒利的刀、戴特殊眼鏡，並沒有提到「切快一點」，故選 (C)。作者在第四段反而提醒要慢慢來，以免切到手。
questions.evidence: First, put the onion in the fridge for half an hour, or leave it in a basin of cold water for a few minutes.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2, the word "barrier" is closest in meaning to ______.
options: something that is easy to break
questions.explain: 眼淚把刺激的氣體沖掉、保護眼睛，所以 barrier 指能「阻擋傷害的屏障」，故選 (A)。(D) 容易破的東西無法發揮保護作用，不合文意。
questions.evidence: In this way, tears work as a natural barrier.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To teach readers how to cook French onion soup
To compare onions from different countries
To warn readers never to cut onions at home
To explain why cutting onions makes us cry and how to cry less
questions.explain: 文章先指出切洋蔥會流淚，接著用化學與生物說明原因，再提供減少流淚的訣竅，目的是解釋原因並提供方法，故選 (D)。(C) 作者只是提醒要小心，並沒有叫人不要切洋蔥，最後還說要享受下廚的樂趣。
questions.evidence: Is there a remedy? Here are a few tips.

vocab.stem: Can you help me ______ how much each of us should pay for dinner?
vocab.explain: 請對方幫忙「計算」每個人晚餐該付多少錢，故選 calculate。cherish（珍惜）、blink（眨眼）、catalogue（將…編入目錄）都不能接 how much 子句表示算錢。

vocab.stem: The old man walks with a ______ because his legs are weak.
vocab.explain: 老先生腿沒力，走路要拄著「拐杖」，故選 cane。ballet（芭蕾舞）、bulletin（公告）、burglar（竊賊）都不能拿來幫助走路。

title: Your Brain on Music
paragraphs: When you listen to your favorite song, your brain does far more than hear sounds. Scientists can now watch the brain at work, and they have found that music lights up many areas at once, including those that control movement, memory, and feelings. This helps explain why we tap our feet to the [[rhythm|L4-0861]] of a song, why an old song can help us [[recall|L4-0803]] a summer from years ago, and why music can make us cry just as a [[comedy|L4-0157]] makes us laugh.

Singing with others seems to be especially good for us. Members of a [[chorus|L4-0138]] must breathe together and follow the hands of a [[conductor|L4-0177]]. Studies have found that singing in a group can [[relieve|L4-0827]] stress and make people feel closer to each other. Many people who join a chorus find not only music but also lifelong [[companions|L4-0164]].

Learning to play music may also train the brain. Children who practice an instrument in a [[consistent|L4-0190]] way often become better at hearing small differences between sounds, and this skill may help them learn languages. Performing on stage can build [[confidence|L4-0180]], too. Even great [[composers|L4-0170]] needed years of practice before they could write their famous [[compositions|L4-0171]].

Still, many questions remain. At [[conferences|L4-0178]] around the world, [[psychologists|L4-0786]] and brain scientists share ideas as they try to [[clarify|L4-0145]] exactly how music changes the brain and why so many people enjoy it. One thing is clear, though: music is far more than background noise.
zh: 當你聽著最喜歡的歌，大腦所做的遠遠不只是聽見聲音。科學家現在能觀察大腦運作的情形，他們發現音樂會同時點亮大腦的許多區域，包括掌管動作、記憶和情緒的區域。這有助於解釋為什麼我們會跟著歌曲的節奏打拍子，為什麼一首老歌能幫我們想起多年前的某個夏天，以及為什麼音樂能讓我們落淚，就像喜劇能讓我們發笑一樣。
和別人一起唱歌似乎對我們特別有益。合唱團的成員必須一起呼吸，並跟隨指揮的手勢。研究發現，團體歌唱能紓解壓力，讓人覺得彼此更親近。許多加入合唱團的人，得到的不只是音樂，還有一輩子的好夥伴。
學習演奏音樂也可能鍛鍊大腦。持之以恆練習樂器的孩子，往往更能聽出聲音之間細微的差別，而這項能力可能有助於他們學習語言。上台表演也能建立自信。即使是偉大的作曲家，也要經過多年的練習，才能寫出他們著名的作品。
不過，仍有許多問題尚待解答。心理學家和腦科學家在世界各地的研討會上交流想法，努力釐清音樂究竟如何改變大腦，以及為什麼這麼多人喜愛音樂。但有一件事是確定的：音樂絕不只是背景噪音而已。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 1, what have scientists found about the brain and music?
options: Music only affects the part of the brain that hears sounds.
Music lights up many areas of the brain at once.
The brain stops working when we hear sad songs.
Old songs make people forget the past.
questions.explain: 第一段說科學家發現音樂會同時點亮大腦的許多區域，包括掌管動作、記憶和情緒的區域，故選 (B)。(A) 正好相反，作者說大腦做的遠不只是聽見聲音；(D) 老歌是幫我們「想起」過去。
questions.evidence: music lights up many areas at once, including those that control movement, memory, and feelings

questions.stem: Which is mentioned as a benefit of singing in a group?
options: It makes people better at math.
questions.explain: 第二段說研究發現團體歌唱能紓解壓力，讓人覺得彼此更親近，故選 (A)。(B)、(C) 文中都沒有提到；(D) 指揮是合唱團成員要跟隨的對象，不是唱歌帶來的好處。
questions.evidence: singing in a group can relieve stress and make people feel closer to each other

questions.stem: In paragraph 3, the word "consistent" in "practice an instrument in a consistent way" is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: consistent 指「一致的、持續穩定的」，以 consistent 的方式練樂器，就是規律、持之以恆地練習，故選 (C)。(D) 輕鬆短暫的練習與後文「作曲家也要練多年」的意思相反。
questions.evidence: Children who practice an instrument in a consistent way often become better at hearing small differences between sounds

questions.stem: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: Scientists already know everything about music and the brain.
Only psychologists are interested in music.
Music is less important than people think.
There is still much to learn about how music affects the brain.
questions.explain: 最後一段說仍有許多問題尚待解答，科學家在研討會上交流、努力釐清音樂如何改變大腦，可推知這個領域還有很多未知，故選 (D)。(A) 與 many questions remain 相反；(C) 也與結尾「音樂遠不只是背景噪音」相反。
questions.evidence: Still, many questions remain.

vocab.stem: The teacher's example helped ______ the difficult rule, and soon everyone understood it.
vocab.explain: 老師舉例幫忙「釐清」困難的規則，大家很快就懂了，故選 clarify。confess（坦承）、conquer（征服）不合文意；classify（分類）是把東西分門別類，無法讓人理解一條規則。

vocab.stem: After winning the speech contest, Emma had more ______ when she spoke in front of others.
vocab.explain: 演講比賽得獎後，Emma 在別人面前說話時更有「自信」，故選 confidence。confusion（困惑）與得獎後的變化相反；conscience（良心）、conference（會議）都不合文意。

title: A Glass Cube Among the Cottages
paragraphs: When a small town by the sea held a [[contest|L4-0203]] to design its new library, more than fifty designers sent in their ideas. The winner was a young woman named Nora Hill. Her plan was simple but bold: a library shaped like a glass [[cube|L4-0243]], standing among the town's old stone [[cottages|L4-0225]].

Not everyone was pleased. Some people [[criticized|L4-0239]] the design, saying that a modern glass box did not fit the [[context|L4-0204]] of a quiet, old street. Others worried that a building with so much glass would [[consume|L4-0198]] too much energy in winter. The town asked a building [[consultant|L4-0197]] to study the plan, and he agreed that some of the [[criticism|L4-0238]] was fair.

Instead of losing [[confidence|L4-0180]], Nora decided to [[cooperate|L4-0217]] with the [[community|L4-0163]]. She held meetings where people could share [[constructive|L4-0195]] ideas, and she answered every question with [[courtesy|L4-0229]], even the rude ones. Then she [[adapted|L4-0018]] her plan. She added thick stone walls on the north side to keep the heat in, and she covered the roof with [[copper|L4-0221]]. Copper slowly turns green over the years, so the new roof would grow old together with the street.

Today, the library has become a local [[landmark|L4-0577]]. Children press their faces against the glass with [[curiosity|L4-0246]], and older people say the building now feels like part of the street. Nora often tells young designers, "A [[courageous|L4-0228]] idea is only the beginning. A good building must also listen to the place where it stands."
zh: 一座海邊小鎮舉辦新圖書館設計比賽時，有五十多位設計師寄來他們的構想。獲勝的是一位名叫諾拉・希爾的年輕女性。她的設計簡單卻大膽：一座立方體形狀的玻璃圖書館，矗立在鎮上古老的石造小屋之間。
並不是每個人都滿意。有些人批評這個設計，說現代感的玻璃盒子和這條寧靜古老的街道格格不入。也有人擔心，用了這麼多玻璃的建築在冬天會耗掉太多能源。鎮上請了一位建築顧問來研究這份設計，他也同意有些批評是有道理的。
諾拉沒有因此失去信心，而是決定和社區合作。她舉辦了幾場會議，讓大家分享有建設性的意見；每個問題她都很有禮貌地回答，即使是不客氣的問題也一樣。接著，她調整了設計。她在北面加上厚厚的石牆來保暖，並用銅覆蓋屋頂。銅會隨著歲月慢慢變成綠色，這樣新屋頂就能和這條街一起慢慢變老。
如今，這座圖書館已成為當地的地標。孩子們好奇地把臉貼在玻璃上，年長的居民也說，這棟建築現在感覺就像是街道的一部分。諾拉常對年輕的設計師說：「勇敢的構想只是開始。好的建築也必須傾聽它所在的地方。」

questions.stem: Why did some people criticize Nora's design at first?
options: They thought the library was too small for the town.
They felt a glass box did not match the old street.
They wanted the library to be built of copper.
They did not like the young designer's attitude.
questions.explain: 第二段說有些人批評這個設計，認為現代的玻璃盒子不符合寧靜古老街道的環境（context），故選 (B)。(C) 銅屋頂是諾拉後來自己修改設計時加上的，並不是批評者的要求。
questions.evidence: saying that a modern glass box did not fit the context of a quiet, old street

questions.stem: Which change did Nora make to her plan?
options: She made the building much smaller.
She moved the library to another street.
She replaced all the glass with stone.
She added thick walls on the north side.
questions.explain: 第三段說她在北面加上厚厚的石牆來保暖，並用銅覆蓋屋頂，故選 (D)。(C) 不對，文中只在北面加了石牆，最後的圖書館仍有玻璃，孩子們還會把臉貼在玻璃上。
questions.evidence: She added thick stone walls on the north side to keep the heat in

questions.stem: The word "constructive" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 諾拉開會是為了讓大家提出能改善設計的意見，constructive 指「有建設性的、有幫助的」，故選 (A)。後文的 even the rude ones 是說連不客氣的問題她也有禮貌地回答，並不是 constructive 的意思，所以 (B) 不對。
questions.evidence: She held meetings where people could share constructive ideas

questions.stem: What does Nora most likely mean when she says a good building must "listen to the place where it stands"?
options: A building should be quiet inside.
Designers should never try new ideas.
A building should fit the people and surroundings around it.
Libraries should be built far from old streets.
questions.explain: 諾拉聽取居民意見、讓銅屋頂隨時間變綠以融入老街，可推知她的意思是建築要配合周遭的環境與居民，故選 (C)。(B) 不對，她也說勇敢的構想是好的開始，並沒有反對新點子。
questions.evidence: A good building must also listen to the place where it stands.

vocab.stem: Fresh carrots are sweet and ______, so many children like to eat them raw.
vocab.explain: 新鮮紅蘿蔔又甜又「脆」，所以很多小孩喜歡生吃，故選 crunchy。courageous（勇敢的）、cunning（狡猾的）、continual（不斷的）都不能用來形容食物的口感。

vocab.stem: Holding the door open for the person behind you is a simple act of ______.
vocab.explain: 幫後面的人扶住門是一種簡單的「禮貌」行為，an act of courtesy 是常見說法，故選 courtesy。cord（細繩）、copper（銅）、cube（立方體）都是具體物品，不能說成一種行為。

title: Volunteering Abroad: Help or Holiday?
paragraphs: Every summer, many young people pack their bags and fly to other countries to [[volunteer|L4-0988]]. They paint schools, teach English, or help at animal centers, often through a travel [[agency|L4-0026]] that arranges everything for them. For many, it seems like the perfect trip: they see the world and do good at the same time.

In recent years, however, such trips have faced growing [[criticism|L4-0238]]. Some [[critics|L4-0236]] argue that short trips may do more for the volunteers than for the people they are supposed to help. A careful [[analysis|L4-0038]] of a typical program shows why. When a group of students with no building skills spends a week building a wall, local workers, who could have been paid for the job, lose a chance to earn money. Children at a village school may meet a new teacher every two weeks, which can lead to [[confusion|L4-0181]] rather than progress.

This does not mean that volunteering abroad is always a bad idea. The key is to choose an [[appropriate|L4-0051]] program and to [[strive|L4-0920]] to be useful rather than simply feel useful. Before signing up, volunteers should find out what the local [[community|L4-0163]] really needs and whether their own skills match those needs. A nurse who can offer medical [[assistance|L4-0065]], or an [[accountant|L4-0012]] who can help a small [[charity|L4-0133]] manage its money, may do far more good than someone who stays for a few days and takes photos. Staying longer also matters, because help that is [[consistent|L4-0190]] is worth more than help that comes and goes.

Above all, good volunteers arrive with [[curiosity|L4-0246]] and respect, ready to learn as well as to give. They [[cooperate|L4-0217]] with local people instead of taking control, and they show [[courtesy|L4-0229]] toward customs that are different from their own. A volunteer who returns home with a deeper [[appreciation|L4-0050]] of another culture and a more [[tolerant|L4-0952]] attitude toward differences has gained something far more valuable than a few holiday pictures.
zh: 每年夏天，都有許多年輕人收拾行囊，飛往其他國家當志工。他們粉刷學校、教英文，或在動物中心幫忙，而且往往是透過旅行社替他們安排好一切。對許多人來說，這似乎是完美的旅程：既能看看世界，同時又能做好事。
然而近年來，這類旅程受到越來越多的批評。有些批評者認為，短期旅程對志工本身的好處，可能比對他們原本要幫助的人還要多。仔細分析一個典型的志工計畫，就能看出原因。當一群沒有建築技能的學生花一個星期蓋一面牆時，原本可以受雇做這份工作的當地工人，就失去了賺錢的機會。村裡學校的孩子可能每兩週就要面對一位新老師，這帶來的可能是混亂，而不是進步。
這並不表示出國當志工一定是壞主意。關鍵在於選擇合適的計畫，並努力真正派上用場，而不只是覺得自己有用。報名之前，志工應該先了解當地社區真正需要什麼，以及自己的技能是否符合這些需求。一位能提供醫療協助的護理師，或一位能幫小型慈善機構管理財務的會計師，所做的好事可能遠遠超過一個只待幾天、拍拍照的人。待得久一點也很重要，因為持續穩定的幫助，比來來去去的幫助更有價值。
最重要的是，好的志工帶著好奇心與尊重而來，準備好學習，也準備好付出。他們與當地人合作，而不是一手掌控，並且以禮貌對待和自己不同的習俗。一位回國時對另一種文化有更深的體會、對差異也更加包容的志工，所得到的收穫遠比幾張度假照片珍貴得多。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why young people should never volunteer abroad
How to find a cheap travel agency
How volunteering abroad can do real good if it is done the right way
Why local workers dislike foreign volunteers
questions.explain: 文章先介紹出國當志工的熱潮，再說明短期志工受到的批評，接著指出選對計畫、真正派上用場、尊重當地，就能帶來真正的幫助，主旨是「用對方法出國當志工才有意義」，故選 (C)。(A) 太過絕對，第三段明說出國當志工並不一定是壞主意。
questions.evidence: This does not mean that volunteering abroad is always a bad idea.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why can short volunteer trips cause problems?
options: Volunteers often get sick during their trips.
Local workers may lose paid jobs, and children may face too many changes.
Travel agencies ask local people to pay too much money.
Volunteers are not allowed to take photos of their work.
questions.explain: 第二段說沒有技能的學生蓋牆，讓當地工人失去賺錢的機會；學校的孩子每兩週就換一位新老師，帶來混亂，故選 (B)。(C) 文中只說旅行社替志工安排行程，沒有提到向當地人收錢。
questions.evidence: local workers, who could have been paid for the job, lose a chance to earn money

questions.stem: Which volunteer would the writer most likely praise?
options: A student who builds a wall in one week and then leaves
A tourist who visits five schools in five days to take photos
A person who insists on doing everything in his own way
An accountant who stays for months to help a charity manage its money
questions.explain: 作者認為志工應該發揮符合當地需求的專長、待久一點並提供穩定的幫助，因此最可能稱讚留下數月幫慈善機構管理財務的會計師，故選 (D)。(C) 與第四段「與當地人合作，而不是一手掌控」相反。
questions.evidence: or an accountant who can help a small charity manage its money

questions.stem: The word "consistent" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 句中把 consistent 的幫助和「來來去去的幫助」對比，可知 consistent 是「持續穩定的」，故選 (A)。(B) quick and easy 反而比較像短暫、來去匆匆的幫助。
questions.evidence: because help that is consistent is worth more than help that comes and goes

vocab.stem: The little boy called himself a ______ because he was too afraid to jump into the pool.
vocab.explain: 小男孩太害怕而不敢跳進泳池，所以說自己是「膽小鬼」，故選 coward。copper（銅）、cube（立方體）、cottage（小屋）都不能用來稱呼人。

vocab.stem: At night, ants ______ into the kitchen and look for sugar.
vocab.explain: 晚上螞蟻會「悄悄爬進」廚房找糖，creep into 表示慢慢地、悄悄地爬進，故選 creep。criticize（批評）、cooperate（合作）、consume（消耗）都不能接 into the kitchen 表示移動。

title: The Bracelet on the Bench
paragraphs: Ten minutes before the [[departure|L4-0269]] of her train, Emma noticed something shining on the bench beside her. It was a [[delicate|L4-0261]] silver [[bracelet|L4-0104]] with a tiny [[decoration|L4-0254]] in the shape of a bird. She looked around, but the crowd on the platform was so [[dense|L4-0267]] that she could not tell who might have dropped it.

Out of [[curiosity|L4-0246]], Emma decided to play [[detective|L4-0276]]. On the back of the bird, she found two small letters: "M.L." She took out her notebook, drew a simple [[diagram|L4-0282]] of the station, and [[devised|L4-0279]] a plan: she would ask at every shop near the bench. The first two shopkeepers shook their heads. Emma felt a little [[discouraged|L4-0296]], and her train was about to leave, but her [[determination|L4-0277]] was stronger than her wish to go home.

At the third shop, a woman selling flowers smiled. "That must be May Lin. She buys roses every Friday, and she always sits on that bench." Emma wrote down her phone number and asked the woman to give it to Mrs. Lin.

A few days later, Mrs. Lin called, and on Friday Emma returned to the station. An old lady was waiting by the bench, looking nervous. When Emma held out the bracelet, the lady's eyes filled with [[delight|L4-0262]]. "My daughter gave me this," she said. "I [[cherish|L4-0135]] it more than anything I own. What a [[delightful|L4-0263]] young lady you are!" Emma had missed her train that first evening, but she did not mind at all.
zh: 火車出發前十分鐘，艾瑪注意到身旁的長椅上有個東西在發亮。那是一條精緻的銀手鍊，上面有一個小鳥形狀的小裝飾。她環顧四周，但月台上的人潮太擁擠了，她根本看不出是誰掉的。
出於好奇，艾瑪決定當一回偵探。她在小鳥的背面發現兩個小小的字母：「M.L.」。她拿出筆記本，畫了一張簡單的車站平面圖，並想出一個計畫：她要到長椅附近的每家店去問問看。前兩家店的老闆都搖搖頭。艾瑪覺得有點洩氣，她的火車也快開了，但她找到失主的決心勝過了想回家的念頭。
到了第三家店，一位賣花的婦人笑了。「那一定是林梅。她每個星期五都會來買玫瑰，而且總是坐在那張長椅上。」艾瑪寫下自己的電話號碼，請婦人轉交給林太太。
幾天後，林太太打電話來，星期五艾瑪又回到車站。一位老太太正在長椅旁等著，看起來有點緊張。當艾瑪拿出手鍊時，老太太的眼中充滿了喜悅。「這是我女兒送我的，」她說，「我把它看得比我擁有的任何東西都珍貴。你真是個討人喜歡的年輕人！」那天傍晚艾瑪錯過了她的火車，但她一點也不在意。

questions.stem: What clue did Emma find on the bracelet?
options: Two small letters on the back of the bird
A phone number written inside it
The name of a shop near the station
A picture of an old lady
questions.explain: 第二段說艾瑪在小鳥裝飾的背面發現兩個小字母「M.L.」，故選 (A)。(B) 電話號碼是艾瑪自己寫下、請賣花婦人轉交的，並不在手鍊上。
questions.evidence: On the back of the bird, she found two small letters

questions.stem: How did Emma finally find the owner of the bracelet?
options: She asked the station office for help.
She waited at the bench every day for a week.
A flower seller knew who usually sat on that bench.
She put a notice on the station wall.
questions.explain: 第三段中賣花的婦人說，林梅每週五都來買玫瑰，而且總坐在那張長椅上，艾瑪便請她轉交電話號碼，故選 (C)。(A)、(D) 文中都沒有提到。
questions.evidence: She buys roses every Friday, and she always sits on that bench.

questions.stem: The word "determination" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 艾瑪雖然有點洩氣、火車也快開了，但 determination 勝過想回家的念頭，她繼續找失主，可知這個字是「決心、堅持下去的意志」，故選 (D)。(B) 想回家的念頭正是被 determination 勝過的東西，意思相反。
questions.evidence: but her determination was stronger than her wish to go home

questions.stem: What can we infer from the last sentence of the story?
options: Emma was angry that she had to wait for the next train.
Emma felt that helping Mrs. Lin was worth missing her train.
Emma decided never to take the train again.
Emma hoped that Mrs. Lin would give her money.
questions.explain: 最後一句說艾瑪那天錯過了火車，卻一點也不在意，可推知她覺得幫林太太找回心愛的手鍊很值得，故選 (B)。(A) 與 did not mind at all 相反；(D) 文中完全沒有提到報酬。
questions.evidence: Emma had missed her train that first evening, but she did not mind at all.

vocab.stem: After the storm, the ______ of the old bridge made it impossible for cars to cross the river.
vocab.explain: 暴風雨過後，舊橋遭到「毀壞」，車子無法過河，故選 destruction。dew（露水）、diagram（圖表）、dignity（尊嚴）都不會造成車子無法過河。

vocab.stem: In the early morning, the grass in the park was wet with ______.
vocab.explain: 清晨公園的草地被「露水」沾濕，wet with dew 是常見說法，故選 dew。defense（防禦）、diploma（畢業證書）、detective（偵探）都不會讓草地變濕。

title: Messages in Knots: The Inca Empire
paragraphs: In the 1400s, the Inca [[Empire|L4-0344]] grew to [[dominate|L4-0315]] the western side of South America. From their capital high in the Andes Mountains, Inca kings [[enlarged|L4-0351]] their land again and again until it stretched for thousands of kilometers. The people believed that their king was the son of the sun god, so they saw him as [[divine|L4-0311]].

Ruling such a huge land was not easy. While many great [[civilizations|L4-0144]] [[elsewhere|L4-0339]] used writing, the Incas had no written language. Instead, they kept records with quipus: sets of colored [[cords|L4-0222]] tied with knots. The type of knot and its place on the cord showed a number. Experts believe that the colors helped people [[distinguish|L4-0303]] one kind of record from another. With quipus, officials could keep track of people, food, and goods.

The Incas also built an [[enormous|L4-0352]] system of roads across mountains, deserts, and forests. Along these [[dusty|L4-0322]] roads, the king's orders traveled quickly. A [[messenger|L4-0631]] would run a short distance to a small station, where the next runner was waiting, and pass the message on, much like a team race. In this way, officials far from the capital could [[enforce|L4-0349]] the king's laws and keep [[disorder|L4-0300]] from spreading.

Today, parts of these roads can still be walked, and visitors from around the world come to see them with great [[enthusiasm|L4-0355]]. [[Researchers|L4-0838]] are also making [[earnest|L4-0326]] efforts to read the quipus that have survived. If they succeed, these strings may one day tell us more of the Inca story.
zh: 在十五世紀，印加帝國逐漸壯大，稱霸南美洲西部。印加國王從位於安地斯山脈高處的首都出發，一次又一次擴大領土，直到國土綿延數千公里。人民相信國王是太陽神之子，因此把他視為神聖的存在。
統治這麼廣大的土地並不容易。世界其他地方的許多偉大文明都使用文字，印加人卻沒有書面文字。他們改用「奇普」來記錄：一組組打了結的彩色繩子。繩結的種類和它在繩子上的位置代表一個數字。專家認為，不同的顏色能幫助人們區分不同種類的紀錄。靠著奇普，官員就能掌握人口、糧食和物資的狀況。
印加人還修建了一套龐大的道路系統，穿越高山、沙漠和森林。國王的命令沿著這些塵土飛揚的道路迅速傳遞。信差會跑一小段路到一個小驛站，下一位跑者已在那裡等候，接著把訊息傳下去，就像一場團隊接力賽。如此一來，遠離首都的官員也能執行國王的法令，防止混亂擴散。
如今，這些道路仍有部分可以行走，來自世界各地的遊客滿懷熱情前來參觀。研究人員也正認真努力，想解讀流傳下來的奇普。如果他們成功了，這些繩子或許有一天能告訴我們更多印加人的故事。

glosses.zh: 奇普（印加人的結繩記事）

questions.stem: How did the Incas keep records?
options: By carving words into stone walls
By painting pictures along the roads
By tying knots in colored cords
questions.explain: 第二段說印加人沒有書面文字，而是用奇普記錄，也就是一組組打了結的彩色繩子，故選 (C)。(A)、(D) 都需要文字，但文中明說印加人沒有書面文字。
questions.evidence: they kept records with quipus: sets of colored cords tied with knots

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, how did messages travel across the empire?
options: Runners passed them on from one station to the next.
One runner carried each message all the way.
They were sent by boat along the coast.
Officials carried them to the capital themselves.
questions.explain: 第三段說信差跑一小段路到驛站，再交給在那裡等候的下一位跑者，像接力賽一樣，故選 (A)。(B) 與「只跑一小段路」的說法矛盾。
questions.evidence: A messenger would run a short distance to a small station, where the next runner was waiting, and pass the message on

questions.stem: In paragraph 1, what does "him" in "they saw him as divine" refer to?
questions.explain: 前半句說人民相信「國王」是太陽神之子，所以把「他」視為神聖的存在，him 指的是印加國王，故選 (D)。(A) 太陽神本來就是神，句中說的是國王因為是太陽神之子才被視為神聖。
questions.evidence: The people believed that their king was the son of the sun god, so they saw him as divine.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the quipus today?
options: No one is interested in them anymore.
People still do not fully understand all of them.
They were mainly used to write long stories.
Most of them have been lost on the roads.
questions.explain: 最後一段說研究人員正認真努力解讀留下來的奇普，「如果他們成功了」才能知道更多，可推知奇普至今還沒有被完全讀懂，故選 (B)。(A) 與遊客、研究人員的熱情相反；(C) 第二段說奇普主要記錄數字。
questions.evidence: Researchers are also making earnest efforts to read the quipus that have survived.

vocab.stem: The twins look so much alike that even their teachers cannot ______ one from the other.
vocab.explain: 雙胞胎長得太像，連老師都無法「分辨」誰是誰，distinguish A from B 是固定用法，故選 distinguish。dominate（支配）、eliminate（消除）、enlarge（擴大）都不能接 one from the other。

vocab.stem: After a long day of hiking, Tom felt so ______ that he fell asleep on the bus.
vocab.explain: 健行一整天後，湯姆「昏昏欲睡」，在公車上睡著了，故選 drowsy。dusty（滿是灰塵的）、earnest（認真的）、elastic（有彈性的）都無法說明他為什麼睡著。

title: Little Ears, Big Learners
paragraphs: Nobody explains the rules of a language to babies. Yet by the time they start school, most children can talk easily about almost anything. How do they [[acquire|L4-0017]] a language so quickly? Scientists have studied this question for years, and some of the answers sound stranger than [[fiction|L4-0398]].

First, [[infants|L4-0525]] are born ready to learn any language. In their first months, they can [[identify|L4-0502]] differences between the sounds of almost every language. By around the age of one, however, they focus on the sounds they hear at home. These early months lay the [[foundation|L4-0417]] for everything that comes later.

Second, real [[interaction|L4-0553]] matters. When adults talk to babies, they often [[exaggerate|L4-0368]] their voices, speaking slowly in a high, happy tone. When babies make sounds back, a parent's smile or answer gives them useful [[feedback|L4-0394]]. In one well-known [[experimental|L4-0374]] study, American babies heard Chinese either from a live teacher or from the same lessons on video. Only the babies with a live teacher learned to hear the new sounds. The [[frequency|L4-0421]] of words matters, too: children usually learn the words they hear most often first.

Finally, children are clever at finding patterns. A child may say "I goed" instead of "I went." This mistake shows that she has worked out a [[formula|L4-0413]] for talking about the past on her own. It is hard to [[estimate|L4-0361]] how many words a child knows, but those who hear two languages at home are especially [[fortunate|L4-0415]]: many of them grow up [[fluent|L4-0407]] in both.
zh: 沒有人會向嬰兒解釋語言的規則。然而，到了開始上學的年紀，大多數孩子幾乎什麼話題都能輕鬆地聊。他們是怎麼這麼快就學會一種語言的呢？科學家研究這個問題多年，有些答案聽起來比小說還要奇妙。
首先，嬰兒天生就準備好學習任何語言。在出生後的頭幾個月，他們幾乎能分辨每一種語言中聲音的差異。不過大約到了一歲左右，他們就會專注於在家裡聽到的聲音。最初這幾個月，為之後的一切打下了基礎。
其次，真實的互動很重要。大人跟嬰兒說話時，常會誇張地調整聲音，用高而愉快的語調慢慢地說。當嬰兒發出聲音回應時，父母的微笑或回答就給了他們有用的回饋。在一項著名的實驗研究中，一群美國嬰兒聽中文，有的是由老師當面上課，有的是透過影片看相同的課程。結果只有當面聽老師上課的嬰兒學會分辨這些新的聲音。字詞出現的頻率也很重要：孩子通常會先學會最常聽到的字。
最後，孩子很擅長找出規律。小孩可能會說「I goed」而不是「I went」。這個錯誤顯示，她已經自己摸索出一套談論過去的公式。我們很難估計一個孩子到底懂多少字，但在家裡聽兩種語言的孩子特別幸運：他們之中有許多人長大後兩種語言都說得很流利。

questions.stem: What happens to babies' hearing of language sounds by around the age of one?
options: They hear sounds from every language more clearly.
They stop paying attention to all sounds.
They begin to learn grammar rules from their parents.
They focus on the sounds of the language spoken at home.
questions.explain: 第二段說嬰兒一開始幾乎能分辨所有語言的聲音，但到了一歲左右，就會專注於在家裡聽到的聲音，故選 (D)。(A) 正好相反，他們是從「什麼語言都能分辨」變成專注在家中的語言。
questions.evidence: By around the age of one, however, they focus on the sounds they hear at home.

questions.stem: What did the experiment in paragraph 3 show?
options: Babies learn faster from videos than from people.
Babies learned the new sounds only from a live teacher.
American babies cannot learn Chinese sounds at all.
Babies prefer low voices to high voices.
questions.explain: 第三段說，只有由老師當面上課的嬰兒學會分辨新的聲音，看影片的則沒有，故選 (B)。(A) 與實驗結果相反；(C) 不對，有老師當面上課的美國嬰兒確實學會了。
questions.evidence: Only the babies with a live teacher learned to hear the new sounds.

questions.stem: In paragraph 4, what does "those" in "those who hear two languages at home" refer to?
questions.explain: those 後面接 who hear two languages at home，指的是「在家裡聽兩種語言的孩子」，接著又說他們長大後兩種語言都很流利，故選 (A)。(B) words 不會「聽」語言，也不會長大。
questions.evidence: but those who hear two languages at home are especially fortunate

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why parents should teach grammar to babies
How children can learn two languages at school
Several ways children pick up their first language
Why videos are bad for young children
questions.explain: 文章先提出「孩子怎麼這麼快學會語言」，再用 First、Second、Finally 說明嬰兒天生的能力、真實互動和找出規律，主旨是孩子學會母語的幾種方式，故選 (C)。(A) 與第一句「沒有人向嬰兒解釋語言規則」相反；(D) 影片只是實驗中的一個細節。
questions.evidence: How do they acquire a language so quickly?

vocab.stem: My aunt lived in Japan for ten years, so she is ______ in Japanese.
vocab.explain: 阿姨在日本住了十年，所以日文很「流利」，be fluent in + 語言是固定用法，故選 fluent。fierce（兇猛的）、explosive（易爆炸的）、fortunate（幸運的）都不能接 in Japanese 表示語言能力。

vocab.stem: The weather ______ says it will rain this afternoon, so take an umbrella with you.
vocab.explain: 「天氣預報」說下午會下雨，所以要帶傘，weather forecast 是固定搭配，故選 forecast。fantasy（幻想）、ferry（渡輪）、fiction（小說）都不會告訴你天氣。

title: The Girl in the Perfect Photos
paragraphs: As a high school [[freshman|L4-0422]], Kelly spent at least two hours a day on social media. Every night she would [[gaze|L4-0435]] at photos of other girls: a [[gifted|L4-0444]] singer on a stage, a [[graceful|L4-0454]] dancer by the sea, friends laughing under a [[glorious|L4-0450]] evening sky. Their lives looked perfect. Then she would look in the mirror and [[frown|L4-0424]].

Kelly had a [[tendency|L4-0940]] to compare herself with everyone, and she began to feel [[frustration|L4-0426]] and [[anxiety|L4-0044]]. She took many photos of herself but removed almost all of them, so the photo [[gallery|L4-0434]] on her phone was nearly empty. "Why can't I look like them?" she asked her older cousin, Amy, one evening.

Amy smiled kindly. "Do you know how many photos those girls take before they post one? And many of them use special tools to make their skin look smooth. That kind of beauty is [[artificial|L4-0057]]. Besides, a perfect photo is no [[guarantee|L4-0467]] of a happy life." Then she gave Kelly a challenge: for two weeks, use social media for only twenty minutes a day, and each night write down three things she was [[grateful|L4-0460]] for.

At first, it was hard. But slowly, Kelly's list grew: a funny joke from her best friend, her mom's chicken soup, a good grade in math. Writing with [[gratitude|L4-0461]] helped her notice the good things she already had. One afternoon, as she [[giggled|L4-0446]] with her friends on the way home, Kelly realized that she had not thought about anyone else's photos all day.
zh: 凱莉是高一新生，每天至少花兩個小時在社群媒體上。每天晚上，她都會盯著其他女孩的照片看：舞台上有天分的歌手、海邊姿態優雅的舞者、在絢麗晚霞下歡笑的朋友們。她們的生活看起來完美無缺。然後她會看著鏡子，皺起眉頭。
凱莉習慣拿自己和每個人比較，她開始感到挫折和焦慮。她幫自己拍了很多照片，卻幾乎全部刪掉，所以手機裡的相簿幾乎是空的。某天晚上，她問表姊艾咪：「為什麼我不能看起來像她們一樣？」
艾咪溫柔地笑了。「你知道那些女生在貼出一張照片之前要拍幾張嗎？而且她們很多人會用特殊工具讓皮膚看起來很光滑。那種美是人工的。再說，一張完美的照片並不能保證快樂的人生。」接著她給凱莉一個挑戰：接下來兩週，每天只用二十分鐘的社群媒體，並且每天晚上寫下三件讓她心懷感謝的事。
一開始，這很困難。但慢慢地，凱莉的清單越來越長：好朋友說的一個好笑的笑話、媽媽煮的雞湯、數學考了好成績。帶著感恩的心書寫，讓她注意到自己早已擁有的美好事物。有一天下午，她和朋友在回家路上咯咯地笑著，凱莉突然發現，她一整天都沒有想起別人的照片。

questions.stem: Why was the photo gallery on Kelly's phone nearly empty?
options: She had lost her old phone.
She did not like taking photos.
She removed most of the photos she took of herself.
Her cousin told her to clean it up.
questions.explain: 第二段說凱莉幫自己拍了很多照片，卻幾乎全部刪掉，所以相簿幾乎是空的，故選 (C)。(B) 不對，她其實拍了很多照片，只是不滿意而刪掉。
questions.evidence: She took many photos of herself but removed almost all of them

questions.stem: What challenge did Amy give Kelly?
options: To use social media less and write down things she was grateful for
To post one photo of herself every day
To stop using her phone for a whole month
To take photos of the evening sky
questions.explain: 第三段說艾咪要凱莉兩週內每天只用二十分鐘社群媒體，並在每晚寫下三件感謝的事，故選 (A)。(C) 不對，挑戰是兩週、每天限時二十分鐘，並不是完全不用手機一個月。
questions.evidence: for two weeks, use social media for only twenty minutes a day, and each night write down three things she was grateful for

questions.stem: The word "artificial" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 艾咪說很多女生用特殊工具讓皮膚看起來光滑，所以那種美是 artificial，也就是「人工的、不真實的」，故選 (B)。(A) natural（自然的）意思正好相反。
questions.evidence: That kind of beauty is artificial.

questions.stem: What can we infer about Kelly at the end of the story?
options: She has decided to stop seeing her friends.
She now posts more photos than before.
She still compares herself with others all day.
She has started to enjoy her own life more.
questions.explain: 最後一段說凱莉透過感恩書寫注意到身邊的美好，和朋友一起笑時，發現一整天都沒想起別人的照片，可推知她更能享受自己的生活了，故選 (D)。(C) 與「一整天都沒想起別人的照片」相反。
questions.evidence: Kelly realized that she had not thought about anyone else's photos all day.

vocab.stem: While her parents were working abroad, her aunt acted as her ______ and took care of her.
vocab.explain: 父母在國外工作時，阿姨擔任她的「監護人」照顧她，故選 guardian。globe（地球儀）、ginger（薑）、grief（悲傷）都不是人，不能照顧她。

vocab.stem: The teacher ______ when she saw that half of the class had not done their homework.
vocab.explain: 老師看到半班沒寫作業，就「皺起眉頭」，故選 frowned。furnished（為……配置家具）、graphed（用圖表表示）、guaranteed（保證）都必須接受詞，句意也不通。

title: When a Storm Is on the Horizon
paragraphs: In North America, they are called [[hurricanes|L4-0497]]; in Taiwan, we call them typhoons. Both are the same kind of powerful storm, and both form over warm oceans. Weather experts can usually [[predict|L4-0755]] a storm's path days before it arrives, but many people still wait until dark clouds appear on the [[horizon|L4-0490]] before they get ready. By then, it may be too late.

Getting ready early means you do not have to do things in [[haste|L4-0479]]. Every [[household|L4-0493]] should have an emergency kit with drinking water, food that does not need cooking, a flashlight, extra [[batteries|L4-0089]], and basic medicine. Put copies of [[essential|L4-0359]] papers, such as [[identification|L4-0501]] cards, in a plastic bag. If you need supplies, visit a [[hardware|L4-0476]] store early, before everyone else rushes there.

Outside, bring in anything the wind could blow away, like plants and chairs, and roll up the garden [[hose|L4-0492]]. If the government tells people in your area to leave their homes, go without [[hesitation|L4-0485]]. [[Rescue|L4-0836]] teams in [[helicopters|L4-0483]] sometimes have to save people who chose to stay behind.

Most of all, do not let [[ignorance|L4-0506]] put you in danger. Follow the advice of weather experts instead of rumors online. While the storm is passing, stay inside and away from windows. If the wind suddenly stops and a strange [[hush|L4-0498]] falls, do not go out. You may be in the eye of the storm, and strong winds will soon return from the other side.
zh: 在北美洲，它們被稱為「颶風」；在台灣，我們叫它們「颱風」。兩者是同一種強烈的風暴，而且都在溫暖的海洋上形成。氣象專家通常能在風暴抵達前好幾天預測它的路徑，但許多人仍要等到烏雲出現在地平線上，才開始做準備。到那時候，可能已經太遲了。
及早準備，就不必匆匆忙忙地做事。每個家庭都應該準備一個緊急避難包，裡面要有飲用水、不需要烹煮的食物、手電筒、備用電池和基本藥品。把重要文件的影本，例如身分證件，放進塑膠袋裡。如果需要補充物資，要提早去五金行，趕在大家蜂擁而至之前。
在屋外，要把任何可能被風吹走的東西搬進室內，像是盆栽和椅子，並把花園的水管捲起來。如果政府要求你所在地區的居民撤離家園，就要毫不猶豫地離開。搜救隊有時必須搭直升機去救那些選擇留在家裡的人。
最重要的是，別因為無知而讓自己陷入危險。要聽從氣象專家的建議，而不是網路上的謠言。風暴經過時，要待在室內，並遠離窗戶。如果風突然停了，四周陷入一片奇怪的寂靜，千萬不要出門。你可能正處在暴風眼中，強風很快就會從另一側再度襲來。

title: When the Wind Stops Blowing
paragraphs: For more than a hundred years, most of the world's electricity has come from burning coal, oil, and gas. These fuels are cheap and easy to use, but they also release gases that warm the [[globe|L4-0449]]. To slow this change, many countries are now turning to renewable energy, which comes from sources that never run out, such as the sun and the wind. Many people hope that clean energy will one day [[dominate|L4-0315]] the market and [[eliminate|L4-0338]] the need for coal altogether.

Yet clean energy has one big problem: it is [[dependent|L4-0270]] on the weather. Solar panels produce nothing at night, and wind farms stand [[idle|L4-0504]] on calm days. Since even the best weather [[forecast|L4-0411]] cannot [[guarantee|L4-0467]] that the sun will shine or the wind will blow, power companies must find ways to keep the lights on when nature does not help.

To solve this problem, engineers have [[devised|L4-0279]] several clever ideas. One is to store extra energy. On sunny, windy days, the extra power can be saved in huge [[batteries|L4-0089]] and used later. Another, still largely [[experimental|L4-0374]], is to use extra electricity to make [[hydrogen|L4-0499]] gas. The gas can be stored for weeks and then used to produce power, leaving mainly water behind. Meanwhile, [[economists|L4-0331]] point out that the cost of solar power has fallen sharply over the past twenty years, making it a more [[economical|L4-0329]] choice than ever before.

Ordinary people can play a part, too. Some families have put solar panels on their roofs, and every [[household|L4-0493]] can save energy by turning off lights and machines that are not in use. The road ahead is still long, and there will be many problems to solve. But with [[determination|L4-0277]] and new ideas, a future powered by clean energy may already be on the [[horizon|L4-0490]].
zh: 一百多年來，全世界大部分的電力都來自燃燒煤、石油和天然氣。這些燃料便宜又好用，但也會釋放讓地球變暖的氣體。為了減緩這種變化，許多國家現在轉向可再生能源，也就是來自太陽和風等永遠用不完的來源的能源。許多人希望，乾淨能源有一天能主宰市場，讓人們完全不再需要煤。
然而，乾淨能源有一個大問題：它得看天氣。太陽能板在夜間無法發電，風力發電場在無風的日子也只能閒置。由於再準確的天氣預報也無法保證會出太陽或颳風，電力公司必須想辦法在大自然不配合時，仍能讓電燈保持明亮。
為了解決這個問題，工程師想出了幾個巧妙的辦法。其一是把多餘的能源儲存起來。在陽光充足、風又大的日子，多出來的電可以存進巨大的電池，留待之後使用。另一個辦法目前大致還在實驗階段，就是用多餘的電來製造氫氣。氫氣可以儲存好幾個星期，之後再用來發電，留下的主要是水。同時，經濟學家指出，太陽能發電的成本在過去二十年間大幅下降，使它成為比以往任何時候都更划算的選擇。
一般人也能出一份力。有些家庭已經在屋頂裝設太陽能板，而每個家庭都可以隨手關掉不用的電燈和電器來節約能源。未來的路還很長，也還有許多問題需要解決。但只要有決心和新的想法，由乾淨能源供電的未來或許已經近在眼前。

title: The Woman Who Watched Chimpanzees
paragraphs: As a girl in England, Jane Goodall loved animals and had an [[imaginative|L4-0511]] mind. She dreamed of living among wild animals in Africa one day. After school, she worked as a waitress to save money for the trip. In 1957, at the age of 23, she finally sailed to Africa.

There, she met a famous scientist who wanted someone to study wild chimpanzees. Jane had no university degree, but he had the strong [[impression|L4-0520]] that her patience and love of animals mattered more than a degree. In 1960, she began her work in a forest in East Africa.

At first, the chimpanzees ran away whenever she came near. Jane did not want to [[interfere|L4-0554]] with their lives; her only [[intention|L4-0551]] was to understand them. She sat and watched day after day until they let her come close. One day, she saw something amazing: a chimpanzee was using a grass [[stem|L4-0914]] to pull insects out of a hole and eat them. At that time, most scientists believed that only humans made and used tools. Her [[observation|L4-0681]] was a clear [[indication|L4-0524]] that animals were smarter than people had thought.

Jane also gave the chimpanzees names instead of numbers and wrote about their feelings. Some scientists [[criticized|L4-0239]] this, but she trusted her [[intuition|L4-0559]]. She showed that chimpanzees [[interact|L4-0552]] much like humans and that young ones learn by [[imitating|L4-0512]] their mothers. Later, her [[informative|L4-0529]] books and talks helped people care about [[endangered|L4-0347]] chimpanzees, and she became one of the most [[influential|L4-0528]] scientists of her time.
zh: 珍・古德小時候住在英國，她熱愛動物，而且富有想像力。她夢想有一天能到非洲，和野生動物生活在一起。中學畢業後，她當女服務生存錢，準備這趟旅程。1957 年，二十三歲的她終於搭船前往非洲。
在那裡，她遇見一位著名的科學家，他正在找人研究野生黑猩猩。珍沒有大學學位，但這位科學家強烈地感覺到，她的耐心和對動物的愛更加重要。1960 年，她在東非的一座森林裡展開了研究工作。
起初，只要她一靠近，黑猩猩就會逃開。珍不想干擾牠們的生活，她唯一的目的就是了解牠們。她日復一日地坐著觀察，直到牠們願意讓她靠近。有一天，她看到一件驚人的事：一隻黑猩猩正用一根草莖把昆蟲從洞裡拉出來吃。當時，大多數科學家認為只有人類會製造和使用工具。她的觀察清楚地顯示，動物比人們以為的還要聰明。
珍還為黑猩猩取名字，而不是用編號稱呼牠們，並記錄牠們的情緒。有些科學家批評這種做法，但她相信自己的直覺。她證明黑猩猩彼此互動的方式和人類很像，小黑猩猩也會模仿母親來學習。後來，她那些內容豐富的著作和演講，讓人們開始關心瀕臨絕種的黑猩猩，她也成為那個時代最有影響力的科學家之一。

title: A Letter to the School Librarian
paragraphs: Dear Ms. Chen,

My name is Lisa Wang, and I am a second-year student. As our school [[librarian|L4-0590]], you have always worked hard to make the library a great place. Thanks to you, our [[literature|L4-0598]] collection is wonderful, and your monthly [[literary|L4-0597]] talks are very popular. However, I would like to share a few problems in the study room, which many of my classmates and I use every day after school.

First, the internet connection is [[lousy|L4-0604]]. Web pages [[lag|L4-0576]] so badly that it can take minutes to open a single file. Second, the hot-water [[kettle|L4-0571]] in the corner has been broken for two weeks. Third, there are not enough chairs, so some students have to sit on the floor or [[lean|L4-0582]] against the shelves while they read. Finally, when [[lectures|L4-0584]] are held in the room next door, the noise makes it hard to [[concentrate|L4-0172]].

Most of us do not come to the library for a [[leisurely|L4-0587]] read. We come to prepare for exams, and the study room is the only quiet [[facility|L4-0383]] we have. With exams coming soon, could you please [[lengthen|L4-0588]] its opening hours until 7 p.m.? I understand that these changes may cost money, but I believe they would be a [[logical|L4-0602]] [[investment|L4-0563]] in our future. Thank you for reading my letter. I would be happy to help in any way I can.
With [[appreciation|L4-0050]],
Lisa Wang
zh: 親愛的陳老師：
我是王莉莎，二年級的學生。身為我們學校的圖書館員，您一直很努力讓圖書館成為一個很棒的地方。多虧了您，我們的文學藏書非常豐富，您每個月舉辦的文學講座也很受歡迎。不過，我想跟您反映自習室的幾個問題，我和許多同學每天放學後都會使用那間自習室。
第一，網路連線很糟。網頁延遲得很嚴重，光是打開一個檔案就要好幾分鐘。第二，角落的熱水壺已經壞了兩個星期。第三，椅子不夠，有些同學看書時只能坐在地上，或是靠著書架。最後，隔壁教室舉辦講座時，噪音讓人很難專心。
我們大多數人來圖書館不是為了悠閒地閱讀，而是為了準備考試，而自習室是我們唯一安靜的場所。考試快到了，能不能請您把自習室的開放時間延長到晚上七點？我明白這些改變可能需要經費，但我相信這會是對我們未來合理的投資。謝謝您閱讀我的信。如果有任何我能幫忙的地方，我很樂意協助。
謹致謝意，
王莉莎 敬上
