vocab.stem: These shoes are a little tight. Can you help me ______ the laces?
vocab.explain: 鞋子有點緊，請人幫忙把鞋帶「鬆開」，故選 loosen。invade（侵略）、kneel（跪下）、lecture（訓斥、講課）都不能用在鞋帶上。

title: The Muddy Hill Marathon
paragraphs: Every spring, runners from all over Taiwan gather in a small [[mountainous|L4-0655]] town for one of the hardest [[marathons|L4-0616]] on the island. The road climbs up and down steep hills, and after a night of rain, the path becomes so [[muddy|L4-0656]] that it almost pulls the shoes off your feet.

Last year, eighteen-year-old Hsu Ya-ting ran the race for the first time. Her [[motivation|L4-0654]] was simple: her grandfather had worked as a [[miner|L4-0637]] in the town, and she wanted to see the hills he always talked about. Her coach, a [[loyal|L4-0605]] friend of the family, warned her not to run at her [[maximum|L4-0619]] speed too early.

At first, Ya-ting felt great. Then, on the second hill, [[misfortune|L4-0644]] struck. She slipped and fell into a [[messy|L4-0632]] pool of mud, and a [[fierce|L4-0399]] pain shot through her knee. For a moment, she wanted to give up. Then an older runner stopped beside her. "Can you stand?" he asked. "Walk with me for a while." They walked side by side until her knee felt better, and with new [[determination|L4-0277]], she began to run again.

Ya-ting finished in the bottom half of the race, covered in mud from head to toe. When a reporter asked about her race, she showed great [[modesty|L4-0649]]. "I wasn't fast," she said. "The real hero was the man who waited for me." She was deeply [[grateful|L4-0460]] to him. It was not her best time, but it was the most [[memorable|L4-0624]] day of her life.
zh: 每年春天，來自全台各地的跑者會聚集在一座多山的小鎮，參加島上最艱難的馬拉松之一。道路在陡峭的山丘間上上下下，下過一夜雨之後，路面泥濘到幾乎會把鞋子從腳上扯下來。
去年，十八歲的徐雅婷第一次參加這場比賽。她的動機很單純：她的爺爺曾在這個小鎮當礦工，她想親眼看看爺爺常常提起的那些山丘。她的教練是她們家忠實的老朋友，提醒她不要太早就用最快的速度衝刺。
一開始，雅婷感覺很好。接著在第二座山丘上，不幸發生了。她滑了一跤，跌進一灘髒亂的泥水裡，膝蓋一陣劇痛。有那麼一刻，她想放棄。這時一位年長的跑者在她身旁停下來。「你站得起來嗎？」他問。「跟我一起走一段吧。」他們並肩走著，直到她的膝蓋好一些，她才帶著新的決心再度跑了起來。
雅婷以後半段的名次完賽，從頭到腳都是泥巴。記者問起她的比賽時，她表現得非常謙虛。「我跑得不快，」她說。「真正的英雄是那位等我的先生。」她打從心底感激他。那不是她最好的成績，卻是她一生中最難忘的一天。

questions.stem: Why did Ya-ting decide to run this marathon?
options: She wanted to win prize money.
Her coach told her that she had to.
She wanted to see the hills her grandfather talked about.
She hoped to meet a famous runner.
questions.explain: 第二段說她的動機很單純：爺爺曾在這個小鎮當礦工，她想看看爺爺常提起的山丘，故選 (C)。(B) 教練只提醒她別太早用最快速度跑，並沒有要求她參賽。
questions.evidence: she wanted to see the hills he always talked about

questions.stem: What happened to Ya-ting on the second hill?
options: She slipped, fell into the mud, and hurt her knee.
She lost her way in the rain.
She ran too fast and had to stop.
Her shoes came off, so she could not go on.
questions.explain: 第三段說她在第二座山丘滑倒、跌進泥水裡，膝蓋一陣劇痛，故選 (A)。(D) 第一段只說泥巴「幾乎」會把鞋子扯下來，並沒有說她的鞋子真的掉了。
questions.evidence: She slipped and fell into a messy pool of mud, and a fierce pain shot through her knee.

questions.stem: The word "modesty" in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to ______.
options: not speaking too highly of oneself
questions.explain: 雅婷沒有誇耀自己，反而說「我跑得不快，真正的英雄是那位等我的先生」，可知 modesty 指「謙虛、不自誇」，故選 (D)。(C) pride（驕傲）正好與文意相反。
questions.evidence: "I wasn't fast," she said. "The real hero was the man who waited for me."

questions.stem: What can we infer from the story?
options: Ya-ting was angry that she did not win the race.
Ya-ting cared more about the older runner's kindness than her finishing time.
The older runner was Ya-ting's coach.
Ya-ting will never run a marathon again.
questions.explain: 雅婷說真正的英雄是等她的那位跑者，並說這雖然不是她最好的成績，卻是最難忘的一天，可推知她更看重陌生人的善意，故選 (B)。(C) 文中的教練是她們家的朋友，與那位年長跑者是不同的人。
questions.evidence: It was not her best time, but it was the most memorable day of her life.

vocab.stem: After playing soccer in the rain, the boys came home with ______ shoes and left marks all over the floor.
vocab.explain: 在雨中踢足球後，鞋子沾滿泥巴，才會在地板上留下痕跡，故選 muddy（泥濘的）。loyal（忠誠的）、measurable（可測量的）、magnetic（有磁性的）都無法說明為何會弄髒地板。

vocab.stem: She trained for months to run in the city ______, a race of about 42 kilometers.
vocab.explain: 約 42 公里的賽跑就是「馬拉松」，故選 marathon。mule（騾子）、mechanic（技工）、miner（礦工）都不是比賽的名稱。

title: Sixteen Sunrises a Day
paragraphs: Imagine watching the sun rise sixteen times in a single day. For astronauts on the International Space Station, this is normal. The station [[orbits|L4-0693]] Earth about once every ninety minutes, flying high above the clouds at a very high speed.

The station is the result of a [[partnership|L4-0713]] between several countries, including the United States, Russia, Japan, Canada, and many countries in Europe. Its first part was sent into space in 1998, and people have lived on board since 2000. Astronauts of different [[nationalities|L4-0664]] live and work together in a small space, so [[mutual|L4-0661]] respect is very important. One small problem that someone [[neglects|L4-0666]] could turn into a [[nightmare|L4-0669]] for everyone.

Daily life up there is full of challenges. Because everything floats, even eating and sleeping take practice. Food must be light to carry, but it also has to be [[nutritious|L4-0676]], since the body slowly loses bone and muscle in space. To stay strong, astronauts exercise about two hours every day. They also carry out [[experimental|L4-0374]] work that cannot be done on Earth, and they must learn to deal with months of [[isolation|L4-0567]] from family and friends.

Long ago, the idea of people living in space sounded like [[nonsense|L4-0671]]. Today, the station is an [[outstanding|L4-0699]] example of what people can do when they share a [[noble|L4-0670]] goal. Many astronauts say that when they look down at Earth and see its [[curved|L4-0249]] [[horizon|L4-0490]], the borders between countries seem to disappear.
zh: 想像一下在一天之內看見十六次日出。對國際太空站上的太空人來說，這是家常便飯。太空站大約每九十分鐘繞地球一圈，以極快的速度在雲層上方高高飛行。
太空站是好幾個國家合作的成果，包括美國、俄羅斯、日本、加拿大，以及許多歐洲國家。它的第一個部分在 1998 年送上太空，從 2000 年起就一直有人住在上面。不同國籍的太空人在狹小的空間裡一起生活和工作，因此互相尊重非常重要。只要有人忽略一個小問題，就可能變成所有人的惡夢。
那裡的日常生活充滿挑戰。因為所有東西都會飄浮，連吃飯和睡覺都需要練習。食物必須輕巧、方便運送，但也要有營養，因為人體在太空中會慢慢流失骨骼和肌肉。為了保持強壯，太空人每天大約運動兩小時。他們也要進行在地球上無法完成的實驗性工作，還必須學會面對與家人朋友分隔好幾個月的孤立感。
很久以前，人類住在太空裡的想法聽起來像是胡說八道。如今，太空站是一個傑出的例子，展現人們懷抱崇高目標時能做到什麼。許多太空人說，當他們俯瞰地球、看見它彎曲的地平線時，國與國之間的邊界似乎都消失了。

questions.stem: How often does the space station travel around Earth?
questions.explain: 第一段說太空站大約每九十分鐘繞地球一圈，故選 (B)。「十六次」是太空人一天看到日出的次數，不是每小時繞行的次數，所以 (C) 錯誤。
questions.evidence: The station orbits Earth about once every ninety minutes

questions.stem: Why must food on the space station be nutritious?
options: Astronauts have no time to cook.
Light food is cheaper to send.
Astronauts do not like the taste of space food.
The body slowly loses bone and muscle in space.
questions.explain: 第三段說食物必須有營養，因為人體在太空中會慢慢流失骨骼和肌肉，故選 (D)。(B) 文中提到食物要「輕」是為了方便運送，並不是營養的理由，也沒有提到價格。
questions.evidence: since the body slowly loses bone and muscle in space

questions.stem: The word "neglects" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 句意是：一個被某人「忽略」的小問題，可能變成所有人的惡夢，故 neglects 意思接近「沒有注意、疏忽」，選 (A)。(B) 若問題被很快修好，就不會變成惡夢，與文意不合。
questions.evidence: One small problem that someone neglects could turn into a nightmare for everyone.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Life on the International Space Station and what it shows us
Why the sun rises sixteen times a day on Earth
questions.explain: 全文介紹國際太空站的繞行速度、多國合作、太空人的日常生活，最後說明它展現人們合作的力量，故選 (C)。(D) 一天看到十六次日出是在太空站上，不是在地球上。
questions.evidence: Today, the station is an outstanding example of what people can do when they share a noble goal.

vocab.stem: Vegetables, fish, and brown rice make a ______ meal that keeps you healthy.
vocab.explain: 蔬菜、魚和糙米組成一頓能讓人保持健康的餐點，應是「營養的」，故選 nutritious。nuclear（核能的）、oval（橢圓形的）、partial（部分的；偏袒的）都無法說明這頓飯為何讓人健康。

vocab.stem: After watching a scary movie, the little boy had a terrible ______ and woke up crying.
vocab.explain: 看完恐怖片後做了可怕的「惡夢」而哭著醒來，故選 nightmare。nursery（托兒所）、orbit（軌道）、overcoat（大衣）都不能「做」，也不會讓人哭醒。

title: Thirty-Six Chances
paragraphs: Last summer, my grandmother gave me her most treasured [[possession|L4-0751]]: an old film camera wrapped in a soft cloth. She had loved [[photography|L4-0734]] since she was a girl.

My phone is light, but the camera is not very [[portable|L4-0748]]. It is heavy, and each roll of film holds only thirty-six pictures. At first, I was [[pessimistic|L4-0728]]. "Why would anyone still use this?" I asked. But after some gentle [[persuasion|L4-0726]] from Grandma, I took it to the park.

Taking a photo turned out to be slow work. I had to [[peer|L4-0719]] through a tiny window, turn the lens, and get the light [[precisely|L4-0754]] right. Our cat, Pudding, followed me and kept trying to [[peep|L4-0718]] into my bag, so one picture shows nothing but her [[paw|L4-0716]]. With my phone, I would have taken another one at once. With film, every picture had to count, and I could not see any of them until later.

When the photos came back a week later, many were far from [[perfection|L4-0723]]. Some were too dark, and one had a [[peculiar|L4-0717]] yellow line across it. Yet I loved them more than the [[plentiful|L4-0741]] pictures on my phone, which I hardly ever look at. Grandma smiled and said something rather [[philosophical|L4-0732]]: "A photo isn't for keeping a moment perfect. It's for keeping you there a little longer." Her words left a deep [[impression|L4-0520]] on me, and to my [[delight|L4-0262]], I now see the world more slowly. I feel [[fortunate|L4-0415]] to have such a gift.
zh: 去年夏天，奶奶把她最珍貴的東西送給了我：一台用軟布包著的老底片相機。她從小就熱愛攝影。
我的手機很輕，但這台相機一點也不方便攜帶。它很重，而且每捲底片只能拍三十六張。一開始我很悲觀。「為什麼還會有人用這個？」我問。但在奶奶溫和的勸說下，我還是帶著它去了公園。
拍一張照片原來是件很慢的事。我得透過小小的觀景窗仔細看、轉動鏡頭，還要把光線調得剛剛好。我們家的貓布丁一路跟著我，一直想偷看我的包包，結果有一張照片只拍到牠的爪子。如果用手機，我會馬上重拍一張。但用底片，每一張都得算數，而且要等到之後才看得到。
一週後照片洗出來時，很多張都稱不上完美。有些太暗，有一張還有一條奇怪的黃線橫過畫面。然而，比起手機裡那大量、我幾乎從不翻看的照片，我更愛這些照片。奶奶笑著說了一句頗有哲理的話：「照片不是為了讓某個瞬間保持完美，而是讓你在那裡多停留一會兒。」她的話讓我印象深刻。令我高興的是，我現在會用比較慢的步調看這個世界。能擁有這樣的禮物，我覺得很幸運。

questions.stem: What did the writer think of the film camera at first?
options: She did not see why anyone would still use it.
She thought it was lighter than her phone.
She believed it took better pictures than her phone.
questions.explain: 第二段說作者一開始很悲觀，還問「為什麼還會有人用這個？」，故選 (A)。(B) 與文意相反，文中說手機很輕，相機卻很重。
questions.evidence: "Why would anyone still use this?" I asked.

questions.stem: Why does one of the photos show only a cat's paw?
options: The writer wanted a picture of the paw.
Grandma took the picture by mistake.
The cat kept trying to look into the writer's bag.
questions.explain: 第三段說貓咪布丁一直想偷看作者的包包，所以有一張照片只拍到牠的爪子，故選 (C)。照片是作者自己拍的，奶奶並沒有一起去公園，所以 (B) 錯誤。
questions.evidence: kept trying to peep into my bag, so one picture shows nothing but her paw

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, what does "them" in "I loved them more" refer to?
options: The pictures on the writer's phone
The film photos that came back
questions.explain: them 指的是前面提到「一週後洗出來」的底片照片，作者說她愛這些照片勝過手機裡大量的照片，故選 (B)。(A) 手機照片是被拿來比較的對象，作者說她幾乎從不翻看。
questions.evidence: When the photos came back a week later, many were far from perfection.

questions.stem: What did the writer most likely learn from using the film camera?
options: Phones always take worse pictures than film cameras.
A photo is only good if it is perfect.
She should give the camera back to her grandmother.
Taking photos slowly can make moments more meaningful.
questions.explain: 作者發現底片照片雖不完美，她卻更喜歡，並說自己現在用比較慢的步調看世界，可推知她學到慢慢拍照能讓時刻更有意義，故選 (D)。(B) 正好與奶奶「照片不是為了保持完美」的話相反。
questions.evidence: I now see the world more slowly

vocab.stem: This small speaker is ______, so you can easily take it to the beach.
vocab.explain: 因為喇叭是「可攜帶的」，所以能輕鬆帶去海邊，故選 portable。passive（被動的）、pessimistic（悲觀的）、peculiar（奇特的）都無法說明為何容易帶著走。

vocab.stem: The cat walked across the wet floor and left little ______ prints everywhere.
vocab.explain: 貓走過濕地板留下的是「爪印」，paw prints 是常見說法，故選 paw。pickle（醃菜）、plum（李子）、postage（郵資）都不是貓會留下的痕跡。

title: From Letters to Pockets
paragraphs: For most of human history, sending a message to someone far away meant writing a letter. After paying the [[postage|L4-0752]], you might wait weeks or even months for a reply, especially if the letter had to cross an ocean. During that long [[lag|L4-0576]], a lot could change. A letter saying "All is well" might arrive long after things had gone wrong.

In 1876, Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone, one of the most [[influential|L4-0528]] [[inventions|L4-0562]] in history. For the first time, two people in different places could hear each other's voices and [[interact|L4-0552]] at the same moment. Early telephones were large [[mechanical|L4-0623]] machines fixed to the wall, and many calls had to be connected by hand by workers at the telephone company.

The next big step was making the phone [[portable|L4-0748]]. The first call from a handheld mobile phone was made in 1973. That phone weighed about one kilogram, and its [[battery|L4-0089]] lasted only about thirty minutes of talking. At the time, few people could imagine that a phone would one day become one of a teenager's most important [[possessions|L4-0751]].

Today's smartphones do far more than make calls. They can show your [[precise|L4-0754]] location on a map, take photos, and let you see the face of a friend on the other side of the world. Teenagers can chat with their [[peers|L4-0719]] all day long. Yet some people worry that we now spend more time with screens than with each other. It is easy to [[misunderstand|L4-0646]] a short text message, and some people feel a deep sense of [[isolation|L4-0567]] even when they are always online.

Not everyone is so [[pessimistic|L4-0728]], however. A phone, after all, is only a tool. Whether it brings people closer or pushes them apart depends on how we use it. Real [[mutual|L4-0661]] understanding still needs time and attention, just as it did in the days when people waited months for a letter.
zh: 在人類歷史的大部分時間裡，要傳訊息給遠方的人，就得寫信。付了郵資之後，你可能要等上好幾週甚至好幾個月才收到回信，尤其是信件必須漂洋過海的時候。在這段漫長的延遲中，很多事情都可能改變。一封寫著「一切安好」的信，可能在事情出了差錯很久之後才送到。
1876 年，亞歷山大・格拉漢姆・貝爾取得了電話的專利，這是史上最具影響力的發明之一。人們第一次能夠在不同的地方聽見彼此的聲音，並且即時互動。早期的電話是固定在牆上的大型機械裝置，許多通話必須由電話公司的員工用手接線。
下一個重大突破，是讓電話變得可以攜帶。第一通用手持行動電話撥出的電話出現在 1973 年。那支電話重約一公斤，電池只能撐大約三十分鐘的通話。當時，很少人能想像有一天電話會成為青少年最重要的隨身物品之一。
今日的智慧型手機能做的遠不只打電話。它們能在地圖上顯示你的精確位置、拍照，還能讓你看見地球另一端朋友的臉。青少年可以整天和同儕聊天。然而，有些人擔心我們現在花在螢幕上的時間比彼此相處的時間還多。簡短的文字訊息很容易被誤解，有些人即使隨時在線上，仍感到深深的孤立。
不過，並非每個人都這麼悲觀。畢竟手機只是一種工具。它讓人們更親近還是更疏遠，取決於我們如何使用它。真正的相互理解仍然需要時間和用心，就像從前人們花好幾個月等待一封信的年代一樣。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to write a good letter
How long-distance communication has changed, and what this means for us
Why phones are bad for teenagers
The life of Alexander Graham Bell
questions.explain: 文章從寫信、電話發明、行動電話到智慧型手機，說明遠距離溝通方式的演變，最後討論它對人際關係的影響，故選 (B)。(D) 貝爾只在第二段出現一次，不是全文重點。
questions.evidence: For most of human history, sending a message to someone far away meant writing a letter.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the first handheld mobile phone?
options: Its battery lasted a whole day.
questions.explain: 第三段說第一支手持行動電話重約一公斤，故選 (C)。(A) 1876 年是貝爾取得電話專利的年份；(D) 文中說電池只能撐大約三十分鐘的通話。
questions.evidence: That phone weighed about one kilogram, and its battery lasted only about thirty minutes of talking.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the writer's view of smartphones?
options: Whether they help or harm us depends on how we use them.
They should be kept away from teenagers.
They have made letters more popular.
They have solved all the problems of communication.
questions.explain: 最後一段說手機只是工具，讓人更親近還是更疏遠取決於我們如何使用，可推知作者對手機持中立的看法，故選 (A)。(D) 第四段提到訊息容易被誤解、有人感到孤立，可見手機並未解決所有溝通問題。
questions.evidence: Whether it brings people closer or pushes them apart depends on how we use it.

questions.stem: The word "lag" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 前一句說寄信後可能要等好幾週甚至好幾個月才有回信，所以 that long lag 指的就是這段「等待、延遲的時間」，故選 (D)。(B) 短訊息和「漫長的」lag 意思不合。
questions.evidence: During that long lag, a lot could change.

vocab.stem: How much is the ______ for sending this package to Japan by air?
vocab.explain: 把包裹空運寄到日本要付的是「郵資」，故選 postage。perfume（香水）、pickle（醃菜）、paw（爪子）都和寄包裹的費用無關。

vocab.stem: Please tell me the ______ time your train arrives so that I can meet you at the station.
vocab.explain: 要去車站接人，需要知道火車抵達的「精確」時間，故選 precise。passive（被動的）、peculiar（奇特的）、poisonous（有毒的）都不能用來修飾抵達時間。

title: Who Gets Paid for Your Chocolate?
paragraphs: In Ms. Kao's class, Jia-hui began her [[presentation|L4-0759]] with a question: "Who gets paid for your chocolate?" A bar of chocolate may cost only a few dollars, but its story starts far away. Most cocoa beans are grown on small farms in hot, wet places such as West Africa, where the heat and [[rainfall|L4-0799]] are right for cocoa trees.

For many of these farmers, however, growing cocoa is not very [[profitable|L4-0773]]. The price of beans goes up and down, and small farmers have little power to ask for more. While some large companies [[prosper|L4-0780]], many farming families struggle to pay for food and school.

This is where fair trade comes in. Under fair trade, buyers [[guarantee|L4-0467]] farmers a fair price even when market prices fall, so a bad year will not [[ruin|L4-0866]] them. Buyers also pay a little extra money that farming [[communities|L4-0163]] can use for [[investment|L4-0563]] in schools, clean water, or better tools. Fair trade alone cannot [[reform|L4-0815]] the whole market, but it makes farmers' needs a [[priority|L4-0765]] and moves the system a step closer to [[equality|L4-0356]].

Thanks to [[publicity|L4-0789]] in schools and online, fair trade has won wider [[recognition|L4-0806]] in many countries. Its products usually cost a little more, though. "So next time you buy chocolate, coffee, or bananas," Jia-hui finished, "stop and [[reflect|L4-0813]] on the people behind them. Our [[pursuit|L4-0793]] of a cheap snack should not stand in the way of someone else's [[prosperity|L4-0781]]."
zh: 在高老師的課堂上，佳慧用一個問題開始她的報告：「你買巧克力的錢，到底付給了誰？」一條巧克力可能只要幾塊錢，但它的故事從很遠的地方開始。大部分的可可豆種在炎熱潮濕地區的小農場上，例如西非，那裡的氣溫和降雨量都很適合可可樹生長。
然而對許多農民來說，種可可並不太賺錢。可可豆的價格忽高忽低，小農幾乎沒有能力要求更高的價格。當一些大公司生意興隆時，許多農家卻連食物和學費都難以負擔。
這就是公平貿易派上用場的地方。在公平貿易之下，即使市場價格下跌，買家也保證付給農民合理的價格，讓一個壞年頭不至於毀了他們。買家還會多付一些錢，讓農村社區用來投資學校、乾淨的水或更好的工具。公平貿易本身無法改革整個市場，但它把農民的需求當成優先事項，讓這個體系朝平等更靠近一步。
多虧在學校和網路上的宣傳，公平貿易在許多國家獲得了更廣泛的認可。不過，它的產品通常比較貴一點。「所以下次你買巧克力、咖啡或香蕉時，」佳慧在結尾說，「請停下來想一想它們背後的人。我們追求便宜的零食，不應該擋住別人邁向富足的路。」

questions.stem: According to the passage, why is growing cocoa often not profitable for small farmers?
options: Cocoa trees need too much rain.
Big companies refuse to buy their beans.
Bean prices change, and the farmers have little power to ask for more.
questions.explain: 第二段說可可豆價格忽高忽低，小農幾乎沒有能力要求更高的價格，所以種可可不太賺錢，故選 (D)。(A) 第一段反而說西非的降雨量很適合可可樹。
questions.evidence: The price of beans goes up and down, and small farmers have little power to ask for more.

questions.stem: Which is NOT mentioned as a way to use the extra fair trade money?
questions.explain: 第三段說額外的錢可以用來投資學校、乾淨的水或更好的工具，文中沒有提到買車，故選 (B)。本題問的是「沒有提到」的選項，作答時要逐一和文章比對。
questions.evidence: use for investment in schools, clean water, or better tools

questions.stem: The word "publicity" in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to ______.
options: making something known to many people
questions.explain: 因為在學校和網路上的 publicity，公平貿易才在許多國家獲得更廣泛的認可，可知 publicity 是「宣傳、讓大家知道」，故選 (C)。(D) 文中反而說公平貿易產品通常比較貴。
questions.evidence: Thanks to publicity in schools and online, fair trade has won wider recognition in many countries.

questions.stem: What does Jia-hui most likely want her classmates to do?
options: Think about the farmers when they buy everyday goods.
questions.explain: 佳慧在結尾請同學買巧克力、咖啡或香蕉時，停下來想一想背後的人，故選 (A)。(D) 與她「追求便宜零食不該擋住別人富足」的提醒相反。
questions.evidence: stop and reflect on the people behind them

vocab.stem: Taiwan gets a lot of ______ in summer, when typhoons often bring heavy rain.
vocab.explain: 颱風常帶來大雨，所以台灣夏天有很多「降雨量」，故選 rainfall。raisin（葡萄乾）、radar（雷達）、rage（盛怒）都和颱風帶來的雨無關。

vocab.stem: The calm lake ______ the mountains like a mirror.
vocab.explain: 平靜的湖面像鏡子一樣「倒映」出群山，故選 reflected。quarreled（爭吵）、prospered（繁榮）、refunded（退款）都不能用來描述湖面映出景物。

title: Small Things: A Youth Poetry Contest
paragraphs: Do you love words? Can you turn a dream, a [[riddle|L4-0862]], or your walk to school into a poem? The Riverside Library invites all high school students to join our tenth Youth Poetry Contest. This year's [[theme|L4-0944]] is "Small Things." Poems may be written in English or Chinese, and they do not need to [[rhyme|L4-0860]].

How to Join: [[Registration|L4-0821]] is free and opens on March 1. To [[register|L4-0820]], fill out the form on our [[website|L4-0991]] and send in your poem by April 15. Each student may enter up to two poems of no more than 30 lines each. Please read the contest [[regulations|L4-0823]] carefully, as poems that do not follow them cannot be accepted. Students who [[renew|L4-0832]] their library cards in March will get a free notebook.

Judging: Our three judges will look for fresh, [[imaginative|L4-0511]] ideas, clear pictures in words, and careful [[revision|L4-0856]]. Every poem must be your own work and [[relevant|L4-0826]] to the theme. All writers will receive short written [[feedback|L4-0394]] from the judges. Winners will be announced on May 20. First prize is a scholarship of NT$10,000.

A word from last year's winner: "Read your poem out loud. If a line makes you stop, change it. Make a [[resolution|L4-0844]] to finish, even if you think your poem isn't good enough. If you don't win, don't see it as a [[rejection|L4-0824]] of you as a writer. The [[satisfaction|L4-0871]] of finishing is a prize in itself."
zh: 你熱愛文字嗎？你能把一場夢、一個謎語，或是上學的路途寫成一首詩嗎？河濱圖書館邀請所有高中生參加第十屆青少年詩歌比賽。今年的主題是「小事物」。詩作可用英文或中文書寫，而且不必押韻。
參加方式：報名免費，3 月 1 日開始受理。報名請在我們的網站填寫表格，並在 4 月 15 日前交出你的詩作。每位學生最多可投兩首詩，每首不超過 30 行。請仔細閱讀比賽規定，不符合規定的詩作恕不受理。在三月份續辦借書證的學生，還可以獲得一本免費筆記本。
評審方式：三位評審會注重新鮮、富有想像力的點子，用文字描繪的清晰畫面，以及用心的修改。每首詩都必須是你自己的作品，並且與主題相關。所有參賽者都會收到評審簡短的書面回饋。得獎名單將於 5 月 20 日公布。首獎可獲得新台幣一萬元獎學金。
去年得獎者的話：「把你的詩大聲唸出來。如果哪一行讓你卡住，就修改它。下定決心把它寫完，即使你覺得自己的詩不夠好。如果沒有得獎，也別把它當成對你這個作者的否定。完成作品的滿足感，本身就是一種獎賞。」

questions.stem: What is the last day to send in a poem?
questions.explain: 第二段說要在 4 月 15 日前交出詩作，故選 (C)。(A) 3 月 1 日是開始報名的日子，(B) 5 月 20 日是公布得獎名單的日子。
questions.evidence: send in your poem by April 15

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the contest?
options: Poems must be written in English.
Every writer will get comments from the judges.
questions.explain: 第三段說所有參賽者都會收到評審簡短的書面回饋，故選 (D)。(A)、(B) 第一段說詩作可用中文或英文、不必押韻；(C) 第二段說報名免費。
questions.evidence: All writers will receive short written feedback from the judges.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of this text?
options: To invite students to join a poetry contest
To teach students how to write in Chinese
To ask students to renew their library cards
questions.explain: 全文說明比賽主題、報名方式、評審標準與獎項，目的是邀請高中生參加詩歌比賽，故選 (A)。(D) 續辦借書證送筆記本只是附帶的小活動，不是本文主要目的。
questions.evidence: The Riverside Library invites all high school students to join our tenth Youth Poetry Contest.

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the word "rejection" is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 去年得獎者說，沒得獎時不要把它看成是對你這個作者的 rejection，可知意思是「被拒絕、被否定」，故選 (B)。(A)、(D) 都是正面的意思，不符合「沒得獎」的情境。
questions.evidence: If you don't win, don't see it as a rejection of you as a writer.

vocab.stem: "Cat" and "hat" ______, so they are often used together in children's songs.
vocab.explain: cat 和 hat 字尾發音相同，也就是「押韻」，所以常一起出現在兒歌裡，故選 rhyme。resign（辭職）、renew（更新；續約）、register（登記）都不是用來描述兩個字發音關係的動詞。

vocab.stem: The library has strict ______: no food, no drinks, and no loud talking.
vocab.explain: 冒號後列出不准飲食、不准大聲說話，這些是圖書館嚴格的「規定」，故選 regulations。riddles（謎語）、revisions（修訂）、rejections（拒絕）都不能用來指這些規則。

title: Three Slow Days on Penghu
paragraphs: When my friend Mei and I [[split|L4-0909]] the cost of a [[ferry|L4-0395]] ticket to Penghu last summer, we [[scarcely|L4-0872]] knew anything about the place. We only knew it was a group of islands off the west coast of Taiwan. Three days later, we did not want to leave.

We skipped the usual [[sightseeing|L4-0889]] bus and rented bicycles instead. The [[scenery|L4-0873]] was [[splendid|L4-0908]]: blue sea on both sides of the road, black stone [[cliffs|L4-0150]], and small fields with low stone walls that protect the crops from the strong winter wind. There is little [[shade|L4-0883]] on the islands, so we stopped often to drink water. By the end of the day, my legs were covered in [[scratches|L4-0876]] from bushes along the path, but I didn't mind.

On the second day, we visited an old temple in Magong. People came and went quietly, lighting incense and praying. Even though I am not very religious, the calm place felt deeply [[spiritual|L4-0907]]. Outside, an old man was [[sprinkling|L4-0910]] water on the hot stone steps to cool them down, while Mei made a quick [[sketch|L4-0895]] of the temple roof in her notebook.

On our last evening, we passed a small shop with a hand-painted sign. Its [[slogan|L4-0898]] read, "Slow down. You're on island time." We took the advice. We spent a [[leisurely|L4-0587]] hour by the harbor, ate ice cream, and watched the sun sink below the [[horizon|L4-0490]]. It was the most [[delightful|L4-0263]] trip I have ever taken.
zh: 去年夏天，我和朋友小美平分了去澎湖的船票錢，當時我們對那裡幾乎一無所知，只知道它是台灣西邊外海的一群島嶼。三天後，我們都不想離開了。
我們沒搭一般的觀光巴士，而是租了腳踏車。風景壯麗極了：道路兩旁是藍色的海、黑色的石頭懸崖，還有被低矮石牆圍起來的小田地，那些石牆能保護作物不受冬天強風吹襲。島上幾乎沒有遮蔭的地方，所以我們常常停下來喝水。一天結束時，我的腿被路邊的灌木叢刮出好多道傷痕，但我一點也不在意。
第二天，我們參觀了馬公的一座老廟。人們安靜地來來去去，點香祈禱。雖然我不太信教，那個寧靜的地方卻讓我感受到深深的心靈力量。廟外有位老先生正在熾熱的石階上灑水降溫，小美則在筆記本上快速畫下廟宇屋頂的素描。
最後一個傍晚，我們經過一家掛著手繪招牌的小店。上面的標語寫著：「慢下來，你現在過的是島嶼時間。」我們聽從了這個建議，在港邊悠閒地待了一個小時，吃著冰淇淋，看著太陽沉入地平線。那是我去過最愉快的一趟旅行。

questions.stem: How did the writer and Mei get around the islands?
questions.explain: 第二段說她們沒搭一般的觀光巴士，而是租了腳踏車，故選 (B)。(D) 渡輪是她們前往澎湖的交通工具，不是在島上移動的方式。
questions.evidence: We skipped the usual sightseeing bus and rented bicycles instead.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, what are the low stone walls for?
options: Protecting crops from the strong winter wind
Keeping visitors out of the fields
questions.explain: 第二段說低矮的石牆能保護作物不受冬天強風吹襲，故選 (A)。(D) 文中反而說島上幾乎沒有遮蔭的地方。
questions.evidence: small fields with low stone walls that protect the crops from the strong winter wind

questions.stem: The phrase "island time" on the shop sign most likely means ______.
options: the time when the ferry leaves
a busy schedule full of sightseeing
the hours when the shop is open
a slow and relaxed way of living
questions.explain: 標語前半句是「慢下來」，作者接著在港邊悠閒地吃冰、看夕陽，可知 island time 指「悠閒、放慢步調的生活方式」，故選 (D)。(B) 行程滿滿的觀光正好與「慢下來」相反。
questions.evidence: "Slow down. You're on island time."

questions.stem: How did the writer most likely feel about the trip?
options: She was bored by the quiet islands.
She was sorry she had rented a bicycle.
She wished she had stayed home.
questions.explain: 作者說三天後不想離開，腿被刮傷也不在意，最後還說這是她去過最愉快的旅行，可推知她非常喜歡這趟旅程，故選 (C)。(B) 她說自己不在意腿上的刮痕，並沒有後悔騎腳踏車。
questions.evidence: It was the most delightful trip I have ever taken.

vocab.stem: Before baking the cookies, Mom ______ a little sugar on top of each one.
vocab.explain: 烤餅乾前在每塊餅乾上「撒」一點糖，故選 sprinkled。shaved（刮）、sewed（縫）、split（分開；分攤）都不能用來描述把糖撒在餅乾上。

vocab.stem: It was so hot that we sat in the ______ of a big tree to cool off.
vocab.explain: 天氣很熱，所以坐在大樹的「樹蔭」下乘涼，故選 shade。socket（插座）、spade（鏟子）、stereo（音響）都不是樹下可以乘涼的地方。

title: Sleep Is Part of the Plan
paragraphs: A student who calls herself "Tired Ting" wrote to our advice column: "My big exam is only five months away. I study until 1 a.m. almost every night, but in class I keep falling asleep. My parents are [[sympathetic|L4-0933]], but they just tell me to try harder. I feel so [[tense|L4-0941]] that I can't fall asleep even when I go to bed. What should I do?"

Ms. Chen replied: "You are not lazy. But scientists have found that sleep helps the brain store what we learned during the day. Without enough of it, your memory and focus will suffer, so please make sleep a [[priority|L4-0765]].

"My [[suggestion|L4-0924]] is to make a simple [[timetable|L4-0948]] and be [[systematic|L4-0935]] about it. Put your hardest subject in the morning, when your mind is fresh, and save easier review for the evening. Instead of a [[thorough|L4-0945]] review of everything every night, focus on two or three topics. Also, look at your [[surroundings|L4-0929]]. A [[messy|L4-0632]] desk and a bright phone next to your bed will not help you rest.

"Finally, give yourself thirty minutes before bed to let go of the day's [[tension|L4-0942]]. Put your phone away, take a warm shower, or write down tomorrow's tasks so they don't stay in your head. A little [[relaxation|L4-0825]] is not a waste of time. And don't be [[timid|L4-0949]] about asking your teachers for help; they are often more [[thoughtful|L4-0946]] than you think. Sleep is not the enemy of your study plan; it is part of it."
zh: 一位自稱「疲倦的婷」的學生寫信到我們的諮詢專欄：「我的大考只剩五個月了。我幾乎每天晚上都讀到凌晨一點，但上課時卻一直睡著。我爸媽很同情我，卻只會叫我再努力一點。我緊張到就算上了床也睡不著。我該怎麼辦？」
以下是陳老師的回覆：「你並不懶惰。但科學家發現，睡眠能幫助大腦儲存我們白天學到的東西。睡眠不足，你的記憶力和專注力都會受影響，所以請把睡眠當成優先事項。
「我的建議是：做一張簡單的時間表，並且有系統地執行。把最難的科目放在早上，那時頭腦最清醒；比較簡單的複習留到晚上。不要每天晚上把所有東西都徹底複習一遍，而是專注在兩三個主題上。另外，看看你周遭的環境。凌亂的書桌和床邊發亮的手機，都不會幫助你休息。
「最後，睡前給自己三十分鐘，放下一整天的緊張。把手機收起來、洗個熱水澡，或是寫下明天要做的事，讓它們不再盤旋在你腦中。適度放鬆並不是浪費時間。還有，別害怕向老師求助，他們往往比你想的更體貼。睡眠不是讀書計畫的敵人，而是計畫的一部分。」

questions.stem: What is Tired Ting's problem?
options: She studies late at night but falls asleep in class.
Her parents do not let her study at night.
She has no time to see her friends.
She does not know which school to choose.
questions.explain: 第一段說婷幾乎每晚讀到凌晨一點，上課卻一直睡著，故選 (A)。(B) 她的父母只是叫她再努力一點，並沒有禁止她晚上讀書。
questions.evidence: I study until 1 a.m. almost every night, but in class I keep falling asleep.

questions.stem: According to Ms. Chen, when should Ting study her hardest subject?
questions.explain: 第三段陳老師建議把最難的科目放在早上，因為那時頭腦最清醒，故選 (D)。(A)、(B) 晚上應該留給比較簡單的複習，睡前則要放鬆。
questions.evidence: Put your hardest subject in the morning, when your mind is fresh

questions.stem: The word "timid" in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 句意是「別 timid 向老師求助」，並說老師往往比你想的更體貼，可知 timid 是「膽怯、不敢」的意思，故選 (C)。(D) tired 和婷的狀況有關，但不是這個字的意思。
questions.evidence: And don't be timid about asking your teachers for help

questions.stem: What is Ms. Chen's main message?
options: Students should study as late as possible.
Good sleep is an important part of studying well.
Phones are the main cause of poor grades.
Parents should do their children's homework.
questions.explain: 陳老師說睡眠幫助大腦儲存所學，建議把睡眠當成優先事項，最後總結「睡眠是讀書計畫的一部分」，故選 (B)。(C) 手機只是她提到的一個小細節，並非主要訊息。
questions.evidence: Sleep is not the enemy of your study plan; it is part of it.

vocab.stem: Check the train ______ before you leave so that you don't miss the last train home.
vocab.explain: 出門前查看火車「時刻表」，才不會錯過末班車，故選 timetable。telescope（望遠鏡）、syllable（音節）、tortoise（陸龜）都無法告訴你火車的時間。

vocab.stem: The ______ little girl was too shy to say hello to her new teacher.
vocab.explain: 小女孩害羞到不敢跟新老師打招呼，可知她很「膽小的」，故選 timid。thorough（徹底的）、systematic（有系統的）、sympathetic（同情的）都無法解釋她為何不敢打招呼。

title: The Ocean Can't Throw It Away
paragraphs: The ocean looks so [[vast|L4-0978]] that it is easy to believe that it can take in anything we throw away. It cannot. Every year, a [[tremendous|L4-0966]] amount of plastic ends up in the sea. A [[twig|L4-0971]] or a leaf soon goes back to nature, but plastic does not. Instead, the sun and waves break it into smaller and smaller pieces that can stay in the water for hundreds of years.

This plastic causes [[troublesome|L4-0969]] problems. Sea turtles may mistake floating bags for jellyfish and eat them. Lost fishing nets, and even the [[wrecks|L4-1000]] of old boats, can trap sea animals for years. Tiny bits of plastic are swallowed by fish, and some of these fish may end up on our dinner plates. Some plastics also carry [[poisonous|L4-0745]] chemicals. When a sea animal dies with a stomach full of plastic, it is a [[tragedy|L4-0957]] that people could have stopped.

Some places now have rules to cut down on plastic [[usage|L4-0975]]. In Taiwan, for example, many stores can no longer give out free plastic bags, and shops that [[violate|L4-0981]] the rules may have to pay a fine.

However, laws alone cannot stop the [[destruction|L4-0275]] of ocean life. Many people take part in [[voluntary|L4-0987]] beach clean-ups on weekends, and others carry their own cups and bags. These actions may seem small, but [[prevention|L4-0762]] is always easier than cleaning up. They also show that we care about the [[welfare|L4-0992]] of sea life, and, in the end, our own.
zh: 海洋看起來如此廣闊，讓人很容易以為它能吞下我們丟掉的任何東西。事實並非如此。每年都有大量塑膠最後流入海中。細枝或樹葉很快就會回歸自然，但塑膠不會。陽光和海浪只會把它分解成越來越小的碎片，這些碎片可能在海水中存在數百年。
這些塑膠造成棘手的問題。海龜可能把漂浮的塑膠袋誤認成水母而吃下肚。遺失的漁網，甚至舊船的殘骸，都可能困住海洋動物好幾年。細小的塑膠碎片被魚吞下，其中有些魚最後可能出現在我們的餐盤上。有些塑膠還帶有有毒的化學物質。當一隻海洋動物因胃裡塞滿塑膠而死去，那是人類原本可以阻止的悲劇。
現在有些地方訂定規則來減少塑膠的使用。以台灣為例，許多商店已經不能再免費提供塑膠袋，違反規定的店家可能要繳罰款。
然而，光靠法律無法阻止海洋生物遭到破壞。許多人在週末參加自發性的淨灘活動，也有人隨身攜帶自己的杯子和袋子。這些行動看似微小，但預防永遠比事後清理容易。它們也顯示我們關心海洋生物的福祉，而說到底，也是關心我們自己。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what happens to plastic in the sea?
options: It goes back to nature like a leaf.
Sea animals turn it into food.
It breaks into smaller pieces that can stay for a very long time.
questions.explain: 第一段說陽光和海浪會把塑膠分解成越來越小的碎片，可能在海水中存在數百年，故選 (D)。(A) 文中說樹枝和樹葉會回歸自然，塑膠卻不會。
questions.evidence: the sun and waves break it into smaller and smaller pieces that can stay in the water for hundreds of years

questions.stem: Why might sea turtles eat plastic bags?
options: They are very hungry in winter.
They think the bags are jellyfish.
People feed the bags to them.
questions.explain: 第二段說海龜可能把漂浮的塑膠袋誤認成水母而吃下去，故選 (C)。(B) 文中沒有提到塑膠袋的味道，是無中生有。
questions.evidence: Sea turtles may mistake floating bags for jellyfish and eat them.

questions.stem: The word "violate" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 違反（violate）規定的店家可能要繳罰款，可知 violate 是「違反、不遵守」，故選 (B)。(A) follow（遵守）正好是相反的意思，遵守規定不會被罰。
questions.evidence: shops that violate the rules may have to pay a fine

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Plastic in the ocean is a serious problem, and both laws and personal actions can help.
Taiwan has the cleanest beaches in the world.
Sea turtles are the only animals hurt by plastic.
Plastic bags should be made stronger.
questions.explain: 文章先說明海洋塑膠造成的問題，再介紹法規與個人行動（淨灘、自備杯袋）如何幫忙，故選 (A)。(C) 文中還提到魚和其他被漁網困住的海洋動物，不只是海龜。
questions.evidence: These actions may seem small, but prevention is always easier than cleaning up.

vocab.stem: The bird built its nest out of small ______ and dry grass.
vocab.explain: 鳥用小「樹枝」和乾草築巢，故選 twigs。wrecks（殘骸）、winks（眨眼）、yawns（呵欠）都不是築巢的材料。

vocab.stem: Joining the school band is ______; no one will force you to take part.
vocab.explain: 分號後說沒有人會強迫你參加，可知加入樂隊是「自願的」，故選 voluntary。tribal（部落的）、youthful（年輕的）、vain（徒勞的；自負的）都和「是否被強迫」無關。

title: Beyond the Harbor
paragraphs: Every Saturday morning for three years, Wei-ling climbed the hill above the harbor to visit Mr. Huang. Before his [[retirement|L4-0851]], he had worked as a [[translator|L4-0963]] on large ships, sailing to ports all over the world. Now he spent his days by the window with an old [[telescope|L4-0939]], watching boats come and go.

He never gave her ordinary lessons. Instead, he handed her a newspaper or an old letter and said, "Tell me what this means. Not word by word, but what the writer feels." When she complained that some lines were too hard to [[translate|L4-0961]], he laughed. "Good. Now you are thinking like a translator." His [[wit|L4-0994]] made even the hardest pages fun, but he could also be strict. Patience, he believed, was a [[virtue|L4-0983]] that no dictionary could teach.

This autumn, Wei-ling won a place at a university in a snowy mountain town far to the north. On her last Saturday, she found Mr. Huang [[gazing|L4-0435]] at the [[vast|L4-0978]] sea. "I'm a little afraid," she admitted. "Everything there will be new. What if I fail?"

Mr. Huang was quiet for a moment. Then he gave her a [[thoughtful|L4-0946]] smile. "When I was young, I was afraid of every [[departure|L4-0269]], too. But as the old saying goes, a ship is safe in the harbor, and that is not what ships are built for. You don't have to see the whole journey. Just make the next port your [[priority|L4-0765]]." He told her to [[reflect|L4-0813]] on how far she had already come and never to give up her [[pursuit|L4-0793]] of learning.

A week later, Wei-ling stood on the ship as it left the harbor. She did not cry at the [[farewell|L4-0388]]. She watched the city grow smaller and smaller, and then she turned toward the [[horizon|L4-0490]]. Somewhere beyond it, mountains covered in snow were waiting for her, and she felt a [[tremendous|L4-0966]] sense of hope.
zh: 三年來的每個星期六早上，薇玲都會爬上港口上方的山丘，去拜訪黃先生。退休前，他在大型船隻上擔任翻譯員，航行到世界各地的港口。如今他整天坐在窗邊，拿著一具老望遠鏡，看著船隻來來去去。
他從不給她一般的課。他會遞給她一份報紙或一封舊信，然後說：「告訴我這是什麼意思。不是逐字翻，而是寫的人有什麼感受。」當她抱怨有些句子太難翻譯時，他笑了。「很好，現在你開始像個譯者一樣思考了。」他的機智讓最難的篇章也變得有趣，但他也可以很嚴格。他相信，耐心是一種任何字典都教不來的美德。
今年秋天，薇玲考上了遙遠北方一座雪山小鎮裡的大學。最後一個星期六，她看見黃先生正凝視著廣闊的大海。「我有點害怕，」她坦承。「那裡的一切都是新的。萬一我失敗了怎麼辦？」
黃先生沉默了一會兒，然後給了她一個若有所思的微笑。「我年輕的時候，每次出發也都會害怕。但就像那句老話說的，船停在港裡很安全，可是那並不是造船的目的。你不必看清整段旅程，只要把下一個港口當作優先目標就好。」他要她回想自己已經走了多遠，並且永遠不要放棄對學習的追求。
一週後，薇玲站在駛離港口的船上。道別時她沒有哭。她看著城市變得越來越小，然後轉身面向地平線。在那之外的某處，白雪覆蓋的群山正等著她，她心中湧起滿滿的希望。

questions.stem: What is the story mainly about?
options: How Mr. Huang became a translator
Why Wei-ling decided not to go to university
How a mentor's lessons help a young woman face a new journey
The history of a harbor city
questions.explain: 故事描寫黃先生如何教導薇玲，以及在她出發前如何鼓勵她勇敢面對新的旅程，故選 (C)。(B) 與文意相反，薇玲考上了北方的大學，最後也搭船出發了。
questions.evidence: He told her to reflect on how far she had already come and never to give up her pursuit of learning.

questions.stem: How did Mr. Huang teach Wei-ling?
options: He asked her to explain what writers felt, not just translate word by word.
He gave her a test every Saturday.
He took her sailing on large ships.
He made her copy words from the dictionary.
questions.explain: 第二段說黃先生會給她報紙或舊信，要她說出寫的人的感受，而不是逐字翻譯，故選 (A)。(D) 文中反而說耐心是任何字典都教不來的美德。
questions.evidence: Tell me what this means. Not word by word, but what the writer feels.

questions.stem: What does Mr. Huang most likely mean when he says a ship "is safe in the harbor" but "that is not what ships are built for"?
options: Ships are dangerous and should stay in the harbor.
He wants Wei-ling to work on a ship like him.
Wei-ling should stay in the city where she feels safe.
People need to leave safe, familiar places in order to grow.
questions.explain: 船待在港裡雖然安全，但船是為了航行而造的；黃先生用這句話鼓勵害怕失敗的薇玲勇敢離開熟悉的地方，故選 (D)。(C) 與他的意思正好相反。
questions.evidence: a ship is safe in the harbor, and that is not what ships are built for

questions.stem: The word "tremendous" in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 薇玲轉身面向地平線，想到雪山正等著她，心中充滿希望，tremendous 形容希望「巨大的、非常強烈的」，故選 (B)。(A) small 正好相反，(D) sad 也與她「沒有哭」、充滿希望的心情不符。
questions.evidence: she felt a tremendous sense of hope

vocab.stem: Honesty is a ______ that every good friend should have.
vocab.explain: 誠實是每個好朋友都該有的「美德」，故選 virtue。wreck（殘骸）、usage（用法）、yawn（呵欠）都不能用來形容誠實這種品格。

vocab.stem: Could you help me ______ this letter from Japanese into Chinese?
vocab.explain: translate A from B into C 是「把 A 從 B 語翻譯成 C 語」的固定用法，故選 translate。withdraw（撤回；提款）、waken（喚醒）、tremble（發抖）都不能接 from Japanese into Chinese。
